city.bed.nap.1: I shut my eyes for a minute. When I opened them the window's shadow had crept onto the other wall.
city.bed.nap.2: I dozed to the ticking of the clock in the corridor. The dream was short and warm, like a sandwich.
city.bed.nap.3: A nurse looked in, tucked the blanket round me and left without a word.
city.bed.night.1: The sheets crackled with starch. The sea was murmuring outside, and then I heard nothing at all.
city.bed.night.2: I dreamt I was climbing an endless staircase to the sun and not getting tired at all.
city.bed.night.3: I woke to spoons ringing in glasses in the corridor: someone was bringing tea.
city.bed.private.1: This is someone's bed. The cover's been smoothed by a hand, there's a dent in the pillow. No.
city.bed.private.2: A stranger's bed smells of a stranger's soap. I just stood next to it.
city.bed.private.3: Someone else sleeps here. I have to find a place of my own.
city.cafe.book.0: The first page, the ink faded: "Open at last. The coffee smells, the stair spirals, and we seem to be sitting inside a saucer. Thanks to the architect. — The first guests."
city.cafe.book.1: "Came with my daughter. She demanded ice cream three times, and three times we didn't mind." Next to it, a cone with three scoops.
city.cafe.book.2: In green ink, in a hurry: "The parrot told me 'Mind the doors, please' and I stepped back. There are no doors here. Thank you, Kesha!"
city.cafe.book.3: "Played chess with the Professor. Lost in seven moves. He said: 'Never mind, you resigned in good time.' A good school."
city.cafe.book.4: In a different pen: "Lighthouse keeper on duty. Dropped in off my watch. I confirm: my beam can be seen from your window. It looks better from here than from my side."
city.cafe.book.5: Two hands side by side, two pens: "We both came. Sat by the window until closing. One told about the static, the other about how long it had been since he'd heard a voice without noise. Paid half and half. No static. — I. and G."
city.cafe.book.6: In a corner of the page someone has drawn a saucer with eyes and written: "This is us." Below, in the barista's hand: "Leaving it as it is."
city.cafe.book.7: A fresh entry by the manager: "The pages are running out, we'll start a new book soon. The pen is next to the book, and if you've no thoughts, draw a saucer. We love saucers."
city.cafe.cake.fri: Friday: the "Anthill", a brown mound with nuts. A small boy at the case has already chosen and is waiting for his mother to.
city.cafe.cake.mon: Monday: the case holds a chocolate "Potato" and two eclairs. The eclairs, judging by the price tag, hope to last until Tuesday.
city.cafe.cake.sat: Saturday: the "Saucer" cake, round, glazed, with a small spiral wafer on top like the stair. People take it whole, for tea.
city.cafe.cake.sun: Sunday: pastries for everyone on a tray with a red rim. A card: "One each, please. In exceptional cases, two."
city.cafe.cake.thu: Thursday: apple puffs. A hand-written line on the price tag: "The last one, don't be shy."
city.cafe.cake.tue: Tuesday: Napoleon cake. The layers are so thin it looks as if someone counted them with tweezers.
city.cafe.cake.wed: Wednesday: little cream baskets with a berry. Each berry sits exactly in the middle, like a seal.
city.cafe.chess.1: I took the Captain's place at the board: he said he had "business at the lighthouse", though he was probably just tired of losing. The Professor moves his pawns as if apologising. Twenty moves later I was the one apologising.
city.cafe.chess.2: After school the board belongs to two schoolboys. They play fast and loud, whispering at every move. They let me into the third game as a newcomer from outside.
city.cafe.chess.3: At weekends the chess moves to the nearest table: here they play for coffee. The loser orders. I lost, but the Captain ordered himself: "A newcomer's first coffee is on us."
city.cafe.chess.4: The Professor mates me on the ninth move, silently, without taking off his hat. Then, just as silently, he sets the pieces back and shows where I could have won. It turns out, on the sixth.
city.cafe.chess.5: The Captain plays only black and only one opening. He calls it the "Lighthouse Defence". He doesn't explain what it means, and wins in such a way that you can't take offence.
city.cafe.chess.6: The game was interrupted by the parrot announcing "Terminus". We finished in a draw: everyone looked at Kesha and forgot whose move it was.

city.cafe.cook.fri: "Friday: curd fritters. Sour cream comes with them, but only whoever remembers to ask gets it."
city.cafe.cook.mon: The cook, without turning round: "Monday, noodle soup. My grandmother's recipe; don't ask my grandmother."
city.cafe.cook.prompt: E — ask the cook about the dish of the day
city.cafe.cook.sat: "Saturday: pilaf for everyone. Whoever comes first gets the bottom of the pot, the best part."
city.cafe.cook.sun: "On Sundays I don't cook. I only warm up what I left from Saturday and call it home cooking."
city.cafe.cook.thu: "Thursday: stuffed cabbage. Probably the best in the district today. Tomorrow merely good."
city.cafe.cook.tue: "Tuesday: rissoles and mash. I make the mash myself and don't spare the butter; dieticians are asked not to look."
city.cafe.cook.wed: "Wednesday: fish and potatoes. The fish came from the pier this morning, still arguing."
city.cafe.crate.1: A crate of sleeves: the records stand on edge like books in a library. On the spines, in pencil, the button numbers. The numbers stopped matching the buttons long ago.
city.cafe.crate.2: A sleeve marked "Left behind in April". Inside, a postcard of the sea and a record of the same sea, only audible.
city.cafe.crate.3: One record is labelled "D-3 (by request, do not take away)". Someone has underlined "do not take away" twice. So it has been taken away.
city.cafe.crate.4: Deep in the crate, a shabby sleeve: "To the Saucer's best listener. Thank you for never interrupting. — The Sanatorium Orchestra."
city.cafe.crate.5: A note is stuck on the side: "The machine takes coins. Not buttons: Kesha tested it." Next to it, a beak print.
city.cafe.esp.d1: At lunchtime the machine never stops: steam, click, steam, click. The cups leave on a tray and come back empty, with spoons in the saucers.
city.cafe.esp.d2: A dark thread creeps slowly from the spout. Watch it for over a minute and you want a glass of water and a second cup.
city.cafe.esp.e1: By evening the coffee is made less often and the steam lasts longer. While the stream runs, the barista looks out of the window: that is where the best part is now.
city.cafe.esp.e2: A note is taped to the machine's panel: "Don't tap the gauge. It's nervous." The needle trembles as if it has heard everything.
city.cafe.esp.m1: By eight everything is ready: the bar wiped, the machine warm, the chairs down on their legs. Now the barista silently watches the pressure gauge like a barometer before a long journey.
city.cafe.esp.m2: The first cup of the morning is not for the guests. It is set on the edge of the bar on its saucer and left to cool until the first visitor comes in. They say the café treats itself first.
city.cafe.esp.m3: The grounds are tamped with one short, level press. A click of the lever, a hiss, and the hall smells so good the chairs seem to shuffle closer.
city.cafe.esp.n: The machine cools, ticking softly. In the morning it will be woken again.

city.cafe.feed.1: I poured the seeds into the saucer and said "Terminus". Kesha waited until I had finished, cracked one, thought, and announced: "Please vacate the cars." The barista laughed and took a pastry from the case: "Finder gets one on the house. You've found him again, more or less."
city.cafe.feed.2: Kesha pecked a seed and said: "Thank you for travelling with us." He never used to say that. The barista set a pastry on a saucer in front of me.
city.cafe.feed.3: Kesha ate one seed and hid the rest under his perch "until the next stop". The pastry on the house is already waiting on the bar.
city.cafe.feed.prompt: E — treat Kesha to sunflower seeds
city.cafe.guestbook.prompt: E — leaf through the guest book
city.cafe.juke.a1: Button A-1: a waltz on a record worn to silver. The machine sighs, creaks, then gives out the waltz as if it had never done anything else.
city.cafe.juke.a4: A-4, a march. Without looking up, the barista turns it down a notch: someone by the window is reading the paper and the drum is in his way.
city.cafe.juke.b1: B-1: a song about the sea in a foreign language. An elderly couple at a table falls silent on the second line and listens to the end, holding on to their cups.
city.cafe.juke.b5: B-5: a twist. The chairs at the nearest table suddenly start tapping along by themselves, and there are shoes underneath them too.
city.cafe.juke.c2: C-2: instead of music, an announcer's voice reading the coastal weather. Someone must have mixed up the sleeve. I listened to the end: no rain tomorrow.
city.cafe.juke.c6: C-6. Next to it, by hand: "DO NOT PRESS". I pressed. A flute began, very quietly, as if from far away. Now I see why nobody presses it.
city.cafe.juke.d3: The third button from the left, D-3: the tune I was looking for plays whole, with no static, to the last note. The barista nods: "It's the most requested. They say someone taped it off the air."
city.cafe.juke.g1: In the morning the jukebox is quiet: G-1, a soft little waltz under the hiss of the coffee machine. The barista nods along without noticing.
city.cafe.juke.g3: In the evening the jukebox is louder: G-3, a foxtrot, and someone by the stairs is already tapping a foot, pretending to tie a shoelace.
city.cafe.kesha.0: Kesha sits on his perch at the end of the bar and looks with one eye as if checking a ticket. Then he announces: "Next stop, the Saucer." We're already on it, but I didn't argue.
city.cafe.kesha.1: Today Kesha is silent and only bobs his head to the jukebox. The barista whispers: "He's on leave after the tour."
city.cafe.kesha.2: "Mind the doors, please!" Kesha announces when someone heads for the stairs. There are no doors in the hall, but everyone ducks a little.
city.cafe.kesha.3: Kesha has learned a new word and says it only when nobody asks. The word is "Horizon". I think he just likes the sound of it.
city.cafe.kesha.4: Kesha studies me for a long time, then says very clearly: "Ticket." I show him my empty palms. Kesha turns away, disappointed.
city.cafe.kesha.5: Beside the perch is a saucer, marked in felt pen: "For Kesha. Sunflower seeds. But first say 'Terminus'." Kesha waits without blinking.
city.cafe.kesha.6: Kesha has got used to me: he no longer turns away but tilts his head a little. The barista says he does that for people who bring seeds.
city.cafe.ledge.d1: By day the glass is warm as a stove, and the spoons on their saucers throw sunbeams on the ceiling. It is hot and very cheerful to sit here.
city.cafe.ledge.d2: On a paper napkin, in pencil: "The window is best at seven in the evening. Do come." No signature.
city.cafe.ledge.m1: The ledge by the glass is still cool, the light grey and soft. Below, the promenade wakes: first the street-washing truck, then the first bicycle.
city.cafe.ledge.m2: Somebody has left a glass of water with a twig in it on the ledge. The twig has already put out a white root.
city.cafe.ledge.n1: At night the ledge is the quietest place in the Saucer. The lamps reflect in the glass, and it seems another hall hangs outside, empty and upside down.
city.cafe.ledge.n2: Below, the promenade lights; above, the stars; between them a black strip of sea. One far-off boat crawls along it, and I feel like waving my glass at it.
city.cafe.ledge.s1: There it is. By seven the glass turns copper, then pink, and every cup throws a long shadow all the way to the stairs. At the nearby tables everyone falls quiet at once.
city.cafe.ledge.s2: A disc of sun lies in my palm, still warm. In a minute it will slide to the floor and go toward the stairs, and I'll sit beside it a little longer.
city.cafe.ledge.s3: The ledge lamp is on but not needed yet: there is light enough. The barista has quietened the machine so as not to disturb it. Nobody says it aloud, but this is called "the minute of sunset".
city.cafe.pen.1: I wrote: "Was here. It's good for thinking, with a staircase underfoot." Thought a moment and added the date.
city.cafe.pen.2: I didn't know what to write, so I drew a saucer. It came out more like a hat. I captioned it: "Saucer (view from below)."
city.cafe.pen.3: I added in a corner: "Hi, Kesha!" with an exclamation mark. Thought and added a second.
city.cafe.pen.4: Under someone else's entry I wrote: "Agreed." What with, I only worked out as I closed the book, but I didn't rub it out.
city.cafe.tel.d1: By day the town in the lens is a scale model: the cable car crawls from station to station, and a tiny cyclist on the promenade never reaches the corner while I watch.
city.cafe.tel.d2: I found the sanatorium roof in the lens. Something is drying on it: washing or flags, I can't tell from here. Maybe both.
city.cafe.tel.m1: In the morning the telescope shows the fishing boats coming home, each with a white thread of gulls behind it. One gull sits on a bow and is in no hurry at all.
city.cafe.tel.m2: Down on the promenade someone is hosing the paving. Through the telescope it shines like a freshly washed plate.
city.cafe.tel.n1: At night the lighthouse beam crosses the lens slowly, like a clock hand. I count: four seconds until the next sweep.
city.cafe.tel.n2: The windows on the hillside burn in different ways: warm ones, blue ones from a TV, and one that blinks. Is somebody signalling? Most likely a bad bulb.
city.cafe.tel.n3: No moon, but for a second the dark eyepiece reflects the whole Saucer from inside: the lamps, the tables, and me with my eye to the tube.
city.cafe.tel.s1: Toward evening the sun settles on the water like a yolk on a saucer, and the water around it turns pink. The coin ran out before the sunset did.
city.cafe.tel.s2: The lighthouse lamp is lit while the sky is still bright. In the lens the beam looks like a thread just pulled through a needle.
city.closed.cafe.bar: The bar is empty, the coffee machine under a towel. A note on the till: "Open at eight."
city.closed.cafe.chairs: The chairs are up on the tables, legs in the air. The floor is still damp from the mop.
city.closed.cafe.machine: The plug is pulled and hung neatly on a hook. The music is asleep.
city.closed.club.counter: The window is latched shut. A card on the glass: "Closed till tomorrow."
city.closed.club.screen: The screen is behind its velvet curtain. The next show is tomorrow.
city.closed.club.seats: The hall is empty, the seats folded up. It smells of curtain dust and, faintly, of tangerines.
city.closed.cog.games: Everything is under covers, the balls and pieces locked away in the cupboard.
city.closed.cog.seats: The chairs are pushed under the tables in neat rows. Someone left a scarf on one.
city.closed.library.desk: The lamp on the lending desk is out, the date stamp put away in the drawer. Waiting for morning.
city.closed.library.shelf: A cord with a card is strung across the shelf: "The library is closed. The books are asleep too."
city.closed.market.stall: The stall is under a tarpaulin weighed down with a brick. The scales went home.
city.closed.store.counter: The department is closed. The display case is under grey cloth with a card: "Stocktaking."
city.cog.bench.boat.1: Today we cut. Lev Arkadyevich laid a sheet of plywood on the bench and pencilled the frames on it. I cut three with the fretsaw. The fourth came out with character. Tomorrow we glue.
city.cog.bench.boat.2: Today we glue. The frames stand on the keel like a fish's ribs. I spread glue on the joints and clamped them with clothes-pegs. The glue smells of apples, which is odd. Now it dries until tomorrow.
city.cog.bench.boat.3: Today we paint. The hull is skinned in veneer and smooth as a pebble. Red below, white deck, blue wheelhouse. Paint up to my elbows. Lev Arkadyevich said that is the first sign of a good model-maker.

city.cog.bench.glider.1: Glider: today the ribs. Thin as kindling. I broke one and cut a new one. Lev Arkadyevich believes a glider loves the patient.
city.cog.bench.glider.2: Glider: today we cover the wing in tissue paper. Glue on every rib, paper without a single wrinkle. A wrinkle, they say, is an air pocket.
city.cog.bench.glider.3: Glider: today we spray the paper with water so it tightens. I watch it dry and breathe, and I know nothing duller or more fascinating.
city.cog.bench.glider.4: Glider: test day. We launched it from the stair landing into the foyer. It made a circle and landed on a bench. The cloakroom attendant, without getting up, gave it a "good".
city.cog.bench.glider.prompt: E — work on the glider's wing
city.cog.bil.1: On Tuesday and Thursday evenings the table belongs to the juniors' section: five of them walk round it counting angles. I was let in last. I learned that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection even when the ball doesn't want it to.
city.cog.bil.2: Friday evenings the league plays: men from the shipyard with their sleeves rolled up. The loser buys tea from the buffet. They poured me one for nothing: witnesses, they say, always get tea.
city.cog.bil.3: On Saturday they play in pairs, two against two, and all four argue over whose ball it was. I stood aside with a cue feeling like a referee. Nobody asked me once.
city.cog.bil.4: Sunday afternoon at the table: fathers with their children. The children stretch on tiptoe, the fathers pretend to miss. I potted two and was a little proud.
city.cog.bil.5: The league final is near. The cushions have been wiped to a shine and the table looks solemn, as before an oath.
city.cog.cart.1: The returns trolley: the books lie with their spines every which way, and you can tell who read what. On top, "Chess for Beginners" with a bookmark at page forty-one. He clearly got no further.
city.cog.cart.2: On Monday the trolley is full: after the weekend everyone returned everything at once. Tamara Ilyinichna sorts without lifting her head or losing count.
city.cog.cart.3: By the weekend the trolley is nearly empty: readers take books away and bring them back later, on Monday. A law of nature.
city.cog.cart.4: In the pile, someone's note: "I didn't take the clock, I only took 'Photography for Amateurs'." On that book's spine, the photo circle's stamp.
city.cog.chess.1: We played on the hourglass from the first-aid room. The sand runs as it pleases. They said it's an ancient method: whoever is faster, the sand is theirs.
city.cog.chess.2: Thursday evening is blitz at the tables. At each, two play and one watches with an opinion. The opinion is louder than the chess.
city.cog.chess.3: Today they play more quietly than usual. Someone is listening for a chess clock to tick somewhere. None does.
city.cog.chess.4: A game with the clock: the left dial cracked, the right whole, both ticking a bit faster than you'd like. I won on time but not on position. They say that counts too.
city.cog.chess.5: A five-minute blitz: the pieces fly, the hand can't keep up with the thought nor the thought with the hand. I lost on the last second and smiled. Tamara Ilyinichna wrote in the log: "Clock in place."
city.cog.clock.1: A chess clock with two dials. The left one has a crack like a lightning bolt. It is ticking. It turns out they use it as a stopwatch: press, the exposure runs, press again, stop.
city.cog.clock.2: Under the clock a note: "Borrowed for a while, will return Thursday. S. G." "Thursday" is crossed out and another Thursday written. Then another.
city.cog.clock.3: The clock ticks as before, but a little sheepishly. Seryozha said he would have taken it back himself but was ashamed, and asked: "Maybe you could carry it? They won't scold you." I thought I would.

city.cog.cues.1: The cues stand by height and by temper. The first was too light. The second was too proud. The third, worn at the tip like an old friend, turned out to be mine.
city.cog.cues.2: On the rail there is a tin of chalk. I chalked the cue and blew on the tip the way the older ones do. At once I felt part of the league.
city.cog.cues.3: At weekends the duty member hands out the cues: "One cue, one person. No waving." I didn't wave.
city.cog.dark.1: Today, negatives. We wind the film in total darkness, by touch, counting in whispers. Seryozha says the dark is where he manages best to stay calm.
city.cog.dark.2: Today, contact sheets: all the frames on one sheet, small as stamps. We choose one. I chose the lighthouse frame; it was the only one not blurred.
city.cog.dark.3: Today, printing. The sheet under the enlarger, red light. We count the exposure on the clock on the second bench: click the left button, click the right; at twelve we lift the frame.
city.cog.dark.4: Today, drying. The prints hang on the line and drip, and it smells of vinegar. Someone is already arguing whether gloss or matt is better.
city.cog.dark.prompt: E — work in the photo lab
city.cog.draft.1: On the drafting board is a drawing: a cable-car lift at 1:20. The angle of the cable is written twice, the second time in red with a question mark.
city.cog.draft.2: A note in the margin: "Seryozha from the photo circle's idea: a mirror in the cabin so passengers see the sea from both sides." Lev Arkadyevich disagreed and agreed.
city.cog.draft.3: A new sheet: "Cabin, model 1:20." The window is cut round, like a porthole. They argued whether it needs a wheel. Those for the wheel won.
city.cog.dry.1: Two finished little boats dry side by side. One has its red side to the very edge, on the other the paint has run a little onto the deck. A card: "Paint takes a day to dry. A day, not five minutes." Underlined twice.
city.cog.dry.2: The little boats on the shelf are dry now and stand upright. A note: "Collect by Sunday or they go to the club fund." Whether anyone will is unknown.
city.cog.dry.3: The shelf is taken up by paint tins: red, white, blue, all open and covered with gauze. It smells like a small harbour.
city.cog.league.1: The Cog Club billiards league: a table in chalk. The top three places belong to the shipyard, fourth to "Unknown", and fifth is a bottle of kefir someone put there for tidiness.
city.cog.league.2: Under the table: "Semi-final on Friday evening. Spectators, please don't stand by the pockets: the pockets get nervous."
city.cog.league.3: The semi-final has been played: a fitter from the shipyard won 3-2 on the last ball. The loser bought tea for everyone, and twice for the witnesses.
city.cog.league.4: "Final on Saturday evening. Spectators sign up with Tamara Ilyinichna. The more people, the quieter they play."
city.cog.league.5: The final has been played. The cup, a bent cog on a stand, sits by the buffet. The winner forgot about it and came back an hour later.
city.cog.lounge.1: "Please do not screw either players or attachments to the table football. Players especially."
city.cog.lounge.2: The machine takes only five-rouble coins and angrily gives back everything else. If anyone knows why, please share.
city.cog.lounge.3: In the photo lab in the evenings something ticks, as if a chess game were being played with nobody there. Anyone in the know, tell Tamara Ilyinichna.
city.cog.meet.1: Circles' meeting on the first Saturday of the month. Agenda: tea. Additionally: the kettle.
city.cog.meet.2: Minutes of the meeting: the clock is to be fixed to the chess table with a chain, and the photographers are to buy a stopwatch. Signed by all, including the stopwatch, which does not exist.
city.cog.models.1: On the stand is yesterday's launch: painted, shining, drying. Next to it a pencilled card: "Don't touch, sticky."
city.cog.models.2: The shelf is almost empty: the launch has gone to the bench, leaving its drawing and an empty stand.
city.cog.models.3: On the stand the launch is unpainted, pale, smelling of pine and glue. Today it gets painted, and tomorrow it will be red.
city.cog.models.4: Next to the launch stands a glider covered in russet paper. On its wing: "Flew. Came back by itself."
city.cog.place.1: On the cloth by the board there is a pale rectangle where the clock stood and a slip: "The clock stood here." For now it's empty.
city.cog.place.2: I pictured the cracked clock coming back to the pale rectangle. For now its only home is the photographers' bench, where it counts the seconds of other people's pictures.
city.cog.place.3: I set the clock on the pale rectangle and the cloth under it seemed to sigh. Tamara Ilyinichna, without getting up, wrote in the log: "Clock in place." There will be a blitz on Thursday.

city.cog.prints.1: A strip of film hangs on the line with wet frames, like a tiny movie. The frames are dark, the faces light: it's always like that with negatives.
city.cog.prints.2: On the line hangs a contact sheet: thirty-six frames in rows. The best are ringed in red. One is ringed three times.
city.cog.prints.3: A large print on the line, still wet: a lighthouse, a dune, a girl with a string bag. The edges curl like pages in a damp book.
city.cog.prints.4: The print has dried and flattened. A pencilled caption: "Dune, six in the evening. S. Gusev." Next to it an empty space for the next one.

city.cog.rd.1: Tamara Ilyinichna: there is no chess clock in the reading room, we looked under the cupboards. We found a button. The button is waiting for its owner at the cloakroom.
city.cog.rd.2: "The clock is loud: it ticks like a grasshopper. If you've heard a grasshopper in the club, please report to the cloakroom before 7 p.m."
city.cog.rd.3: The Thursday blitz is back on! Sign up with Tamara Ilyinichna. We play on any clock that ticks. Not the hourglass, though.
city.cog.reh.1: The rehearsal schedule on squared paper: Tuesday, Thursday, drama circle, 5 p.m. Wednesday, dance, 4 p.m. Saturday, amateur evening, 5 p.m. Sunday: "the stage rests."
city.cog.reh.2: Today the drama circle rehearses at 5 p.m. Added: "Latecomers play the trees."
city.cog.reh.3: Today dance at 4 p.m. Added: "Indoor shoes required. Socks are not shoes."
city.cog.reh.4: Tonight, the amateur evening. A hand-lettered poster: "Choir, accordion, verse. Entrance free, exit too."
city.cog.reh.5: Today the stage is free. Added: "If you want to rehearse, sign up with the cloakroom attendant."
city.cog.reh.6: A notice: "On Thursday after the blitz, the prize-giving on stage. The drama circle has promised to present the cup with expression."
city.cog.sh.art.1: An album, "Painting of the Baltic." Under the dunes someone has written: "Went there yesterday. Just the same, only no mosquitoes." You can tell the painting was checked against the shore.
city.cog.sh.art.2: An exhibition catalogue. On the print of the lighthouse there is a tea stain shaped like a small cloud. Tamara Ilyinichna said the stain now counts as part of the display.
city.cog.sh.birds.1: "Birds of the Baltic", the borrower's slip on the last page: "Returned. The gull turned out not to be a gull." The pages about gulls are the most thumbed.
city.cog.sh.birds.2: In the margin by the chaffinch, in big letters: "Saw one in our yard! Tamara Ilyinichna, this is for you." Below, the reply: "I saw it. Thank you."
city.cog.sh.chess.1: In the margins of a textbook a hand marks the moves and writes: "Blundered the queen here, never playing again. See you Thursday." Judging by the number of such notes, Thursday has come round more than once.
city.cog.sh.chess.2: A sheet sticks out of the book: the Thursday blitz schedule. The last line: "The clock belongs to the club, take care of it." Below, in another hand: "(if it turns up)."
city.cog.sh.eng.1: "Photography for Amateurs." On the page about exposure someone has written: "Don't count aloud, you cheat. You need a clock that ticks evenly." Good advice.
city.cog.sh.eng.2: A model-maker's magazine with a drawing of a motor launch. The sizes are pencilled in, and on the last page there is a thumbprint in glue.
city.cog.sh.local.1: A bound run of the town paper. In the piece on the club's opening the word "cog" is circled: "It isn't a wheel," the architect explained, "it's hands taking hold of one another."
city.cog.sh.local.2: An old map of the town, the club still on the outskirts. Beside it a dotted line, a road to come that does not exist yet. Someone has carefully drawn it in pencil across the margins.
city.cog.sh.poetry.1: On the flyleaf of the collection is the stamp "Cog Club. Library" and in pencil: "Reading aloud: whispers only." I read it in a whisper. It came out even better.
city.cog.sh.poetry.2: A bookmark between the pages: last year's buffet coupon. The poem on this page is about winter, so the coupon is probably not there by accident.
city.cog.sh.science.1: A popular-science magazine. In an article on the pendulum, in the margin: "A chess clock is a pendulum too. Tested." The signature is illegible, the handwriting hurried.
city.cog.sh.science.2: A physicist's handbook. On the page about light and shadow a developed print is tucked in: the reading-room window with a gull's silhouette on the glass. On the back, the photo circle's stamp.
city.cog.sh.sea.1: A Baltic pilot book, the corners worn. The bookmark is a thread with a bit of sea glass. In the sun the glass puts a green patch on the page.
city.cog.sh.sea.2: A book on sailing ships. Next to a drawing of a schooner, in a child's hand: "We'll build one like this in the workshop." Signed: "Lev Arkadyevich doesn't mind."
city.cog.stage.1: A rehearsal is on: the drama circle works through the farewell scene at the lighthouse. The director claps after every line and the line has to be said again. Not once did it sound the same.
city.cog.stage.2: Saturday evening: a choir of nine, an accordion and a girl who recites verse looking at the ceiling, so as not to be afraid. The hall claps longer than she recited.
city.cog.stage.3: Wednesday, the dance circle. To the piano and a count of "one-two-three" the girls go round the stage in circles. A boy drags a chair: he is the scenery. He tries very hard to be a chair.
city.cog.stagen.1: Dear audience: please do not move the chairs, they stand by rank. Whoever sits in the wrong seat sits in somebody else's.
city.cog.stagen.2: After the Thursday blitz the photo circle will show slides on stage. Do not turn off the light: we see everything anyway.
city.cog.swap.1: Above the rack a slip: "Bring one, take one; take one, bring one." The magazines have gone round here for years. I took the one on top.
city.cog.swap.2: On Mondays the rack has something new: a man from the workshops leaves a stack of popular-science magazines with drawings on the inserts. I took the top one.
city.cog.swap.3: By the weekend the rack is almost bare: everything's gone. One magazine is left, covered in glue stains. It must have been read at the workbench.
city.cog.swap.4: On Sundays the rack isn't restocked. A note on it: "Out of magazines, come on Tuesday." But one turned up anyway, under the note.
city.cog.swap.prompt: E — take a magazine from the swap rack
city.cog.tray.1: The tray is empty, the last drop of developer shining on the bottom. The print hasn't been made yet.
city.cog.tray.2: On the white sheet in the tray outlines are surfacing: two vertical strokes and a horizon. It isn't clear yet what it is, but it will be soon.
city.cog.tray.3: The print is clear now: the lighthouse against the evening sky and a gull that got into the frame by accident and now won't leave. Seryozha swears he didn't feed it.
city.cog.tray.4: The trays are empty. The print has gone to dry and hangs last on the left of the line. It dried lighter than it looked in the red light.
city.cog.tt.1: On Mondays and Wednesdays the circle trains here: the coach puts a tin can on the table and teaches them to hit it with a serve. The can is covered in dents and seems proud of it.
city.cog.tt.2: Tuesday and Thursday evenings they play round-robin: lose, and you go to the end of the queue on the bench. The queue, the old-timers say, is the main part of the game.
city.cog.tt.3: On Friday and Saturday the older pupils come and play knockout. The noise carries to the reading room, and Tamara Ilyinichna knocks on the pipe. The pipe answers.
city.cog.tt.4: On Sunday morning the table is free and the ball is in no hurry. I practised my serve until it worked twice in a row, and stopped on that high note.
city.cog.wsb.1: Today in the workshop: cutting. Plywood on the bench, fretsaws with Lev Arkadyevich. Whoever has no fretsaw draws.
city.cog.wsb.2: Today in the workshop: gluing. Clothes-pegs issued against a signature. Please do not glue the pegs to your sleeves.
city.cog.wsb.3: Today in the workshop: painting. Aprons on the nail. Whoever has no apron paints to one side, and quietly.
city.cog.wsb.4: Please do not bring the chess clock to the workshop: we don't have it, we looked. Lev Arkadyevich.
