city.do.aquarium.1: The guppies dart in a shoal, and the catfish lies on the bottom pretending to be a stone. He's good at it.
city.do.aquarium.2: One fish swam up to the glass and looked at me. I'm not sure which of us is in the tank.
city.do.aquarium.3: Bubbles rise steadily from the little castle on the bottom. Watch long enough and you start breathing in time.
city.do.aquarium.4: A sign on the tank: "Do not feed the fish. They are on a diet. Especially Boris." I couldn't find Boris.
city.do.arcade.1: "Sea Battle": I sank two ships out of five. The periscope smells of rubber and other people's foreheads.
city.do.arcade.2: Racing: on the third lap my car went into the ditch and stayed there. The machine beeped something sympathetic.
city.do.arcade.3: "Sniper": nine out of ten. The machine gave me a token for a free game, but the token rolled away somewhere.
city.do.arcade.4: I played "Goalkeeper" until three boys were queuing behind me. Gave way. They played worse.
city.do.barbell.1: I took off all the plates but two small ones. Lifted ten times. The plates weren't that small after all.
city.do.barbell.2: The coach straightened my back and said: "The strength is in your legs, not your face." I stopped grimacing.
city.do.barbell.3: The bar is cold and smells of iron. After the third set my arms hummed like wires.
city.do.barbell.4: Up, down, up. In the wall mirror, a boy with red ears and a very determined look.
city.do.basketball.1: Three out of ten. Every time the ball went thoughtfully round the rim, deciding whether to drop.
city.do.basketball.2: The net is torn, so you can hardly hear a basket. You have to take your own word for it.
city.do.basketball.3: A tall lad showed me how to put backspin on it. The ball obeyed him, and then me.
city.do.basketball.4: The ball thuds on the tarmac like a big heart. I kept going till the sun dropped behind the hoop.
city.do.billiards.1: Aimed for five minutes, struck, and the ball went round every cushion and quietly dropped in. I pretended I'd meant it.
city.do.billiards.2: A man in braces showed me how to chalk the cue and said: "It's not the ball that matters, it's the pause before the shot."
city.do.billiards.3: I'd have torn the cloth if they hadn't stopped me in time. They did. Let me play again, from a safe distance.
city.do.billiards.4: The balls click like chattering teeth. I potted two. Not bad, they say, for the first time in my life.
city.do.binoculars_post.1: Through the binoculars: the buoys, and nobody beyond them. Good. The lifeguard said: "If only it were always like this."
city.do.binoculars_post.2: I found a gull sitting on a buoy looking my way. We stared at each other for a long time.
city.do.binoculars_post.3: Far out a swimmer in a red cap goes steadily, unhurried, as if he knows where.
city.do.binoculars_post.4: The eyepieces are warm from other people's eyes. The sea is closer through them, but quieter, somehow.
city.do.binoculars_post.prompt: E — look through the lifeguard's binoculars
city.do.blackboard.1: I chalked "2 + 2 =" and paused. The chalk squeaked by itself, as if prompting.
city.do.blackboard.2: Left on the board from the last lesson: "On duty: Lebedev." I added: "and me".
city.do.blackboard.3: I drew a sun, rubbed it out, then drew it again, bigger. The cloth smells of chalk and wet wool.
city.do.blackboard.4: I wrote my name and looked at it a long time. On the board it looked like someone else's.
city.do.checkup.1: The doctor listened with a cold stethoscope and said: "Your heart works. Sometimes overtime."
city.do.checkup.2: "Say 'ah'." "Ahh." "Good. More sun, fewer sweets, and sleep at night."
city.do.checkup.3: The doctor tapped my knee with a little hammer and my leg jerked. "Reflexes fine. We'll check your thoughts another time."
city.do.checkup.4: They wrote "Practically healthy" on my card. I asked what "practically" means. The doctor smiled and didn't say.
city.do.chess.1: I lost to an old man in a beret. But he showed me the Sicilian defence and said I had "honest moves".
city.do.chess.2: Drew with a girl of about nine. She thought a long time over every move and swung her legs.
city.do.chess.3: I won! My opponent shook my hand and said he'd let me. Then he thought and said he hadn't.
city.do.chess.4: We both forgot whose move it was and started over. Then again. The game never really began, but it was nice.
city.do.chess.prompt: E — play a game of chess
city.do.choir.1: The choir sang without words, just voices, and the vaults overhead hummed like a vast seashell.
city.do.choir.2: The choir leader stopped them: "Altos, you're singing about the sun as if it were the bus timetable. Again!"
city.do.choir.3: An old man in the back row sang slightly off, but so happily that nobody corrected him.
city.do.choir.4: They went over the song about ten times, and on the tenth I caught myself quietly singing along.
city.do.choir.prompt: E — listen to the choir rehearsal
city.do.cinema.1: The Man Who Waited for the Lighthouse. He waited forty years, and all that time the lighthouse waited for him. The whole hall cried at the end. Me too, a bit.
city.do.cinema.2: A comedy about a holidaymaker whose hat blew away. The hat flew round the whole town and came back. We laughed so hard the screen shook.
city.do.cinema.3: Before the film, the reel "The Sun Is Our Home". The film snapped at the best bit, and for a minute we all watched white light.
city.do.cinema.4: The film was old and silent, with a pianist playing along. By the end I felt it was me up there on the screen, walking down an empty street.
city.do.cooking.1: They trusted me with the potatoes. The peel came off in one long spiral, and the cook said, "There's a husband in the making."
city.do.cooking.2: I chopped onions and cried while the cook told me about her first husband, and I couldn't tell which was making me cry.
city.do.cooking.3: I stirred the kissel with a big wooden spoon so it wouldn't go lumpy. It went lumpy anyway, but less than it might have.
city.do.cooking.4: I laid the cutlets on the tray in neat rows, like toy soldiers. They let me taste the first one. It was the general.
city.do.dance.1: I shuffled about to a waltz, counting one-two-three under my breath. On "three" I always trod on my own foot.
city.do.dance.2: An old couple turned so lightly the floor might have been water. I tried it: the floor turned out to be parquet.
city.do.dance.3: The dance teacher clapped: "Straighten your back, young man! You're not picking mushrooms!"
city.do.dance.4: The music stopped and I turned a little longer. Nobody laughed. That's how it's done here.
city.do.darkroom.1: In the red light the pier slowly surfaced on the white paper. As if someone were remembering it.
city.do.darkroom.2: Left it too long in the developer and the print went black. The club leader said: "Night photography. Conceptual."
city.do.darkroom.3: On someone else's film that we developed, there was me. From behind, on the promenade. I don't remember being photographed.
city.do.darkroom.4: It smells of vinegar and secrets. The prints dry on a line with clothes-pegs, like washing.
city.do.darkroom.prompt: E — develop prints in the darkroom
city.do.darts.1: First dart in the wall, second in the two, third dead in the bull. I stopped there so as not to spoil it.
city.do.darts.2: The board is full of holes like a night sky. I added three more stars.
city.do.darts.3: Someone behind me said: "Don't aim with your eye, aim with your elbow." I tried. Hit the door frame with my elbow.
city.do.darts.4: Forty-one points. Someone chalked my name on the board. Spelt wrong, but still nice.
city.do.easel.1: I painted the sea. It looks like the sea, if you really want it to. The studio leader said: "Bold."
city.do.easel.2: I mixed blue and yellow and got green. Mixed everything and got a puddle. That's a discovery too.
city.do.easel.3: I drew the sun in the corner like a little kid, with stick rays. Someone beside me sighed: "Like everyone does. And rightly so."
city.do.easel.4: I spent an hour on one cup. The cup came out crooked, but its shadow looks real.
city.do.exercise_bike.1: I rode three kilometres on the exercise bike and stayed where I was. Like in a dream.
city.do.exercise_bike.2: The counter's broken and always shows "12". I pedalled until twelve started to feel like a lot.
city.do.exercise_bike.3: The bike faces a window onto the sea. I imagined riding the promenade to the lighthouse, overtaking the bus.
city.do.exercise_bike.4: The pedals creak in waltz time. One-two-three, one-two-three. My legs got tired; the tune stayed.
city.do.eye_chart.1: E, F, P… T, O, Z… I read the bottom line by heart: it's the same in every clinic in the world.
city.do.eye_chart.2: I covered my left eye with the spoon. The right sees better, but the left seems to see something else.
city.do.eye_chart.3: "Twenty-twenty!" said the nurse. I was alarmed at first, then understood it was good.
city.do.eye_chart.4: The last line blurs and forms a word that isn't on the chart. I blinked, and everything was as it should be.
city.do.fortune.1: The mechanical fortune-teller nodded and gave me a card: "Soon you will be where you have already been."
city.do.fortune.2: The card: "Your sun is rising. Don't oversleep." In small print: "The machine accepts no responsibility."
city.do.fortune.3: The fortune-teller froze with her hand raised, thought, and gave me a blank card. Probably a good sign.
city.do.fortune.4: "The person you seek is seeking you too. Meet in the middle." The middle of what, it doesn't say.
city.do.fountain.1: The water's so cold my teeth ached. The jet squirts sideways, so I washed my face as well.
city.do.fountain.2: I drank and felt the water going down, as if someone had drawn a cool ruler through me.
city.do.fountain.3: The fountain tastes of iron and childhood. I don't know how I know what childhood tastes like.
city.do.fountain.4: A pigeon waited beside me while I drank. I stepped away and it didn't drink. Maybe it just wanted to stand there.
city.do.haircut.1: "How do you want it?" "However." "Short back and sides, then." Half an hour later I looked like a photo on a notice board.
city.do.haircut.2: The barber talked about fishing and never once looked at the scissors. It came out even. Nearly.
city.do.haircut.3: They sprayed me with cologne, and all evening I smell like someone's grandad at a party.
city.do.haircut.4: In the mirror facing the mirror I saw an endless corridor of me. In the furthest one I think I was smiling.
city.do.jukebox.1: I pressed B7 and A3 started playing. The machine knows best. A song about a gull who didn't come back.
city.do.jukebox.2: The record hisses like sea on shingle. A woman sings of a summer that "isn't over yet but is already remembered".
city.do.jukebox.3: I put on a foxtrot. Two old ladies by the window got up and went once round the floor, then sat down as if nothing had happened.
city.do.jukebox.4: The jukebox swallowed the coin and pondered. A minute later it played a march, loud and out of place.
city.do.lottery.1: I unrolled the ticket: "A postcard." No-lose means honest. A postcard of the lighthouse.
city.do.lottery.2: On the back of the winning ticket, handwritten: "And a little extra luck." They gave me no luck, just a postcard.
city.do.lottery.3: Three of us turned the ticket drum: me, the woman and the wind. Out came a postcard of the promenade.
city.do.lottery.4: "The top prize is a bicycle," the woman said. "Nobody's ever won it. Maybe it doesn't exist. Here's a postcard."
city.do.lottery.prompt: E — draw a no-lose lottery ticket
city.do.mats.1: Forward roll, backward roll. On the third the world slid a little, so I lay there until it came back.
city.do.mats.2: The mats smell of rubber, dust and other people's victories. Lying on them is nice and a little shameful.
city.do.mats.3: I tried a handstand. Held it a second, just long enough to see the hall upside down. I liked it.
city.do.mats.4: I did a cartwheel. Crooked as a squiggle, but a cartwheel. The mat sighed under me with all its foam.
city.do.microphone.1: "One, two, testing." My voice flew round the hall and came back someone else's, grown up.
city.do.microphone.2: The mic howled, and the cleaner in the doorway shook her mop at me. I pretended it was intentional.
city.do.microphone.3: I said "Hello" to the empty hall. The hall didn't answer, but it seemed to be listening.
city.do.microphone.4: I wanted to sing but only remembered the chorus. Sang the chorus. The echo sang it again, better.
city.do.microphone.prompt: E — say something into the microphone
city.do.misc.1: I fiddled with it, prodded it, broke nothing. A success already.
city.do.misc.2: I didn't work out how it works, but I looked very serious.
city.do.misc.3: Someone had left a note on it: "Don't touch. Touched. Broken." I didn't touch it.
city.do.payphone.1: I dialled a number at random. A woman answered, said "Hello, hello", fell silent and said softly: "Is that you?" I hung up.
city.do.payphone.2: I rang the speaking clock. "The time is exactly…" and the voice faltered. Then went on brightly.
city.do.payphone.3: Long rings in the receiver, and between them a faraway murmur, like in a seashell.
city.do.payphone.4: The phone ate the coin and didn't connect. I thumped it, the way everyone does. It returned my coin and someone else's.
city.do.photo_booth.1: Four flashes. In the first I'm blinking, in the second serious, in the third smiling, in the fourth I'm not there.
city.do.photo_booth.2: The photographer ducked under the black cloth and said "watch the birdie". A real sparrow flew out from under the roof.
city.do.photo_booth.3: The prints were ready in ten minutes. I look more like myself in them than in a mirror. They're going in my diary.
city.do.photo_booth.4: The photographer stood me against a painted sea. The real one was right outside, but the painted one, he says, comes out better.
city.do.photo_portrait.1: "Chin up a little. Don't blink. Think of something nice." Click. "Ready on Thursday."
city.do.photo_portrait.2: The photographer moves the lamp, then me, then the lamp again. In the picture I'll look as if I'd lived here for years.
city.do.photo_portrait.3: Behind me a pale blue backdrop, like the sky over a calm sea. "Smile, young man, this is a resort."
city.do.piano.1: I played "Chopsticks" with one finger. Behind a door someone joined in on a violin, in a different key.
city.do.piano.2: One key sticks and sounds like a cough. I played the whole tune so as to avoid it.
city.do.piano.3: I pressed three white keys in a row and got something like a sunrise. Couldn't do it again.
city.do.piano.4: The music on the stand says "play as if no one is listening". I did. And no one was.
city.do.pool.1: I swam four lengths of crawl and two of doggy paddle. The lifeguard whistled, approvingly I think.
city.do.pool.2: Underwater everything is green and echoing. I lay on the bottom and watched the light dance over the tiles in a net.
city.do.pool.3: It smells of chlorine and wet towels. I got out and my body felt heavy and happy.
city.do.pool.4: A granny in a flowery cap swam beside me and lapped me twice. She said she'd been swimming like that for fifty years.
city.do.potters_wheel.1: The clay spun and wriggled out of my hands like a live fish. It ended up an ashtray. I'd wanted a vase.
city.do.potters_wheel.2: The potter laid her hands over mine and the walls rose by themselves. "Like that. Don't press. Persuade."
city.do.potters_wheel.3: Clay up to my elbows. The little bowl is lopsided, but it's mine. They promised to fire it by Thursday.
city.do.potters_wheel.4: The wheel hums like a bumblebee, and to that hum I stopped thinking entirely. Very useful.
city.do.potters_wheel.prompt: E — sit at the potter's wheel
city.do.pump_room.1: I filled a bottle at the tap. The water smells of iron and a bit of egg. "Good for you," said a guest in a sun hat.
city.do.pump_room.2: In the pump room everyone sips from the spouts of china mugs and looks out of the window as if at a screen.
city.do.pump_room.3: A sign by the spring: "Temperature 12°. High mineral content. Drink slowly, think of good things."
city.do.pump_room.4: The water runs warm from the tap, as if it passed something hot underground. The sun, probably.
city.do.pump_room.prompt: E — fill a bottle with mineral water
city.do.punching_bag.1: The bag swung and came back, like a grudge. I hit it until it was just a bag.
city.do.punching_bag.2: An old coach showed me a one-two and said: "Punch as if you're knocking on a door you really need."
city.do.punching_bag.3: The gloves are too big and smell of other people's victories. The bag is old leather, all patches.
city.do.punching_bag.4: After ten minutes I was puffing like a steam engine, and inside it went quiet and empty, like a gym in the evening.
city.do.radio.1: "…wind north-westerly, five to seven metres a second, clear on the coast, fog in places in the mountains…" I'm fog in places too.
city.do.radio.2: Between stations I caught a rustling silence, as if someone very far away were breathing into a phone.
city.do.radio.3: A request show: "For Nina Petrovna on the third floor, from the neighbours who promise to stop drilling."
city.do.radio.4: The time signal: six short pips. Every clock in the room suddenly felt guilty.
city.do.radio_set.1: "CQ, CQ, this is Lyudmilovsk." Through the crackle someone in Tiksi answered: they have snow and are in good spirits.
city.do.radio_set.2: The meter needle trembles, the valves glow orange. The Morse in the headphones sounds like rain on a tin roof.
city.do.radio_set.3: On the wall, QSL cards from all over the world. One from a Japanese schoolboy: a mountain and a hundred signatures.
city.do.radio_set.4: I called for half an hour. Only the sea answered: an even hiss on every frequency at once.
city.do.record_player.1: I lowered the needle. Crackle first, then a violin, then crackle again, as if the music were coming through rain.
city.do.record_player.2: On the sleeve, an orchestra on a beach, all in tailcoats and barefoot.
city.do.record_player.3: The record stuck on one phrase: "…and the sun, and the sun, and the sun…" I didn't fix it.
city.do.record_player.4: A fairy-tale record. The narrator's voice is so kind I listened to the whole of "The Runaway Bun", though I know how it ends.
city.do.ring_toss.1: One ring landed on a bottle and slid straight off. The woman said: "I'll count it, you tried."
city.do.ring_toss.2: The rings are as light as pancakes and fly where they like. One went into the ice cream kiosk next door.
city.do.ring_toss.3: Three out of three! The prize was a paper flower. I tucked it in my breast pocket. It looks good there.
city.do.ring_toss.4: The boy next to me scored every time and dutifully gave the prizes to his little sister. I watched instead of throwing.
city.do.scales.1: The nurse slid the weight along and wrote down a number. "You're growing," she said. I didn't know I was.
city.do.scales.2: The scales showed the same as yesterday, though I wasn't here yesterday. The nurse wasn't surprised.
city.do.scales.3: I took my trainers off to make it fairer. Three hundred grams lighter, and one small worry less.
city.do.scales.4: Height and weight went into a card in beautiful handwriting. The card, it turned out, already had my name on it.
city.do.school_desk.1: Geography. The teacher pointed on the map to where we live, and there was only blue paint there.
city.do.school_desk.2: Literature: poems about autumn. The boy by the window read so well that it clouded over outside for a minute.
city.do.school_desk.3: Carved on the desk: "Whoever reads this is great." I read it. Astronomy, topic: "Our Sun". I listened without breathing.
city.do.school_desk.4: Nobody asked who I was. They gave me a squared exercise book and said: "Take notes, you'll be asked later."
city.do.school_desk.prompt: E — sit in on a lesson
city.do.sewing_machine.1: The machine chirred like a grasshopper. The seam went zigzag though I wanted straight. Zigzag is a style too.
city.do.sewing_machine.2: I sewed a sun-shaped patch on my jacket. The women in the circle said that's what's in this season.
city.do.sewing_machine.3: The thread snapped, the needle broke, and the machine, an old Seagull older than my mum, carried on as if nothing had happened.
city.do.sewing_machine.4: I learnt to thread a needle. On the twelfth try it worked, and I felt like a surgeon.
city.do.shooting_gallery.1: I knocked down the duck, the windmill and the bear. The bear played a tune as it fell. The man said it hadn't done that in ages.
city.do.shooting_gallery.2: The rifle pulls left. I aimed further right, and it took offence and started pulling right.
city.do.shooting_gallery.3: Five shots, no hits. But now I know exactly where their light bulb hangs.
city.do.shooting_gallery.4: I hit the little sun on the backdrop. It didn't fall, just swayed. The man went pale for some reason.
city.do.sink.1: The tap coughed first, then gave water as cold as a mountain stream. I washed my face and woke up a second time.
city.do.sink.2: A mountain of cups in the sink. I washed three and set them upside down. Someone will be surprised later.
city.do.sink.3: The water smells of iron and a little of the sea. Probably everything here smells a little of the sea.
city.do.sink.4: A sign above the sink: "Save water: there's little of it and many of us." I turned the tap tighter.
city.do.slide_projector.1: A filmstrip, "The Journey of a Droplet". It evaporated, became a cloud, fell as rain and went back to the sea. Happy ending.
city.do.slide_projector.2: A frame jammed and a surprised-looking owl hung on the wall for ages. Everyone laughed; the owl went on being surprised.
city.do.slide_projector.3: Slides from someone's trip north: a geyser, snow, tents, people in jumpers squinting at the sun.
city.do.slide_projector.4: Click, a new frame. Click, another. The projector hums warmly like a cat and smells of heated dust.
city.do.stage.1: They were rehearsing a play about fishermen. An actor in a pea coat forgot his lines, and the prompter whispered them to the whole hall.
city.do.stage.2: A conjurer pulled a pigeon from his hat, then another, then another. They settled on the chandelier and stayed.
city.do.stage.3: A children's troupe danced the sailors' hornpipe. The smallest sailor was always a beat behind and the best of them all.
city.do.stage.4: The stage is empty, one spotlight on. Somehow watching an empty stage is as interesting as a full one.
city.do.stove.1: The gas caught in a blue crown with a soft "pff". The kettle thought about it and began to hum.
city.do.stove.2: On the stove, a pan with painted words: "Kompot. Don't touch. This means you, Valera." I'm not Valera.
city.do.stove.3: The kettle whistled like a little steam engine, and everyone in the corridor turned round as if someone had arrived.
city.do.stove.4: I waited by the stove. My face was reflected in the oven window, warm and a little bit someone else's.
city.do.strongman.1: The needle crawled up to "Schoolboy". Fair enough. I am one.
city.do.strongman.2: I hit it so hard the bell at the top rang. Everyone turned. I turned too, to see who'd done it.
city.do.strongman.3: Missed. The mallet slipped, and the tester showed "Dreamer". There's no such mark on it, actually.
city.do.strongman.4: "Hero"! Well, nearly: "Nearly Hero". My palm stings, but the pride stings more.
city.do.study_desk.1: In the exercise book, a problem about two trains heading towards each other. I decided they'd better just wave.
city.do.study_desk.2: The lamp warms the top of my head, the pen leaks, outside someone calls someone out to the yard. Not me.
city.do.study_desk.3: In the margin someone has drawn a little man running from the word "TEST". I drew him a bicycle.
city.do.study_desk.4: I learned four lines by heart. The fifth kept running off, like a cat called in for a bath.
city.do.table_football.1: I spun the rods so hard the goalie did a somersault. I let the goal in anyway.
city.do.table_football.2: One player has a chipped nose and always misses. I named him Senya and cheered for him.
city.do.table_football.3: Five–three! The boys round the table clapped as if it were a World Cup final.
city.do.table_football.4: The ball got stuck in a corner and the two of us shook the table for a minute. Best part of the game.
city.do.table_tennis.1: We played to eleven. The ball went under the radiator twice, and both times the cleaner fished it out with her mop.
city.do.table_tennis.2: My opponent served with so much spin the ball seemed to go back to him on its own. Lost, but learnt the stance.
city.do.table_tennis.3: Tock-tock-tock. In five minutes I forgot everything but the white ball. Better than sleep.
city.do.table_tennis.4: The net sagged, the bat was sticky and the ball had a dent. 11–9 to me. Not fair, but nice.
city.do.telescope.1: The coin clinked and the shutter opened. I saw a barge, on the barge a dog, and the dog looking very important.
city.do.telescope.2: I pointed the telescope at the horizon. Where the sea ends something glints: a wave or a window.
city.do.telescope.3: I found our lighthouse through it, then my own footprints on the sand, then my time ran out.
city.do.telescope.4: I looked north at the mountains. On one slope something is steaming, thin as a kettle in a faraway kitchen.
city.do.track.1: I ran on the roof, with the whole town and the whole sea below. It felt as if with a big enough run-up I could take off.
city.do.track.2: Three laps. At every bend the wind changed: at my back, in my face, from the side smelling of fried fish.
city.do.track.3: Painted on the track: starts, finishes and, for some reason, a little sun. I finished on the sun.
city.do.track.4: An old resident jogged beside me in tracksuit bottoms and said he'd run here since the building went up. He wasn't even out of breath.
city.do.track.prompt: E — run a lap of the roof track
city.do.tv.1: A wildlife programme was on. A pelican swallowed a fish and looked into the camera as if waiting for applause.
city.do.tv.2: The weather: "Sunny tomorrow. Sunny the day after. Beyond that we haven't looked yet."
city.do.tv.3: The set showed only snow, and the guests watched it anyway, swaying their heads as if it were the sea.
city.do.tv.4: A request concert was on. Someone from Lyudmilovsk asked for a song "for the one who'll come back". It was a song about summer.
city.do.vaulting_horse.1: I ran up, pushed off the springboard and landed sitting astride the horse, like a real rider. The horse didn't mind.
city.do.vaulting_horse.2: I cleared it! Landed on the mat, palms burning, and everything inside me ringing like the last bell of the day.
city.do.vaulting_horse.3: The leather on the horse is rubbed shiny in one spot: thousands of palms before mine pushed off right here.
city.do.vaulting_horse.4: The coach gave me a thumbs-up from across the hall. Or he was fixing his whistle. I decided it was the thumb.
city.do.wall_bars.1: I climbed right up to the ceiling. From there you can see a volleyball on top of the cupboard, lost about five years ago.
city.do.wall_bars.2: I hung and raised my legs in an L. My stomach protested, but my head cleared.
city.do.wall_bars.3: The rungs are smooth as river pebbles: so many hands have held them.
city.do.wall_bars.4: I hung upside down and the world turned over. It's not bad that way either, it turns out.
city.do.wall_bars.prompt: E — hang on the wall bars
city.do.washing_machine.1: Someone's socks circle in the round window like fish in a tank. The blue one keeps falling behind.
city.do.washing_machine.2: On the spin cycle the machine hops across the floor like a living thing. I held it with my hand and it calmed down.
city.do.washing_machine.3: A rota above the machines: "Mon: 2nd floor, Tue: 3rd…" For Sunday: "Whoever gets up first."
city.do.washing_machine.4: It smells of warm laundry and Lotus washing powder. I'd like to climb into the basket and sleep.
city.do.washing_machine.prompt: E — look into the washing machine
city.do.watch.1: I watched until I forgot I was watching. That only happens with the sea and fire.
city.do.watch.2: Nothing special happened, and that was good.
city.do.watch.3: Time went past me like a tram past an empty stop.
city.do.workbench.1: I planed a block of wood. The shavings curled like the hair of the girl on a postcard. Smells of pine and summer.
city.do.workbench.2: Got the nail in on the third try. The first two went into my thumb. The shop teacher said: "Happens. You'll remember now."
city.do.workbench.3: I made a nesting box. Crooked, but they say birds prefer them that way: cosier.
city.do.workbench.4: Carved into the bench: "Vitya was here, 1979." I thought about it and carved nothing.
city.door.any.1: Locked. Behind the door a tap is dripping.
city.door.any.2: The door won't give. Not today, probably.
city.door.gallery.1: The lift to the viewing gallery, 32 metres. A sign: "Ride: 40 seconds. View: free. Dizziness: at your own expense."
city.door.gallery.2: The GALLERY button is rubbed shiny, the floor buttons look new. Everyone here rides up to look at the sea.
city.door.gallery.3: The lift attendant knits on a stool by the doors. "It's windy up top. Hold on to your hat or it'll fly off to the lighthouse. It's happened."
city.door.roof.1: "Roof access. No unauthorised persons." The caretaker probably has the key.
city.door.roof.2: Wind and sunlight seep from under the door. Up there you must see the whole sea.
city.door.staff.1: "Staff only." Behind the door someone is laughing and clinking cups.
city.door.staff.2: A sign: "Knock before entering." I knocked. Nobody answered.
city.fest.cashier.1: The cashier in a paper crown: "Happy holiday! If I run out of coins, your change comes in sweets today."
city.fest.cinema.1: "Holiday screening: an old comedy, one ticket lets two in. Bring the person you laugh with."
city.fest.cinema.2: "December 31: a midnight screening of Carnival Night. No champagne inside. Tangerines are fine."
city.fest.cloakroom.1: "Happy holiday! Don't lose your tag: half the town's here today, and all the hats look the same."
city.fest.club.1: "Holiday today! No clubs, the choir sings on the square at seven. The chess tournament is postponed: the pieces are resting too."
city.fest.club.2: "Lantern night: we're gluing paper lanterns in the foyer from four. Glue and paper are ours, the candle is yours."
city.fest.counter.1: Happy holiday! We're open till the last customer today, and then everyone's off to the square.
city.fest.counter.2: The tangerines ran out this morning. Happy New Year all the same! Come early on the thirty-first.
city.fest.health.1: "On holidays the doctor on duty sees patients. Don't overeat, keep your ears away from the crackers and your eyes away from the sparklers."
city.fest.lost.1: "Found on the square after the holiday: three mittens, a little flag, a toy pipe and someone's brand-new hat. Ask at the kiosk."
city.fest.prices.1: Chalked at the top: "For the holiday, pies at the old price, free tea with any pie."
city.fest.prices.2: "Sea Festival: fresh herring straight from the boats, smoked by lunchtime. Queue from the lamppost."
city.fest.tickets.1: "No tickets left for the holiday concert, but the square is free to everyone, and you hear it better there anyway."
city.fest.timetable.1: Added in pencil: "Holiday today: buses run to the Sunday timetable, the last one at 23:40."
city.fest.wallpaper.1: The wall newspaper's holiday issue: all foil stars, and in the corner a poem by class 7B that rhymes "holiday" with "go away" three times.
city.home.aoki.bed.1: The bed is covered with a patchwork quilt. Each patch is from someone's dress, and on some the name is pinned.
city.home.aoki.bed.2: In the middle of the quilt, a bright yellow patch with no name. Her own, I suppose.
city.home.aoki.bed.3: Someone else's bed, and the quilt is like a family album. I didn't touch it; I only looked.
city.home.aoki.calendar.1: A calendar of fittings. "Tuesday: wedding dress, Zoya from the vegetable row. Thursday: costumes for the Rassvet, the tale of the Sun and the Wind."
city.home.aoki.calendar.2: Added on Thursday: "The Wind's cloak is ready. The Sun isn't. Ring the Rassvet: tell the Sun to wait."
city.home.aoki.calendar.3: Hanging from a nail under the calendar, a tape measure. She has measured the whole town with it, I suppose: waists, heights, sleeve lengths.
city.home.aoki.machine.1: Under the needle, a dress of pale linen, almost finished. Suns are embroidered round the hem, small as freckles. One isn't finished.
city.home.aoki.machine.2: Beside it, an order tag: "The girl from the market, for her graduation. Her fabric, my suns. She didn't ask for them. But they'll suit her."
city.home.aoki.machine.3: The sewing machine is older than the woman of the house. A sticker on it: "Don't rush me." I'm not sure which of them it's addressed to.
city.home.aoki.machine.4: In the pincushion, threads in every shade of yellow: lemon, honey, "like six in the morning", "like seven in the evening".
city.home.aoki.patterns.1: Twenty years of a fashion magazine, but the designs have been re-cut: in the margins her pencil corrects every dress.
city.home.aoki.patterns.2: An album of patterns "for the whole family". On the children's coat page: "Made for Timo from house three. He outgrew it in a month. Making it again."
city.home.aoki.patterns.3: Between the patterns, a sketch of the Sun's costume for the play: a round cloak and rays to be sewn on "so that they give warmth".
city.home.aoki.picture.1: A still life: spools of thread, scissors and an apple. Inscribed: "Painted by a friend because I took up her coat. We consider ourselves even."
city.home.aoki.picture.2: The scissors in the picture are open and pointing at the window, as if they'd like to cut out a piece of sky.
city.home.aoki.picture.3: Three pearl-headed pins are stuck in the picture frame. This is where they live, it seems.
city.home.aoki.record.1: A tango record. A note on the sleeve: "Don't sew to this: the seam starts dancing."
city.home.aoki.record.2: I dropped the needle. A slow tango with a bandoneon. I caught myself swaying and stopped.
city.home.aoki.record.3: Under the records, a box of buttons, all different. On the lid: "Not one is spare. Each came from someone."
city.home.aoki.science.1: On the shelf where you'd expect science: a handbook of textile fibres, with a bookmark: "Linen loves the sun. So do I."
city.home.aoki.science.2: A little book, "The Chemistry of Dyes". The recipe "yellow from onion skins" is underlined; beside it: "Smells of soup, but the colour is like morning."
city.home.aoki.science.3: A dried marigold between the pages. One more attempt at "that" yellow, it seems.
city.home.aoki.swatches.1: A wall of fabric swatches pinned in rows. Each is labelled not by name but by weather: "Overcast", "Windy", "Clear but cold".
city.home.aoki.swatches.2: In the last row, an empty space and a note: "Sun: not found yet. Gold isn't it, yellow isn't it."
city.home.aoki.swatches.3: I looked at the swatches a long time and picked the one labelled "Like seven in the evening". I laid it by the empty space. Didn't pin it: let her decide.
city.home.asanov.cot.1: The caretaker's camp bed, a neatly folded blanket on it and a torch. "In case something leaks in the night," he explains, though I didn't ask.
city.home.asanov.cot.2: Over the camp bed, a calendar of lighthouses. The days are crossed off up to today; today is ringed: "Don't forget: bulb on the fourth floor."
city.home.asanov.cot.3: "Don't sit there, it's a workplace," the caretaker says of the camp bed. And sits down on it himself with a newspaper.
city.home.asanov.desk.1: The caretaker, Toivo Asanov, looks up from the repair book. "Going up to Markovich? Go on, it's open. Just don't touch the paint; his paint's alive."
city.home.asanov.desk.2: "Requests this week: taps, two; light bulbs, five; 'neighbours singing', one. I don't act on the neighbours. Let them sing."
city.home.asanov.desk.3: "Markovich is at his window every evening at sunset. If his light's off, he's painting. If it's on, the sunset's over."
city.home.asanov.radio.1: The radio in the den has been tuned to one station for so long the knob has rusted. "...and finally: all quiet in Lyudmilovsk."
city.home.asanov.radio.2: A football match on. The caretaker isn't for either side. "I'm for the ball. It gets the worst of it."
city.home.asanov.radio.3: Between weather reports, a button accordion plays softly. The caretaker taps his foot and pretends he isn't.
city.home.asanov.rules.1: "House rules: 1. Quiet after 23:00. 2. Bicycles under the stairs. 3. Don't feed the cat from the third floor; he lies about being hungry."
city.home.asanov.rules.2: "The roof key is with the caretaker. Watching the sunset from the roof: by appointment. Appointments always open."
city.home.asanov.rules.3: Under the rules, a photo: the whole house at a Saturday clean-up, with rakes and buckets. Everyone is squinting at the sun except the cat.
city.home.girma.bed.1: A double bed, and pushed right up against it a child's camp bed. Tomo comes over to Papa's at night, it seems.
city.home.girma.bed.2: On Mama's pillow, a parcel in gift paper with a tag: "For Mama. Open on Friday. There's a sun inside (not a real one)."
city.home.girma.bed.3: Someone else's bedroom, someone else's presents. I backed towards the door, trying not to rustle.
city.home.girma.calendar.1: The family calendar. Mama's work days are marked with a train. Days off with little suns. There are fewer suns than trains.
city.home.girma.calendar.2: Friday is ringed: "Mama home!" Beside it in another hand: "Show Mama the spots. Tomo, his drawing. Daisuke, don't be late back from the market."
city.home.girma.calendar.3: I pencilled a tiny star into Friday's square, so small no one would guess who. Let there be one more sun.
city.home.girma.chart.1: A poster on the wall: "The Sun in Cross-section": core, layers, prominences. The core is ringed in pen: "Warm in here. Just like home."
city.home.girma.chart.2: At the bottom of the poster, a table of sunrises for the year. The ones Daisuke saw himself are ticked. Almost as many ticks as days.
city.home.girma.chart.3: A child's question is taped to the side: "What if the sun gets tired?" No answer. A hard one, I suppose.
city.home.girma.picture.1: A still life: a teapot, a lemon and three apples. On the back: "From the market, from the woman at the next stall. In exchange for the story of Saturn's rings."
city.home.girma.picture.2: The apples in the picture are exactly the kind Daisuke sells: red with a yellow side. She must have painted them straight from his stall.
city.home.girma.picture.3: The picture hangs a little crooked. Under it, a child's hand has drawn a fourth apple on the wallpaper. Very like the others.
city.home.girma.record.1: A record, "Music of the Spheres": electronic sounds like outer space. In pen on the sleeve: "For Nino. To listen to on the train."
city.home.girma.record.2: I dropped the needle. The sounds stretch out like light from a distant star. Good music for waiting, I'd think.
city.home.girma.record.3: Beside it, a stack of children's records; on the top one a sticker: "Tomo's. Don't touch, it's mine. Only Papa can."
city.home.girma.science.1: "Observing for Amateurs", pages full of notes. The chapter on sunspots is marked with a train ticket: the line Nino rides.
city.home.girma.science.2: An eighth-year physics textbook, for Tomo to grow into, it seems. On the flyleaf: "To my son. When you ask 'why', think first yourself. Then ask me."
city.home.girma.science.3: A pamphlet, "How to Keep an Observing Diary". Tip number one is underlined: "Write down even what seems unimportant. Especially that."
city.home.girma.shelf.1: On the shelf, star charts rolled into tubes and held with rubber bands. Each with a tag: "Spring", "Summer", "Autumn", "Winter", "Tomo".
city.home.girma.shelf.2: I unrolled the chart tagged "Tomo". The night sky, every constellation, and in the middle a big felt-tip sun. Caption: "Papa said there's no sun at night. I drew one anyway."
city.home.girma.shelf.3: Under the child's sun, Papa's handwriting, small: "He's right. It's always there. Just on the other side."
city.home.girma.shelf.4: The other charts are covered in pencil: arrows, dates, question marks. "Winter" has a ring from a mug of tea. The nights were long.
city.home.girma.telescope.1: A telescope by the window with a dark solar filter on the lens. Beside it, a notebook headed "Spots": a drawing of the sun with dots every single day. Not one day missed in three years.
city.home.girma.telescope.2: I looked through the eyepiece with the filter on. The sun is a dark orange disc with two tiny dots on it, like freckles. I drew them in the notebook next to his drawings.
city.home.girma.telescope.3: A slip on the tripod in a child's hand: "Papa! Don't look without the filter! Mama told me to keep an eye on you."
city.home.girma.telescope.4: The last entry in the notebook: "Fewer spots. The sun is calm. As if it were waiting for something." Hurried writing: before the market, I suppose.
city.home.holm.aquarium.1: Inside the tank, a model lighthouse and a sunken ship. The fish swim through its portholes as if it were their regular route.
city.home.holm.aquarium.2: A label on the lid: "Crew: Bosun, Cook, Second Mate." No sign of the second mate. On watch, probably.
city.home.holm.aquarium.3: The air pump hums steadily, like a ship's engine far below. A good sound for a retired navigator to fall asleep to, I suppose.
city.home.holm.bed.1: The bed is made navy-fashion, not a single crease. You could measure the blanket with a ruler.
city.home.holm.bed.2: Over the headboard, a barometer. The needle points to "Change". A slip of paper is stuck under it: "Same as me."
city.home.holm.bed.3: It's someone else's bed. I didn't even sit down: just stood beside it and left the bedroom more quietly than I came in.
city.home.holm.chess.1: A game left unfinished. Next to it, a postcard with a move: "Queen to f5. Your move, old pirate. Write back. K." The postmark is two months old.
city.home.holm.chess.2: The pieces stand as if just set down. The white queen is slightly off her square: someone picked her up and put her back.
city.home.holm.chess.3: Under the board, a stack of postcards held with a rubber band. Forty years of games by post. I didn't count who's winning.
city.home.holm.chess.4: I studied the position a long time. There's an answer, I think. But it isn't my game, and I put my hands in my pockets.
city.home.holm.concierge.1: "Here for Viktor Sergeyevich? His door's not locked; he never locks it. He says: 'On board ship we never locked the cabins.'"
city.home.holm.concierge.2: "Every morning at six he goes out on the steps to watch the sunrise. Then he reports to me like on watch: 'Sun in position.'"
city.home.holm.concierge.3: "He's got a friend overseas; they play chess by post. No postcards for a while now. He checks the box every day and tells me: 'The post is like the sea: sometimes it's becalmed.'"
city.home.holm.cooking.1: A cookbook, "A Galley for One". Bookmarked at "Navy macaroni". The bookmark hasn't moved in years, by the look of it.
city.home.holm.cooking.2: Between the pages, a dried bay leaf and a note in a woman's hand: "Vitya, salt goes in at the end, not whenever you remember."
city.home.holm.cooking.3: A recipe for "Navigator's tea": brew it strong, drink it at dawn, look east. The last step is underlined twice.
city.home.holm.log.1: Between the pilot books, a fat exercise book: "Watch Log. Ashore." Every day: wind, pressure, sunrise. "Sunrise 6:12. Saw it."
city.home.holm.log.2: The last entries are shorter: "Wind W, 4 m/s. The receiver's dead. No forecast. No forecast is like no compass." After that, blank.
city.home.holm.log.3: In the margin, in a child's handwriting: "Grandpa, is the sun on a timetable too?" And the answer: "It's the only thing that's never late."
city.home.holm.log.4: The pilot books' spines are worn: the Baltic, the North Sea, Biscay. The ones about far seas are like new. He never got there, it seems.
city.home.holm.painting.1: A storm: a wave higher than the mast and a small steamer with no intention of giving up. In the corner, in pencil: "MV Ladoga, Biscay, 1974. All alive."
city.home.holm.painting.2: The frame hangs slightly crooked. It's been straightened many times: there's a pale mark on the wallpaper all round it, as if from the ship's roll.
city.home.holm.painting.3: If you look at it long enough, the floor seems to start listing too. I stepped back, just in case.
city.home.holm.radio.1: I turned the dial of the house radio. Through the crackle: "...the coast: westerly wind, three to five metres, clearing towards evening, sea up to force one..." Viktor Sergeyevich would have liked that.
city.home.holm.radio.2: "Sunrise tomorrow: six fourteen." The announcer said it as solemnly as if announcing a train's arrival.
city.home.holm.radio.3: The concierge, from her desk: "He comes down every evening to hear the forecast. His own set broke, and he won't have it fixed. Says it gives him a reason to come out."
city.home.holm.record.1: A record of waltzes on the player, a globe beside it. The globe is turned to the Atlantic, with a sticking plaster on one spot.
city.home.holm.record.2: I dropped the needle. A waltz, crackling as if it were being played in the middle of a storm.
city.home.holm.record.3: Written on the sleeve in pen: "For Nina. We danced in Riga, 1961." There is no other Nina in the flat. Only this record.
city.home.holm.write.1: On the kitchen table the log lies open at today's date. I wrote in, under his hand, in mine: the wind, the temperature, what the radio promised. Next to his writing mine looks like a first-former's.
city.home.holm.write.2: In the "Sunrise" column I put a dash: I slept through it. Then I thought about it and added: "But it happened, that's certain."
city.home.holm.write.3: A sugar bowl on the table, an empty mug and glasses on a cord. He's only popped out: the kettle is still warm. I finished my line and left before he came back.
city.home.holm.write.prompt: E — write the forecast in the log
city.home.keeper.bed.1: I lay down on the keeper's cot. Overhead the shadow of the lamp above turns slowly, like the hand of an enormous clock.
city.home.keeper.bed.2: I dozed off to the sound of the sea. Woke because someone had put a rug over me. No one there. Only a cooling cup of tea on the table, not mine.
city.home.keeper.bed.3: The cot is narrow and hard, but you sleep surprisingly well on it. Because all night someone above you is keeping the light, I suppose.
city.home.keeper.chart.1: A chart of the coast with lighthouses and shoals. The arc of the light is pencilled in, and at its edge: "Beyond here nobody can see us. But we're here."
city.home.keeper.chart.2: To the west, where the land is, the chart breaks off, and two words are written there by hand: "Mires. Don't shine."
city.home.keeper.chart.3: Pinned in the corner, a postcard of a train running over the water to the island. On the back: "Arkasha, did you see? Off into the sunset again. Aram."
city.home.keeper.log.1: Two hands in the log: a round one, Aram Oliveira, evening watch, and a sharp one, Arkady Kobayashi, night watch. They hand over at half past midnight, always in one line: "Light burning."
city.home.keeper.log.2: On the inside of the cover, a tide table: "High water at the pier" for every day of the week. Tomorrow's time is underlined, with: "For the student from the capsules, if she asks."
city.home.keeper.log.3: An entry of Arkady's: "03:40. Quiet. Saw something glowing blue near the horizon. Not a ship. Noting it because I note everything."
city.home.keeper.log.4: An entry of Aram's: "21:15. Sunset. Someone on the promenade waved at the lighthouse. The lighthouse, I believe, waved back."
city.home.keeper.radio.1: The keepers' radio hisses, then a voice: "Lighthouse, this is the seiner Maria, we see you well, thank you." I don't know how to answer, and just nod at the radio.
city.home.keeper.radio.2: A forecast for sailors, slow enough to write down: "...visibility good; after midnight off the western shore, a glow of unknown origin..."
city.home.keeper.radio.3: Between messages, quiet: just the sea and, somewhere far off, someone's "over, over". The keepers listen to this silence for hours, I suppose.
city.home.keeper.shelf.1: "Lights and Marks of the Coast", "Sea Knots", and a fat exercise book of poems composed at night by the two keepers, a line per watch.
city.home.keeper.shelf.2: Aram's line: "We keep the light so someone will come back." Arkady's under it: "And if no one does, we keep it for the sun while it sleeps."
city.home.keeper.shelf.3: Between the books, a box of spare lamps, and on it: "Last spare. Order more. (Ordered 3 times.)"
city.home.kravets.bed.1: The bed is covered with a rug patterned with mountain goats. On the pillow, an open book face down: she fell asleep over it.
city.home.kravets.bed.2: Over the bed, a string of paper cranes. As many as the days she's lived by the sea. The last one isn't finished.
city.home.kravets.bed.3: Someone else's bed. I stood there, looked at the cranes and left without touching anything.
city.home.kravets.chart.1: A periodic table, and pinned over it, a drawing of a sunfish and a month's tide table. Today's line is empty.
city.home.kravets.chart.2: I pencilled the time of high water from the lighthouse log into a corner of her chart. Small, so she can rub it out if she wants to work it out herself.
city.home.kravets.chart.3: Under the chart, a poster of constellations. At the bottom, in her hand: "Once I pass, I'm going to the cape to watch the sun set right into the water."
city.home.kravets.desk.1: An oceanography exercise book open at a problem: "Find the time of high water at Lyudmilovsk pier tomorrow." No answer, just three crossed-out attempts and "???".
city.home.kravets.desk.2: In the margin of her notes: "The moon pulls the water. The sun pulls too, but less. Like Mum and Gran: both pull, one louder."
city.home.kravets.desk.3: Under the lamp, a countdown slip: "6 days to the exam". The 6 was a 7, the 7 was an 8.
city.home.kravets.desk.4: Next to it, an envelope with a letter from home, a mountain village: "Norochka, aren't you tired of the sea yet? It's snowing here. Come back once you've passed."
city.home.kravets.records.1: A record of songs from her mountains; a snowy peak on the sleeve and, in her mother's hand: "So you don't forget what home sounds like."
city.home.kravets.records.2: I dropped the needle. A choir sings in a language I don't know, but it's clearly about how far you can see from the top.
city.home.kravets.records.3: Beside it, a cassette, "Lectures, Year 2". On side two, the sea has been recorded over the lecture. Easier to study that way, I suppose.
city.home.kravets.shelf.1: "Physics of the Sea" in paperback, swollen with damp, as if it had been in the ocean itself.
city.home.kravets.shelf.2: An atlas of currents. The warm current is coloured orange, the cold one blue, and one near our shore yellow, with the question "why is it warm?".
city.home.kravets.shelf.3: Among the textbooks, a book of problems with answers. The answers at the back are covered with paper. On it: "Don't peek, Nora."
city.home.kravets.window.1: In the round window, a piece of sea. Today it's grey and silver. Yesterday, judging by the drawing on the glass, it was green.
city.home.kravets.window.2: On the sill, a jar of seawater, labelled: "Samples. Week 1." The water in it is the same as the sea, only quieter.
city.home.kravets.window.3: If you press against the glass you can see the lighthouse. At night she probably checks it's still lit.
city.home.notebooks.prompt: E — look at the exercise books
city.home.okada.art.1: An album of a painter who painted only haystacks at different times of day. In the margin: "There. I'm not the only one."
city.home.okada.art.2: A textbook, "Colour and Light". The chapter "Why the sun in a painting can never be brighter than white" is scribbled over: "It can. You just have to want it badly enough."
city.home.okada.art.3: A catalogue of an exhibition at the Rassvet culture house, 1979. His name is last on the list, in small type. Someone has ringed it in red.
city.home.okada.bed.1: A narrow bed covered with a checked rug spotted with paint. He sometimes falls asleep in his work shirt, it seems.
city.home.okada.bed.2: The bed is placed so that from the pillow you can see the window and the easel. The first thing he sees each morning is his work.
city.home.okada.bed.3: Thick glasses and a magnifier on the bedside table. The magnifier is turned to the window, catching a patch of sunlight.
city.home.okada.easel.1: On the easel, the sea seen from this very window. The same view as outside, only the sun on the canvas is lower and brighter than the real one.
city.home.okada.easel.2: On the back of the stretcher, in chalk: "No. 1112". Under the easel, a stack of canvases, all of the same window. The numbers run in order.
city.home.okada.easel.3: The paint tubes are labelled in big capitals: "YELLOW", "BLUE", "MORE YELLOW". His eyes aren't what they were, it seems.
city.home.okada.easel.4: A brush lies across the water jar, still damp. Today's canvas is begun: one horizon line and nothing else. He left in the middle of a thought.
city.home.okada.letter.1: On the table, an unfinished letter: "Dear Asya. Today I painted our window again. You'll say, why a thousand times the same..." I didn't read on.
city.home.okada.letter.2: Out of the corner of my eye I saw the last line anyway: "...because one day the sun will set differently, and I want to be at the window."
city.home.okada.letter.3: The envelope is already written, the stamp stuck on. No address. Only a name. Letters don't arrive like that, I think. But he seems to write anyway.
city.home.okada.paintings.1: The big picture over the sofa looks like blotches from a distance. Close up you see it: sunsets, layered one over another, hundreds of them.
city.home.okada.paintings.2: In the corner a signature and a date, then another, and another. He adds to this picture every year. The latest date isn't there yet.
city.home.okada.paintings.3: Beside it, a small portrait of a woman turned away towards a window. No face, only light on her cheek. I think he chose not to turn her round.
city.home.okada.paintings.4: The pictures hang so close together you can hardly see the wallpaper. The room is like a window looking every way at once.
city.home.okada.poetry.1: A book of poems bristling with paper strips. On each, a scrap of sky painted the colour that was in the line.
city.home.okada.poetry.2: Underlined: "I look out of the same window, and it is different every time." Next to it: "Yes."
city.home.okada.poetry.3: An inscription on the flyleaf: "For Lyova, so you remember that words are paint too. Asya." Is it the same hand as the letter on the table?
city.home.okada.record.1: A cello record on the player. One side is worn down: it's been played so often that the other side is still like new.
city.home.okada.record.2: Slow music, like paint drying. The right music for painting the same window a thousand times, I suppose.
city.home.okada.record.3: On the sleeve, a fingerprint in blue paint. And yellow. And more yellow.
city.home.okafor.bed.1: The bed under the shelves, hastily made. Headphones on the pillow: he falls asleep on the air, it seems.
city.home.okafor.bed.2: Over the bed on a nail, an old striped sailor's scarf. The radio man went to sea once too, it seems.
city.home.okafor.bed.3: Someone else's bed, someone else's headphones. I put them on for a second: silence. Put them back as they were.
city.home.okafor.manuals.1: The transmitter's manual, rebound. On the last page: "If nothing helps, switch off and look out of the window."
city.home.okafor.manuals.2: A frequency directory full of bookmarks. One frequency has been ringed so often the paper's worn through: 7055.
city.home.okafor.manuals.3: A Morse primer for children. On the flyleaf, a sun and three dots, three dashes, three dots. Underneath: "That's not SOS. That's 'I'm here.'"
city.home.okafor.map.1: A world map with threads running from Lyudmilovsk in every direction. The shortest thread goes to the next street, to the capsule tower.
city.home.okafor.map.2: In the map's margin: "Tiksi, snow. Valparaíso, heat. Capsule, tea with jam." The important things, it seems, you discuss with the ones nearby.
city.home.okafor.map.3: Pinned in the corner of the map, a photo of two aerials at sunset, taken from a roof. Caption: "Us. 1 km."
city.home.okafor.music.1: A shelf of record sleeves sorted by weather: "For rain", "For wind", "For sun". The last section is the thickest.
city.home.okafor.music.2: On the shelf I found a sleeve with a trumpeter on a promenade. The very tune, third on side two. I pencilled the title onto the reel, small, next to "unknown".
city.home.okafor.music.3: A songbook with chords. On the lullaby page: "Played it on air for Ilmar when he had the flu."
city.home.okafor.radio.1: I sat down at someone else's transmitter and pressed the key. An answer came at once: "Capsule here. Ilmar's at his post. Says he saw the sunset, and yes, it was green."
city.home.okafor.radio.2: On the desk, a microphone wrapped in insulating tape and a sign: "Lyudmilovsk-11. On air, be polite." I said "hello" into the microphone very politely.
city.home.okafor.radio.3: Two receivers side by side tuned to the same frequency. One for listening, the other "in case the first one starts daydreaming".
city.home.okafor.radio.4: The contact log lies open. Last entry: "23:00. Capsule. Talked about the weather for forty minutes. Good talk."
city.home.okafor.records.1: A reel on the tape recorder labelled: "Off air, 14 May. Music unknown. Didn't hear the end: static at three minutes."
city.home.okafor.records.2: I pressed play. Through the hiss, a simple tune on a trumpet, sad and cheerful at once. At three minutes the crackle swallows it like a wave swallowing sand.
city.home.okafor.records.3: Beside it, boxes of reels, each with a date and the weather: "Rain. Chopin." "Fog. Unknown waltz." "Clear. Silence, a good one."
city.home.okafor.records.4: The newest reel is labelled in fresh pencil: "The tune from 14 May: the Saucer café, the jukebox, third button. Found it!" Not his handwriting. Mine? No. But it looks like it.
city.home.okafor.shelf_radio.1: Twenty years of a radio magazine, bound. Numbers on the spines, not a single issue missing.
city.home.okafor.shelf_radio.2: A diagram of a home-made aerial; on the back, a plan of the kitchen in the same hand: "Fridge here, aerial there, kitchen later."
city.home.okafor.shelf_radio.3: Between the books, a QSL card with a steamer: "MV Ladoga confirms contact. The navigator sends regards to the radio operator." An old date.
city.home.okonkwo.abstract.1: An abstract made of clay shards glued onto a board. Title: "Everything that broke this year. No regrets."
city.home.okonkwo.abstract.2: The shards are laid in a circle from dark to light. In the centre, a yellow one from a broken cup. Like a sun made of fragments.
city.home.okonkwo.abstract.3: One shard is labelled: "E. broke it, E. owned up." It's glued right in the middle, in the place of honour.
city.home.okonkwo.art.1: A book, "Ceramics for Beginners", covered in clay fingerprints. Two sizes.
city.home.okonkwo.art.2: A children's encyclopaedia, "Whales and Dolphins". A sweet wrapper for a bookmark. On that page a whale spouts, and the spout is ringed: "Like this."
city.home.okonkwo.art.3: An exercise book of glaze recipes. The last one is headed: "Sunny. Don't try it before M. gets back."
city.home.okonkwo.blank.1: A smaller easel, a child's. A blank sheet on it and a sign: "Emiliano's easel. Grown-ups may only look."
city.home.okonkwo.blank.2: The sheet is blank, but in the corner, faintly, in pencil: "Papa goes here. When he comes home I'll draw him from life."
city.home.okonkwo.blank.3: Am I a grown-up? Not very, probably. But I only looked anyway.
city.home.okonkwo.daybed.1: The divan is heaped with cushions, and a plush whale is hidden under them. Well hidden: only the tail sticks out.
city.home.okonkwo.daybed.2: A clay-stained apron folded on the divan. It isn't washed, "so it smells of the studio", as the tag says.
city.home.okonkwo.daybed.3: Someone else's divan in someone else's studio. I didn't sit: somehow there's clay on my shoes already.
city.home.okonkwo.drafting.1: Sketches of vases with measurements and notes: "Wall 6 mm. Glaze: the colour of the sea in October." Everyone here knows that colour, it seems.
city.home.okonkwo.drafting.2: Beside them, a used one-way train ticket. On the back: "Two weeks. 14 days. 336 hours. Counting."
city.home.okonkwo.drafting.3: A pencil sketch: a whale with two tails. Underneath, in a grown-up's hand: "All right. Two it is."
city.home.okonkwo.dunes.1: Dunes painted fast with a broad brush. Underneath: "Seen from the train window. Our train doesn't go there. Pity."
city.home.okonkwo.dunes.2: The sand on the canvas is real: mixed into the paint. Run a finger over it and it rustles faintly.
city.home.okonkwo.dunes.3: The picture isn't finished, but someone has already drawn a tiny whale in the corner, swimming through the sand.
city.home.okonkwo.exhibit.1: A board with a calendar, days crossed off, and children's drawings: Papa on a ship, Papa on a train, Papa waving from a tiny window.
city.home.okonkwo.exhibit.2: The coming Saturday is ringed in red and labelled "Whale". Under it, in a grown-up's hand: "We'll fire it together. I promise. M."
city.home.okonkwo.exhibit.3: In the corner of the board, a photo: a boy and a man in aprons, both covered in clay, both laughing and looking at the sun.
city.home.okonkwo.pines.1: Pines on a cliff, and at their roots clay pots painted in great detail. Someone here loves pots more than pines.
city.home.okonkwo.pines.2: At the bottom, a child's addition in felt-tip: "A hedgehog lives here." No hedgehog to be seen. But I believe him.
city.home.okonkwo.pines.3: The frame is made from offcuts of board and painted blue. The frame and the picture are clearly the work of different hands, and different years.
city.home.okonkwo.portrait.1: A portrait of a woman with scissors in her hand and a craftsman's squint. Caption: "Yasmin at work. Don't move or she'll cut your hair."
city.home.okonkwo.portrait.2: The portrait is clumsily painted but very like her. Painted not by an artist, it seems, but by someone who'd looked for a long time.
city.home.okonkwo.portrait.3: A note on the frame: "Yas, I'm off for two weeks. The whale's on the wheel. Don't let Emiliano give it a second tail."
city.home.okonkwo.record.1: A record of children's songs about animals, and right next to it a record of jazz trumpet. They take turns, it seems.
city.home.okonkwo.record.2: I dropped the needle. A little song about a whale looking for its home. The whale finds it at the very end, and that's good.
city.home.okonkwo.record.3: A note on the sleeve in Yasmin's hand: "Play when you miss Papa. But not more than three times a day: the neighbours."
city.home.okonkwo.wheel.1: On the potter's wheel, a half-dry bowl and a note in a child's scrawl: "Papa, this is a whale. Fire it when you come home. E."
city.home.okonkwo.wheel.2: The whale looks more like a bowl with a tail. But the tail has been shaped with great care: you can see the prints of small fingers.
city.home.okonkwo.wheel.3: On the shelf beside it, a row of fired animals: a tortoise, a horse, something with wings. Each dated: weekends, two weeks out of three.
city.home.okonkwo.wheel.4: The wheel is covered with a damp cloth so the clay won't dry out. Someone wets it every morning. Mum, probably.
city.home.santos.birds.1: A poster, "Birds of Our Coast". A tick and a date beside each bird. Beside the cormorant: "Saw it! Timo." Beside the albatross: "Not yet."
city.home.santos.birds.2: In the corner of the poster, a bird that isn't in any atlas: yellow, with rays instead of feathers. Caption: "Sun bird. Saw it in a dream."
city.home.santos.birds.3: Under the poster on the sill, a feeder made from a milk carton and a note: "Tits in the mornings. Sparrows whenever they like."
city.home.santos.board.1: The kitchen board: "Chores. Dishes, Lina. Bins, Timo. Noel, smiling. Dad, everything else."
city.home.santos.board.2: Below, in big letters: "CONTEST! First to see Venus gets a week off the dishes. Telescope in the loft. Mum is the judge."
city.home.santos.board.3: Two entries under the notice. Lina: "Saw it! (probably)". Timo: "That was the lighthouse lamp." Mum: "Neither counts."
city.home.santos.board.4: A note held to the board by a magnet: "Vera, I'm at work till seven. Soup in the pan, sun on the windowsill. E."
city.home.santos.books.1: The children's shelf: fairy tales, an animal atlas and a fat book, "How Everything Works". Its bookmark is at the chapter "Why the Sun Shines".
city.home.santos.books.2: A name sticker on every spine: "Lina", "Timo", "Lina", "Lina", "Noel (to grow into)".
city.home.santos.books.3: A home-made bookmark falls out of the fairy tales: a sun cut from foil and "Timo, give me my book back. L."
city.home.santos.bunk.1: A bunk bed. On the top bunk a star map is pinned to the wall; on the bottom, a football pennant. No need to argue who sleeps where.
city.home.santos.bunk.2: A torch sticks out from under the bottom bunk's pillow. Pirate stories at night, I'd guess.
city.home.santos.bunk.3: The ladder to the top bunk is wrapped in tape in three places. "Timo fell here", "and here", "and here too."
city.home.santos.chess.1: A chess table in the loft. An odd position: White has three queens. A note beside it: "Dad, that's not fair, I made up the rules!"
city.home.santos.chess.2: Under the board an exercise book: "Games with Timo". Score: Dad 41, Timo 3. Timo's three wins are framed with little suns.
city.home.santos.chess.3: The black king is wrapped in a sweet wrapper. Labelled: "The king is ill, under treatment." The game is adjourned until he's better, it seems.
city.home.santos.cot.1: A baby's cot with rattles. Over it a mobile: a sun, a moon and three clouds turning slowly in the draught.
city.home.santos.cot.2: A plush rabbit asleep in the cot, tucked in up to its ears. No Noel: out for a walk with Mum, probably.
city.home.santos.cot.3: I adjusted the mobile so the sun was on top. Then I thought they might have hung it lower on purpose, and put it back.
city.home.santos.desk.1: Lina's nature-study book: "Planets. Venus is the brightest star, though it isn't a star. Seen in the west after sunset."
city.home.santos.desk.2: I sat at the children's desk and pencilled into the corner of the book: "Venus: in the west, right after sunset, over the lighthouse. Checked." Let someone else do the dishes.
city.home.santos.desk.3: In Timo's maths book, between sums, a ship with cannons. The cannons fire numbers. The teacher gave a 4 and added: "Ship: 5."
city.home.santos.desk.4: A lamp, a glass of pencils and a stone with a hole through it, a "hag stone". Through the hole, they say, you see what can't be seen. I looked: I saw the window.
city.home.santos.map.1: A world map on the slope of the roof. Flags mark where they've been: Lyudmilovsk, Lyudmilovsk, Lyudmilovsk. And one flag in the ocean: "Someday."
city.home.santos.map.2: A thread runs along the equator with a paper sun on it. You can slide it: right now it's over us. Someone moves it every day.
city.home.santos.map.3: By Antarctica, in a child's hand: "Penguins and frost here, Mum says we're not going." Beside it, in Dad's: "We'll see."
city.home.santos.parents_bed.1: The parents' bed has a sunflower bedspread. On one pillow a book, on the other a child's sock.
city.home.santos.parents_bed.2: Over the bed, a wedding photo: the couple squinting at the sun, and behind them this very street, the trees still small.
city.home.santos.parents_bed.3: Someone else's bedroom. I looked in and left at once, but I noticed: the alarm is set for six, and a note beside it says "Oh please, half past six."
city.home.santos.science.1: Dad's shelf: "Astronomy for Fun", "The Amateur's Star Atlas", and between them a children's book, "Why the Moon Follows Us".
city.home.santos.science.2: In the star atlas, on the Venus page, a bookmark: a child's drawing of Venus in a crown, captioned "Queen of the Evening".
city.home.santos.science.3: On the last page of "Astronomy for Fun", in Dad's hand: "Explain to the kids that the Sun is a star too. Explain to myself why that still surprises me."
city.home.santos.sea.1: A calm sea in the picture, and on the shore five tiny figures of different heights. The smallest is in the arms of the tallest.
city.home.santos.sea.2: Signed in the corner: "Our first day by the sea. Painted from memory a year later. It seems sunnier than it was."
city.home.santos.sea.3: The frame is studded with shells. One was clearly glued on recently, upside down. Timo's work, without a doubt.
city.home.santos.sewing.1: Under the sewing machine's needle, a little sun costume in yellow felt, with rays. One ray is missing.
city.home.santos.sewing.2: Beside it, a pattern labelled: "Timo, the sun, school show on Saturday. Lina, a raincloud (not pleased)."
city.home.santos.sewing.3: The needle has stopped in the middle of a seam. The thread is still taut. Mum stepped away for a second, and the second stretched.
city.home.santos.telescope.1: A small telescope on a tripod, pointing out of the dormer window to the west. A slip of paper on the tube: "NEVER at the sun! Only Venus."
city.home.santos.telescope.2: I looked through the eyepiece. Over the lighthouse, low down, a bright white point is shining, steady, not flickering. Not the lamp. It's her.
city.home.santos.telescope.3: In daytime the eyepiece shows only sky and the edge of the lighthouse gallery. Blue on blue, like looking into very deep water.
city.home.santos.telescope.4: Scratched into the tripod: "E. + V." The telescope is older than the children, it seems.
city.home.santos.wardrobe.1: A poster on the wardrobe: "A Schoolchild's Daily Routine". The line "Get up: 7:00" is crossed out. Above it: "When the sun reaches the wardrobe."
city.home.santos.wardrobe.2: Pencil height marks on the wardrobe door: "Lina 9", "Lina 10", "Timo 7"... and one very low: "Noel, lying down."
city.home.santos.wardrobe.3: A sleeve of Mum's polka-dot dress sticks out of the wardrobe, and a sleeve of Dad's checked shirt. As if they were holding hands.

city.home.singh.bed.1: A narrow bed under the round window. The pillow is at the foot end, so as to fall asleep looking at the sky.
city.home.singh.bed.2: Under the bed, a box of transmitter valves, each wrapped in newspaper like a Christmas ornament.
city.home.singh.bed.3: An alarm clock on the bedside table set for 22:55. The caretaker gets up at night for the air like for a shift.
city.home.singh.map.1: A world map full of pins with coloured flags. Hundreds of them, on every continent. The most worn one is right here in Lyudmilovsk, in the next block.
city.home.singh.map.2: QSL cards pinned beside it. One from Lyudmilovsk-11 came by post, stamped: "Contact confirmed. Reception excellent. Distance: 1 km."
city.home.singh.map.3: A letter on the wall, no envelope: "Ilmar, let's meet at last. The Saucer café, Saturday." Below, an answer in pencil: "But what will we talk about with no static?"
city.home.singh.radio.1: The set is on, the valves warm. A note on the desk: "If I'm on my rounds, listen on 7055 for me. Gunnar comes on at 23:00. Tell him I'm here."
city.home.singh.radio.2: Crackle in the headphones, then a calm voice: "...Lyudmilovsk-11 calling the capsule. Ilmar, you there? The sunset was green tonight, did you see?"
city.home.singh.radio.3: Over the desk, a contact log. Thousands of entries, and nearly all one call sign: Lyudmilovsk-11. A kilometre lies between them. They've never met.
city.home.singh.radio.4: The Morse in the headphones sounds like dripping water. I don't know the code, but I think I understood one word: it repeats like "hello".
city.home.singh.records.1: A record of surf sounds "for sleep". A note on the sleeve: "Doesn't work. The air works."
city.home.singh.records.2: I dropped the needle. An old station's call signal, a waltz and an announcer's voice. The caretaker listens to radio even on records, it seems.
city.home.singh.records.3: A stack of records tied with string and a tag: "For Gunnar. To give when we meet." The tag is old. The meeting hasn't happened, it seems.
city.home.singh.shelf.1: "The Shortwave Operator's Handbook", read to pieces. The page with the day-and-night propagation chart is covered in pencil marks.
city.home.singh.shelf.2: Among the technical books, an exercise book headed "Rounds": "3rd floor, bulb. 7th, door creaks. 11th, someone crying; left a chocolate bar by the door."
city.home.singh.shelf.3: A pamphlet, "Why radio waves travel better at night". The answer is underlined: "In daytime the sun interferes." A note beside it: "It doesn't interfere. It's talking too."
city.home.singh.window.1: Through the round window, a piece of street and a piece of sky. Just enough not to get bored.
city.home.singh.window.2: On the inside of the glass, a pencil mark and a note: "The sun sets here on midsummer's day."
city.home.singh.window.3: From the window you can see an aerial on the roof of a distant building. Probably the one at the other end of the line.
