city.home.tadesse.abstract.1: An abstract: blue circles and one yellow. The title on the label: "The aquarium at night, when the light was switched on."
city.home.tadesse.abstract.2: From the door the blue circles turn into fish and the yellow into the lamp. Or the sun, if you squint.
city.home.tadesse.abstract.3: A price in pencil on the frame, crossed out. Below: "Not for sale. H. won't allow it."
city.home.tadesse.aquarium.1: A big aquarium in the corner of the studio, and all round it on the walls the same fish, painted. There are more painted ones than live ones.
city.home.tadesse.aquarium.2: A list of names in chalk on the glass: "Hamlet, Ophelia, Captain, Friday..." Fifty-four names. I counted eight fish. The rest live in the paintings, I suppose.
city.home.tadesse.aquarium.3: A note by the feeding dish: "Valya, the food's in the blue tin, not the yellow. The yellow one's for me: sweets. H."
city.home.tadesse.aquarium.4: A fish with a golden flank swam up to the glass and looked at me. In the painting over the tank it's the same fish, only younger, and wearing a hat.
city.home.tadesse.art.1: An album of Dutch still lifes, open at a fish on a platter. In the margin: "Poor thing. Mine would be swimming."
city.home.tadesse.art.2: A textbook, "How to Paint Water". Underlined: "You don't paint water; you paint the light on it."
city.home.tadesse.art.3: An exercise book with scraps of coloured paper pasted in: "The colour of the sea at 7 a.m., noon, 8 p.m." Each with a date and a tiny sun.
city.home.tadesse.blank.1: A blank canvas, primed long ago: the ground has yellowed. On the side of the stretcher: "For the sun. When I dare."
city.home.tadesse.blank.2: Before the canvas on a stool, a brush that has never been dipped in paint. It's lain here so long there's dust on it.
city.home.tadesse.blank.3: If you stand where she would, you see it: the hexagonal window faces due south. In the morning the sun falls right on this canvas. It's almost painted already.
city.home.tadesse.daybed.1: A daybed behind a screen, a rug and two cushions on it: one embroidered with a fish, the other with a fishing rod.
city.home.tadesse.daybed.2: The grandchild's drawings pinned on the screen: fish with legs, fish in hats, a fish holding the sun. The last one is framed.
city.home.tadesse.daybed.3: It's their daybed, not mine. I only straightened the rug where it had slipped and backed quietly away.
city.home.tadesse.drafting.1: Life-size sketches of fish on the drawing table, labelled: "Hamlet, full face. Hamlet, profile. Hamlet, offended."
city.home.tadesse.drafting.2: Under the sketches, a squared sheet: a shopping list in Hamish's hand. "Bread. Fish food. Ultramarine (don't forget!!). Flowers, just because."
city.home.tadesse.drafting.3: The pencils are sharpened with a knife, stubby, a centimetre each. She can't bring herself to throw them out: every one has drawn something.
city.home.tadesse.dunes.1: Sand dunes, endless and pale, and a thin path that breaks off in the middle of the canvas. "The Mires. From memory. You can't paint them from life: your eyes won't hold."
city.home.tadesse.dunes.2: Look long enough and the dunes seem to creep slowly from place to place. I blinked: they were still. Blinked again: I'm not so sure.
city.home.tadesse.dunes.3: At the very bottom, almost on the frame, a strip of blue light. A river? Next to it, small: "Saw it once. At night. Never went back."
city.home.tadesse.exhibit.1: A board of exhibition posters spanning half a century: "V. Tadesse: Fish." "V. Tadesse: Fish and the Sea." "V. Tadesse: Fish Again."
city.home.tadesse.exhibit.2: Among the posters, a postcard from a granddaughter: "Granny, paint the sun! It's all fish, fish, fish with you." No reply on the card. Maybe the reply is the empty easel.
city.home.tadesse.exhibit.3: A newspaper cutting: "The artist claims fish pose better than people: 'They never ask if it's a good likeness.'"
city.home.tadesse.pines.1: Pines on a cliff, the wind bending them all one way. The trunks are painted so you can hear them creak.
city.home.tadesse.pines.2: On the back of the stretcher: "Painted while H. was fishing. He caught one fish; I caught the pines. Score in my favour."
city.home.tadesse.pines.3: Between the pines, a tiny figure with a fishing rod. You can hardly see it. But it was painted first: the paint is thickest under it.
city.home.tadesse.portrait.1: A portrait of a young man with a fishing rod and a smile as if a fish had just bitten. Signed: "Hamish. First date. Nothing was biting."
city.home.tadesse.portrait.2: The paint is rubbed thin in places, as if someone had stroked his cheek with a hand. For many years.
city.home.tadesse.portrait.3: Upstairs someone is walking about and humming. The same man as in the portrait, fifty years on. I stepped away quickly.
city.home.tadesse.record.1: A record of fishermen's songs. Theirs together, clearly: on the sleeve two hands argue over which song is best.
city.home.tadesse.record.2: I dropped the needle. A choir sings about a boat that will be back for supper. The aquarium bubbles almost in time.
city.home.tadesse.record.3: A note on the player: "Not loud: H. naps after lunch. Quietly is fine; he likes to fall asleep to this one."
city.home.tape.prompt: E — switch on the tape recorder
city.home.wheel.prompt: E — look at the potter's wheel
city.look.birds.1: A poster, "Feed the birds!": a tit, a bullfinch, a nuthatch. Below: "Bird guide at the town library, feed on the first floor, Garden department."
city.look.birds.2: A chart, "What to offer": unsalted suet for tits, rowan for bullfinches, and for sparrows anything not nailed down.
city.look.birds.3: A photo: a grey-haired man in glasses holding a tiny bird on his palm, both very serious. Caption: "Ornithologist. Our town."
city.look.birds.4: How to make a feeder from a kefir carton, in six pictures. In the sixth a bird is already sitting there looking at you reproachfully: where's the food?
city.look.catalogue.1: I pulled out the catalogue drawer for S. Cards: "Steamers", "Sand", "Seabirds", "Sea, see also Memory".
city.look.catalogue.2: A handwritten card: "The book everyone's looking for. Shelf mark: none. Location: with whoever is reading it."
city.look.catalogue.3: In the drawer for S there are more cards on the sun than on anything else. The drawer won't shut properly.
city.look.catalogue.4: A card marked "On loan" has been in the catalogue for twenty years. To whom isn't written.
city.look.catalogue.5: The drawers smell of glue and wood. Run a finger along the cards and they rustle like dry grass in the northern meadows.
city.look.cinema.1: A poster: The Man Who Waited for the Lighthouse. Drama. A grey fisherman and a huge yellow beam that looks right at you.
city.look.cinema.2: "Children's show: The Hedgehog's Cable Car Adventure. Sundays at 11:00. Under sixes with a parent or a hedgehog."
city.look.cinema.3: The comedy "Unpaid Leave": on the poster a holidaymaker chases his flying hat across the whole town.
city.look.cinema.4: "Before the film, a science reel: 'The Sun Is Our Home'." Someone added underneath: "And we're the guests."
city.look.cinema.5: The week's programme: the same film every day. Under the table: "By popular demand."
city.look.club.1: "Amateur photography circle. Thursday, 18:00. Bring film and a good mood. Film is a must."
city.look.club.2: "Dances for the over… for anyone. Saturday, 19:00. Waltz, foxtrot, slow ones on request."
city.look.club.3: "Chess tournament. The winner gets a cup, the losers get tea. The tea's better, we've checked."
city.look.club.4: "The choir needs basses. No tenors, please: our tenors already sing for everyone."
city.look.club.5: "Lecture: 'Why do we love the sun?' Free entry. Questions from the floor welcome; answers not guaranteed."
city.look.exhibit.1: A plaque: "Anchor of the schooner Lyudmila, 18—. Found by divers in 19—. The schooner itself has never been found."
city.look.exhibit.2: "Model of the first cable car cabin, scale 1:10." Inside sits a tiny passenger with a newspaper.
city.look.exhibit.3: A case of amber. In one piece a mosquito is frozen, looking as if it's about to say something.
city.look.exhibit.4: "Sundial from the old Sun Square. The shadow tells the time to the nearest quarter hour, and mood."
city.look.exhibit.5: Trophies of the Surf sports society. The smallest is engraved: "For the will to win. Nearly won."
city.look.fair.1: "Wave Fair: carousel, shooting gallery, ice cream, a lottery where nobody loses. Fri–Sun, noon till dark." "Till dark" is underlined.
city.look.fair.2: A notice: "Found: a child's sandal, the right one. Left one, where are you?"
city.look.fair.3: A hand-painted poster: dancing under the canopy on Saturday night, "in any weather except a hurricane".
city.look.fair.4: Carousel rules: "Hold the horse's neck, not your neighbour. Feeling dizzy? See the ice-cream lady, she knows a cure."
city.look.garden.1: Seedlings on the table in sour-cream pots. Each is labelled: "Tomato, Ox Heart. Don't water on Tuesdays."
city.look.garden.2: Seed packets: asters, dill, "early radish". The pictures are so lovely the vegetable patch will be ashamed.
city.look.garden.3: The rubber plant in the tub has outlived three directors. It has its own sign: "Don't touch. Old-timer."
city.look.garden.4: A long-spouted watering can, a rake, a ball of twine. It smells of earth and of something about to grow.
city.look.health.1: A poster: "Wash your hands before meals!" The drawn boy washes them with such joy you'd think it was the sea.
city.look.health.2: "Sunbathing: no more than 20 minutes. The sun isn't going anywhere, but you'll burn."
city.look.health.3: "A holidaymaker's day": rise, exercises, breakfast, sea, lunch, quiet hour, sea, supper, sea, sleep.
city.look.health.4: A chart: "How to breathe sea air properly." In on a count of four, out on the count of a wave.
city.look.health.5: "Vaccinations on Wednesdays. Crying is permitted any day."
city.look.kids.1: In the window, a doll's house with a wall that opens. In the kitchen a doll is frying a button. Smells good, probably.
city.look.kids.2: A wind-up chick on the counter pecks at the glass. Its key is lost, so it pecks forever.
city.look.kids.3: A "Young Chemist" set, stickered "Temporarily not for sale" after the business with the neighbour's cat.
city.look.kids.4: A wooden rocking horse with a real mane. I'd have a go if nobody were looking. Somebody's looking.
city.look.local.1: Under the glass: "Lyudmilovsk 900 years" badges, shells saying "Greetings from the sea!" and a stone that looks like an admiral's head.
city.look.local.2: An old photo of the promenade: ladies with parasols, a boy with a hoop, and the same lighthouse, only younger.
city.look.local.3: A hand-drawn map of the town. In the north, at the edge: "Meadows. Beyond: the mountains' smoke." In the west: "The Mires. Don't go."
city.look.local.4: A drop of amber with a gnat inside that didn't make it anywhere forty million years ago. It probably wanted to get to the sea too.
city.look.logbook.1: The lighthouse log: "02:10. Light normal. Fog. Heard a horn, answered." The handwriting is as even as the surf.
city.look.logbook.2: "Clear night. The freighter Akademik passed, blinked. Blinked back." And underneath: "I miss you."
city.look.logbook.3: Every page starts with the weather and ends with one word: "Shone." Thirty years in a row.
city.look.logbook.4: A pencilled entry: "An owl spent the night on the gallery. Flew north at dawn. Light normal." The owl got logged too.
city.look.lost.1: "Found: horn-rimmed glasses. Good eyesight. Ask at the cloakroom."
city.look.lost.2: "Lost: Barsik the cat, ginger, answers to a rustling bag. Finder gets eternal gratitude and pies."
city.look.lost.3: "Whoever took my striped deckchair from the beach, please bring it back: it remembers my back."
city.look.lost.4: "Found: a key on a blue ribbon. What it opens is unknown. Possibly something important."
city.look.lost.5: "Lost: the feeling that everything is still ahead. If found, keep it, you need it more." Unsigned.
city.look.medicine.1: The teaching skeleton in the corner is holding someone's forgotten mitten. Just in case, apparently.
city.look.medicine.2: A poster, "Structure of the ear". The ear is drawn so huge it seems to be eavesdropping right now.
city.look.medicine.3: Someone has put a sun hat on the skeleton. The nurse has been pretending not to notice for two weeks.
city.look.medicine.4: A chart, "The 206 bones of the human body". So far I've found about twenty on myself. The rest must be somewhere inside.
city.look.misc.1: Notices pasted one over another like layers of paint. The bottom one has gone the colour of tea.
city.look.misc.2: "Whoever found a blue umbrella: it means a lot to me. Ask for Tamara Ilyinichna."
city.look.misc.3: The drawing pins are all colours, and one is shaped like a little sun. Nobody seems to touch that one.
city.look.misc.4: I read everything, down to "Notices are kept for 10 days." This one's been up about ten years.
city.look.painting.1: A painting, "Morning on the Pier": fishermen, gulls, mist. In the corner a boy in a hood is looking not at the sea but straight at me.
city.look.painting.2: A still life: a watermelon, a knife, tea in a glass holder. The tea is painted so you can see it going cold.
city.look.painting.3: A huge panel: people reach their hands towards the sun, and the sun reaches back. The fingers almost touch.
city.look.painting.4: A watercolour, "The Northern Meadows". The grass is a single brushstroke, and it seems to sway in the wind right now.
city.look.painting.5: A portrait of a woman in blue. The label: "Unknown artist. Unknown sitter. Very familiar."
city.look.prices.1: "Apples 5 rub., corn 14, seeds 9. The seller's smile free, but not always in stock."
city.look.prices.2: In chalk on a board: "Adyghe cheese. Fresh. Yesterday's is fresh too, just less so."
city.look.prices.3: "Check scales. Weigh your purchase!" Beside it, old scales with weights; one weight has a chipped edge.
city.look.prices.4: "Fish bought from the public from 6 to 9 a.m. Fish with stories, any time."
city.look.prices.5: Market rules: "Trading until 18:00. After 18:00, conversation only."
city.look.rules.1: "Library rules. 1: Keep quiet. 2: Especially in the capsules. 3: Whispering counts as quiet."
city.look.rules.2: "Books are lent for 14 days. Poetry for as long as you need."
city.look.rules.3: "Don't fold the corners of pages. That's what bookmarks, memory and the librarian are for."
city.look.rules.4: "A library card is issued on showing a passport or an honest face."
city.look.rules.5: "Taking books out of the reading room is forbidden. Taking thoughts out is encouraged."
city.look.store.1: Store directory: "Ground floor: grocery, confectionery, haberdashery, drinks. First floor: books, sports, garden, souvenirs. Second floor: none."
city.look.store.2: "Dear customers! First choose, then pay at the till, then collect. The order matters, as in life."
city.look.store.3: "The complaints and suggestions book is kept by the manager." Below, in small print: "There are more suggestions."
city.look.store.4: "Fresh bread delivered at 9:00 and 16:00. Pies when you're lucky."
city.look.store.5: A poster, "Summer Is Holiday Time!": a family with a rubber ring and a ball. The dad is very tanned and the mum very happy.
city.look.sun.1: The roof solarium: deckchairs, striped awnings and a sign: "Sunbathe no longer than 15 minutes. Our sun is strong."
city.look.sun.2: A sundial on the parapet. The shadow says almost the same as my watch. One of us is right.
city.look.sun.3: I squint into the sun. Through my eyelids everything is red and warm, like looking out from inside an orange.
city.look.sun.4: Someone has chalked a circle on the concrete: "Here the sun stands at noon on 22 June." I stood in the circle. Nothing happened. Yet.
city.look.timetable.1: "Bus No. 3: Promenade, School, Sanatorium. Every 20 minutes, or however it works out."
city.look.timetable.2: Cable car times: first cabin 6:00, last 23:40. Added underneath: "The last one is for those in no hurry to get home."
city.look.timetable.3: A week's tide table. Someone crossed out Thursday and wrote: "On Thursdays the sea rests."
city.look.timetable.4: The local train "to the Northern Meadows" leaves on Saturdays at 7:15. A dry blade of grass is pinned beside it.
city.look.timetable.5: Opening hours for the bathhouse, the post office and the lighthouse. For the lighthouse: "Always. Especially at night."
city.look.travel.1: A world map with pins: red for "been", blue for "want to". Three times as many blue. One is stuck right in the sea.
city.look.travel.2: A cable-car diagram. From our station a thin line is drawn north to the volcanoes, marked "someday".
city.look.travel.3: A sea chart with depths. The figures are tiny as poppy seeds. The deepest spot is circled and labelled: "Quiet."
city.look.travel.4: A route drawn in pencil: from the door to the sea, from the sea to the mountains, from the mountains "home, but another way".
city.look.view.1: The sea is striped today: turquoise by the shore, blue further out, nearly silver at the horizon.
city.look.view.2: Down below a tiny bus crawls along the promenade, and above it a cable car cabin, as if they were racing.
city.look.view.3: To the north, beyond the roofs, the mountains go blue, and on one summit lies a patch of snow. In summer. Strange and beautiful.
city.look.view.4: West of town the sand rolls away in waves to the edge of the world. Somehow I can't look that way for long.
city.look.view.5: The sun lies on the water in a path straight to me. Wherever I stand, the path turns to follow.
city.look.wallpaper.1: The school wall newspaper: class 7B on cleaning the beach and finding a message in a bottle. The note is in a foreign language.
city.look.wallpaper.2: "Our Top Pupils": the photos smile; one boy has his eyes shut. Underneath: "Blinked at the crucial moment."
city.look.wallpaper.3: A poem by a girl in 5A: "The sun sits down in the sea / as if in a warm bath. / Tomorrow it'll wake up early / all rosy and laughing."
city.look.wallpaper.4: A cartoon: the physics teacher as a pendulum. Caption: "Wavers, but holds on." They say the teacher liked it.
city.look.wallpaper.5: From the pupils' council: "Waste paper drive. The heaviest class gets a cake. Don't hand in encyclopaedias, it's a shame."
city.night.binoculars.1: At night the binoculars show little: black water, white crests and the buoys glowing green.
city.night.binoculars.2: Something dark drifts along the moon's path. A log, probably. Or a very calm seal.
city.night.binoculars.3: Far out a ship's lights are burning: red, green, white. As if it were looking out for someone too.
city.night.binoculars.4: On the empty beach someone sits right by the water, not moving. I lowered the binoculars: let them be.
city.night.telescope.1: The coin clinked and the eyepiece filled with stars. So many, as if someone had spilled salt on a black tablecloth.
city.night.telescope.2: I found the Moon. You can see the craters and one long bright streak, like a scratch on a record.
city.night.telescope.3: I aimed it at the sea. Dark, only a barge's light rocking, and the lighthouse sweeping its beam right across the glass.
city.night.telescope.4: To the north, over the mountains, something glows faintly red. Maybe the volcano isn't asleep. Maybe I imagined it.
city.night.telescope.5: A satellite! A steady dot crawling between the stars, not blinking. I followed it until my time ran out.
city.night.view.1: At night, from up here, the town is a handful of lights by dark water. A red lamp blinks on the boiler-house chimney.
city.night.view.2: The cable-car cabins hang dark; only the last one has a lit window. Someone in no hurry to get home.
city.night.view.3: The lighthouse turns its beam, and each time the beach steps out of the dark for a second, like a photograph.
city.night.view.4: So many stars over the sea that there's no horizon: where the water ends, the sky begins.
city.night.view.5: In the west, beyond the sands, something glows quietly in the dark. Not a town, not the moon. I looked that way for a long time.

city.ps.booth.am: Early on the booth is quiet. The assistant puts on the first record that comes to hand: someone sings about the sea as softly as one sings in an empty hall. It ends and I keep standing there.
city.ps.booth.any.1: The sleeves stand slanted in the crate like teeth in a smile. I chose by the cover: it had a lighthouse. It played one about a lighthouse. A coincidence, of course.
city.ps.booth.any.2: The booth is lined in blue and the voice from the speaker comes closer, as if the singer stood at my shoulder. I didn't turn round: what if he does.
city.ps.booth.eve: By evening the booth is warmer: the music has warmed the walls. Something lazy and jazzy plays. Beyond the glass people head home, and I somehow don't.
city.ps.booth.noon: After lunch the booth is crowded with other people's thoughts: someone's fingerprints on the sleeve. The needle settles into the groove, a waltz plays. I don't know it, yet somehow I remember it.
city.ps.chalk.fri.1: "FRIDAY IS FISH AND CHEESE DELIVERY. Buy at once or they'll say it's gone. The fish is at the grocery counter, the smell is everywhere."
city.ps.chalk.fri.2: Under it someone has chalked: "Cheese first, fish as you feel." The assistant leaves it up: she says it's good advice.
city.ps.chalk.mid: "WEDNESDAY AND THURSDAY are the quietest days. Choose in your own time; the shop assistants don't bite, and if they do, they do it politely."
city.ps.chalk.mon: In chalk on the board: "MONDAY IS STOCKTAKING. If you can't find it, it isn't missing, it's accounted for."
city.ps.chalk.sat: "SATURDAY — no delivery. We take what there is. What there is, see the shelves." Beside it, a smiling bottle of kefir is drawn.
city.ps.chalk.sun: "SUNDAY — no shop assistants, the till is open. Looking is allowed, bread is tomorrow." The lettering is clearly by the cashier: very even.
city.ps.chalk.tue.1: "TUESDAY IS THE DAIRY DELIVERY. The van arrives at ten. Queue starts here, along the red runner. Two per person."
city.ps.chalk.tue.2: Lower down, in another hand and smaller: "There is enough kefir for everyone who is standing. Don't fret. Kefir doesn't like the fretful."
city.ps.clothes.1: I flick through the hangers. Tags are sewn inside the collars: "46-3", "48-4", "50-2". Size and height, like a cipher only the assistant knows.
city.ps.clothes.2: No item has a price. The assistant explains: this is a showing, not a sale. "Touch, try, beauty has to be touched. But we won't take it away."
city.ps.clothes.3: A heavy woollen coat smells of wardrobes and mothballs. Next to it a pale rustling raincoat crackles: thin as wrapping paper, yet it keeps the rain out as well as the coat.
city.ps.clothes.4: A small child's raincoat hangs on the lowest bar, with a hood and a mushroom-shaped button. On the tag: "For those who grow faster than we sew."
city.ps.delivery.am.1: Crates of milk are stacked against the wall, the bottles clinking in their slots. A porter in an oilcloth apron counts aloud while the assistant checks it against a slip.
city.ps.delivery.am.2: The queue already stretches along the red runner, though nothing is out on the shelves yet. People look at the crates with respect, like at guests.
city.ps.delivery.pallet: Wooden pallets are stacked by the wall; they smell of damp planks and a little of milk.
city.ps.delivery.pm.1: The crates are empty; what's left are the slats and the smell of kefir. The porter has gone, leaving his apron folded neatly on a slat: back again tomorrow.
city.ps.delivery.quiet.1: The hand-truck by the wall stands idle. The crates on it are empty, but their sides still hold a coolness, as after winter.
city.ps.delivery.quiet.2: On the pallet in chalk: "Don't touch, it's not our day." The pallet obeys and touches nobody.
city.ps.fitting.1: I drew the curtain and was left alone with somebody else's coat. The sleeves are longer than my arms: it was clearly cut with room for future growth.
city.ps.fitting.2: From beyond the curtain: "Well, how is it?" "Fine!" I lied: I was wearing a scarf from a different outfit. The assistant tactfully didn't check.
city.ps.fitting.3: Hat askew, scarf wound three times. In the mirror somebody older looked at me. I smiled at him; he didn't smile back: an adult, after all.
city.ps.fitting.am: In the morning the fitting room smells of pressed cloth and dust. Nobody hurries you, and you want to keep the coat on a while longer.
city.ps.fitting.eve: In the evening, by the next curtain, two people argue whether blue suits. Somebody sighs and says: "It suits."
city.ps.fmirror.1: A narrow-framed mirror, a little cloudy in one corner. I stand in it down to the waist, and imagination paints the rest. Mine is generous.
city.ps.fmirror.2: Behind me in the mirror I can see the aisle, and in it an assistant with a tape measure on her shoulder. She nods at my reflection. I nodded too, not wanting to be rude.
city.ps.fmirror.3: On the frame in chalk: "The mirror doesn't flatter, but doesn't lie. Please don't confuse it with us." Seems the joke gets passed from hand to hand.
city.ps.hooks.am: The hooks are almost empty: it's early. One holds somebody's scarf left over from last night; the attendant pretends it isn't there.
city.ps.hooks.any: Over every hook there's a number. A coat and its token live in pairs, like the two halves of one ticket.
city.ps.hooks.day: Half the hooks are taken: coats, a rustling raincoat, a hat with a fur crown, and a child's jacket on the lowest hook so its owner can reach.
city.ps.hooks.eve: By evening the hooks are so full that coats hang two to a hook. The attendant flits along the row, tokens jingling on her wrist like sleigh bells.
city.ps.hooks.night: The empty hooks sway a little in the draught. The tokens are piled on the counter: every coat has gone home for the night.
city.ps.lost.b1: Behind the desk sits a woman with glasses on a chain; in front of her a form headed "Record of Found Property" and an ink pad. "What have you lost?" "Nothing." "Then do come in, only don't take anything. It's all somebody else's."
city.ps.lost.b2: "The bureau takes everything," she says. "Umbrellas, mittens, keys. Once we took an accordion. The accordion turned out to be a wedding one."
city.ps.lost.b3: "We keep things for a month. If nobody comes, we send them to the fair, for the lottery. Better they make somebody happy."
city.ps.lost.d1: "The yellow umbrella with the duck-head handle? Yes, we have it today. The night watchman found it in the records department last night, perched on the counter as if on a roost."
city.ps.lost.d10: "We've decided: the announcement will be made not by the announcer but by somebody younger. The microphone is over there on the desk. Press the button and tell her the umbrella has been found. But like a human being, not like we do it."
city.ps.lost.d4: "The owner came and took it. An hour later they brought it to me from the fabrics department. I'm not surprised any more, I just write a new record. We have plenty of forms."
city.ps.lost.d7: "She admitted she loses it on purpose. I said: 'Lidiya Sergeyevna, you can't do that.' She said: 'I know,' and asked that next time it be announced louder."
city.ps.lostshelf.1: A right-hand mitten, red with stripes. No left one. The tag: "Waiting for its pair until the fifteenth."
city.ps.lostshelf.2: Keys on a ring with a plastic fish. If the fish could talk, it would have said long ago what they open.
city.ps.lostshelf.3: An empty violin case. The tag: "No violin was found. The case was. Perhaps it has gone off to play by itself."
city.ps.lostshelf.4: Horn-rimmed glasses folded with the arms inside. The tag: "Probably it isn't them that is wanted but whoever will see them." I decided not to try them on.
city.ps.lostshelf.5: A photograph: two people laughing in front of a lighthouse. The tag: "Found under a display case. We will return it to whoever knows who they are."
city.ps.lostshelf.6: A seventh-grade algebra textbook with a bookmark at the problem about two trains. The tag: "If you're still travelling, come back, we know the answer."
city.ps.lostshelf.7: A single child's shoe, left, toe worn. Beside it a note: "The right one went ahead and hasn't come back yet."
city.ps.lostshelf.8: A knitted hat with a pompom. The tag: "The pompom was not lost. It has always been like that." So the pompom is the great arguer here.
city.ps.lostumb.base: In the stand by the lost and found: ten umbrellas, one torn, two for children, the rest somebody's. Each has a dated tag and no two dates are the same.
city.ps.lostumb.d1: The yellow umbrella with the duck isn't among them. They say it moves between departments by itself: here today, in fabrics tomorrow.
city.ps.lostumb.d5: One umbrella is furled especially neatly and tied with a ribbon: yellow, with a duck's head. On the tag four entries: "Issued. Returned. Issued. Returned." There's no room left on the tag.
city.ps.lostumb.d9: The tag on the yellow umbrella is new and clean. The old one, written over from edge to edge, lies beside it under a paper clip, for keeps.
city.ps.menu.am: On the board: "Breakfast: semolina porridge, tea, a cheese sandwich." The porridge comes with jam if you ask, and asking is allowed.
city.ps.menu.eve: "Tea and supper: pies, tea, ice cream." Ice cream is written last and underlined twice: somebody's hope.
city.ps.menu.night: The menu has been wiped half away: the cleaner left a single word, "tea". Nothing more is needed.
city.ps.menu.noon: "Lunch: soup of the day, cutlet with mash, compote." The soup of the day is the same as yesterday: "of the day" here is a concept, not a date.
city.ps.mic.1: I pressed the button and the lamp turned red. The loudspeaker overhead repeated my words a moment late, an echo: "...attention, customers... customers... customers..."
city.ps.mic.2: "A customer in a blue jacket found someone's mitten on the stairs. The mitten awaits its pair at the lost and found. Thank you." The assistant nodded approvingly: short and to the point.
city.ps.mic.d10: "Lidiya Sergeyevna! Your umbrella has been found! It is waiting for you at the lost and found. I repeat: your umbrella has been found. Come, it misses you." For a second everybody in the hall froze. Then somebody clapped.
city.ps.shoemirror.1: The low mirror is tilted to show only feet. New shoes look even newer in it, and my own seem to walk apart from me.
city.ps.shoemirror.2: I tried on one shoe. It fit like a glove. The assistant watches me walk up and down in just the one and nods: "Go on, walk. The shoe has to get used to you."
city.ps.shoemirror.3: In the mirror my socks don't match. I knew that, but the mirror couldn't have been politer: it showed them and kept quiet.
city.ps.shoemirror.4: Beside it on the mat stands a shoehorn as long as an oar. Somebody in the family must have had very narrow heels.
city.ps.staff.fri: "Friday. Fish and cheese delivery. Fish to take home only by an entry in the log. Cheese isn't logged: it's in plain sight anyway."
city.ps.staff.mon: A sheet held by drawing pins: "Monday. Meeting at 8:40 by the till. Whoever is late takes the minutes. The minutes are one line, no more."
city.ps.staff.sat: "Saturday is a short day. Cash handed in at 19:30, counters wiped, kefir put in the cold. Smile at customers until the last minute."
city.ps.staff.sun: "Sunday. Only the cashiers are on. To the shop assistants: nobody has cancelled watering the flowers on the windowsill."
city.ps.staff.thu: "Thursday. Wages at the till until 13:00. Sign legibly: signatures 'in the shape of a fir tree' will not be accepted."
city.ps.staff.tue: "Tuesday. Dairy delivery: porters at 9:30. Have the scales, two buckets and patience ready for the intake. Patience is issued by the manager, one per person."
city.ps.staff.umb: A fresh notice pinned over the old ones: "Umbrellas found in departments are to be taken to the lost and found. Do not let them go walking. Management."
city.ps.staff.wed: "Wednesday: sanitary day in the fabrics department. Do not be alarmed by the smell of mothballs. The mothballs are on duty and will not leave."
city.ps.tannoy.closing.1: "The store closes in an hour. We ask customers not to rush, but not to linger either."
city.ps.tannoy.lost.1: "Lost and found, upstairs: a mitten has been found, right hand, red with stripes. The left one, apparently, is still with you."
city.ps.tannoy.lunch.1: "Dear customers! The shoe department is closed for a fifteen-minute break. The shoes won't go anywhere, we'll keep an eye on them."
city.ps.tannoy.morning.1: "Attention! Flowered cotton has arrived in the fabrics department. Lengths are measured from the shoulder to the fingertips. The ruler is with the assistant, but each of us has our own conscience."
city.ps.tannoy.morning.2: "Hot pies are available in the café upstairs. The pies are waiting, but not for very long."
city.ps.tannoy.night.1: The loudspeaker is silent. Now and then it crackles, as if the store were listening to itself at night.
city.ps.tannoy.open.1: The loudspeaker clicks and a pleasant woman's voice greets the whole store: "Good morning, dear customers! The store is open. Happy shopping and a good day."
city.ps.tannoy.sat: "It's Saturday and the café upstairs has ice cream. Please don't leave ice cream in your pocket."
city.ps.tannoy.tue: "The dairy counter is receiving its delivery. Please don't worry: there is enough kefir for everyone in the queue, and even for those who are thinking of joining it."
city.ps.tannoy.umb1: "A request to the owner of the yellow umbrella with the duck-head handle: your umbrella was found in the records department and is waiting for you at the lost and found. It is waiting patiently."
city.ps.tannoy.umb2: The announcer reads slowly, as customers asked: "Lidiya Sergeyevna. Lidiya Sergeyevna. Your umbrella has been found. I repeat: Lidiya Sergeyevna, your umbrella has been found."
city.ps.tannoy.umb3: "The announcement is cancelled. The yellow umbrella with the duck-head handle has been returned to Lidiya Sergeyevna. The store thanks everyone who helped to search, and the umbrella too."
city.ps.toy_train.prompt: E — wind up the little train
city.ps.train.1: I turned the key on the little locomotive's side until the spring crackled. It ran round the loop, its wagons clinking, and never left the rails, though I hoped it would.
city.ps.train.2: The little train rolled on solemnly and stopped in front of a cardboard box marked "Station". The passengers must have been boarding. I nudged it with a finger: time to go.
city.ps.train.3: A boy stands frozen next to me, mouth open. He watches the train as if it were carrying him. I wound it once more and stepped away so as not to be in the way.
city.ps.train.4: A date is stamped under the little locomotive: before I was born. The spring still remembers how to run.
city.ps.type.1: I put in a sheet and typed: "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog." Every letter is there. I left the sheet in the carriage for the next customer.
city.ps.type.2: The carriage rang at the end of the line and I jumped: I'm used to keys being silent. The test sheet is full of names: "Vasya", "Masha", "We were here".
city.ps.type.3: One letter, the Russian "zh", sticks. The assistant says it isn't a fault but a character. A typewriter with character costs five roubles more.
city.ps.umbstand.base.1: In the stand by the cloakroom: three black umbrellas, one checked, and a walking stick with a rubber tip. Each has a token tied to the handle. All very orderly.
city.ps.umbstand.base.2: The cloakroom attendant says you can tell the weather from the umbrellas: if they stand dry, by evening you'll be borrowing one.
city.ps.umbstand.y1: Among the umbrellas there's a yellow one with a duck-head handle. A tag on the handle reads: "Found. Awaiting owner." The duck looks at me with dignity.
city.ps.umbstand.y2: The yellow umbrella isn't in the stand. On the hook beside it hangs an empty tag, and on it in pencil: "Gone on business."
city.ps.umbstand.y3: A note is pinned to the stand: "The yellow umbrella is at the lost and found, not here. It is busy: waiting for Lidiya Sergeyevna." Signed: the cloakroom attendant.
city.ps.umbstand.y4: The umbrella is back in the stand, wiped clean. Beside it a note: "For Lidiya Sergeyevna. Returned at noon over the radio. Please don't lose it until next Tuesday."
city.ps.window.am.1: Behind the glass a woman stands on a stepladder with pins in her mouth. She is dressing a dummy in a coat and keeps turning it until the folds fall right.
city.ps.window.am.2: A second dummy stands next to her, headless for now, waiting its turn. The window is half empty. The winter things have arrived, the autumn ones haven't been taken away yet.
city.ps.window.am.3: On the window floor, chalk footprints mark where each dummy's foot belongs. The woman checks them the way a dancer checks steps.
city.ps.window.day.1: The window is finished. The dummies, all in the same pose, look out over the passers-by at the square. A small card says modestly: "Display piece. Not for sale."
city.ps.window.day.2: On the inside of the glass chalk marks are left, showing where each foot goes. The dummies' shoes cover them now.
city.ps.window.day.3: One coat is pinned at the back: perfect from the front, a gamble from behind. The window is honest from one side only.
city.ps.window.night.1: The window glows alone. The dummies gaze at the empty square as if they too had something to think over at night.
city.ps.window.night.2: The lamp in the window flickers a little. In that light the dummy's coat looks blue, then grey. In the morning it will be dressed all over again.
city.ps.window.umb: The dummy in the blue coat holds a yellow umbrella with what looks like a duck-head handle. Up close I read the tag: "Duplicate. In case the original goes off to the toy department again."
city.rassvet.dance.free1: The floor is empty and polished to a shine. A record lies on the player waiting for the teacher. I did three waltz steps to my own count and the echo answered.
city.rassvet.dance.free2: The mirror shows all of me, which is usually enough for a minute. I pretended to be only straightening my shirt, and straightened it three times.
city.rassvet.dance.fri: Friday is polka. We hop so hard the mirror trembles and nobody wants to stop first. When the record ended we kept hopping for another second.
city.rassvet.dance.sat: Saturday is a request night. Whoever asks for a waltz gets a waltz, whoever asks for a foxtrot gets a foxtrot. One couple ordered something that is not in the programme, and the teacher played it herself.
city.rassvet.dance.thu: Thursday is slow dances. The light is dimmed, the record rustles, couples sway on the spot as if the floor were drifting a little. The teacher walks among them whispering, "Breathe."
city.rassvet.dance.tue: Tuesday is waltz. The teacher claps: "One-two-three, young man, not one-two-stop!" I tried not to tread on myself and trod on my neighbour.
city.rassvet.dance.wed: Wednesday is foxtrot. The steps are quick and everybody's face is solemn, as at an exam. My partner said, "Don't look at your feet." I looked and lost the beat.
city.rassvet.door.1: Behind the door they are warming up: "do-re-mi-fa", then "do-re-mi-fa" again, but crosser. The choirmaster asks for basses. The tenors come in first: they always do.
city.rassvet.door.2: Behind the door the drama circle is rehearsing. Somebody says loudly and with feeling, "Dinner is served!" and somebody just as loudly answers, "No!" Then both laugh and it begins again.
city.rassvet.door.3: Late. Behind the door one voice and one violin, both quiet. They play the same passage for the fourth time: it does not come right, but it gets lovelier each time.
city.rassvet.door.4: Silence. The red lamp over the door is out. I put my ear to it: the radiator hums and nothing else. I decided not to disturb anyone.
city.rassvet.film.fri.d: A boy from the yard wants to win the table-tennis championship and trains against the wall of the house, on the garage roof, in the bread queue. His coach is a caretaker who plays left-handed and without a net. The final is won not by him but by a small girl with pigtails, but the cup goes round all the same and everyone is happy. For a long while afterwards the ball keeps tapping in the yard.
city.rassvet.film.fri.e: A musical. Every evening on the pier gather those who can dance and those who cannot but are shy. One couple cannot find the step: she leads, he treads on her foot. They waltz on the wet planks until the last lamp goes out. The lamp does not go out before the music ends: that is how it is done in films. The hall files out into the street, and somebody hums.
city.rassvet.film.mon.d: A comedy. A holiday-maker arrives for a week and his hat blows away on the first day. The hat tours the whole town: it sits on a monument, sails in a boat, rides in a cable-car cabin. He chases it all through his holiday and at the end realises he has rested better than anyone. The hall laughs so hard the screen shakes.
city.rassvet.film.mon.e: An old fisherman has waited forty years for a new lighthouse to be lit on the point. Every morning he goes down to the shore and straightens his scarf as if before an important meeting. At last the lighthouse is lit, and for the first time in his life he does not know what to do with his morning. He just stands and looks at the light. The hall weeps and nobody hides it.
city.rassvet.film.sat.d: A detective story for children. The most important gull has vanished from the fish quay, and a boy with a magnifying glass and a sandwich becomes the detective. He questions the witnesses: a herring, a cat and one very evasive swan. The gull is found on the cinema roof: she was being shown the films too. At this point the hall turns round to look at the ceiling every time.
city.rassvet.film.sat.e: A film about the projectionist of a small town. He loves every film he runs, but he only ever watches a sliver through the little window of the booth. One day he comes down into the hall and sits in the front row to see a whole film at last. It turns out the most interesting thing in the hall is happening not on the screen but on the faces. The hall can't help glancing back at the booth.
city.rassvet.film.sun.d: A cartoon. A hedgehog gets into a cable-car cabin to take an apple to a friend at the other end of town. First a giraffe rides along, then an orchestra, then one very serious snail. By the time they reach the station the apple has gone off, but everybody else arrives, and it turns out it is the friend's birthday. The children in the hall shout "Catch!" in chorus, although nobody has thrown anything.
city.rassvet.film.sun.e: An old silent film: a pianist plays to the screen, and the hall is so quiet you can hear the seats creak. A man walks down an empty street and every time turns the wrong way. He meets a closed shop, a wet umbrella on a bench and a window where somebody is playing a piano. At the end he finds the house, but we are not shown whose. You come out and for a few minutes you walk slowly.
city.rassvet.film.thu.d: A summer comedy. Three friends carry one watermelon across the whole town to a house where it is expected. On the way the watermelon manages to be a pillow, a ball and an important witness. When they arrive it turns out they were expected yesterday. They eat it on the porch anyway, four of them: the fourth is the neighbour's dog.
city.rassvet.film.thu.e: A radio amateur catches a call sign at night that is in no directory. For three nights he writes down dots and dashes and tells no one, and on the fourth he finds the courage to answer. One word comes out of the speaker: "Hearing you." After that there is not a word in the film: only the valves glowing orange and the needle trembling. Afterwards you want to keep quiet for a while.
city.rassvet.film.tue.d: A black-and-white newsreel. Cranes, concrete, and a girl with a tape measure giving orders to a gang of grown men. The cable car cuts across the sky and the cabins slide over the roofs like beads on a string. At the end the announcer says, "The town is ready", while on screen people carry a piano up the stairs of a new house.
city.rassvet.film.tue.e: The night shift on the cable car. The operator brings down the last cabin and always finds something forgotten in it: a glove, a book, somebody's word on the misted glass. The last passenger carries a letter in his pocket and is afraid to hand it over. The cabin reaches the station, the door will not open, and for two minutes they look at the sea in silence. Then the door opens.
city.rassvet.film.wed.d: A popular-science film. The announcer explains that the sun is a star and that we live next to it, which is perfectly normal. Drawn rays run to the Earth for eight minutes while the whole hall counts along with him. At the end we see a sunflower turning after the light, and then a sleepy cat doing exactly the same.
city.rassvet.film.wed.e: A girl finds a bottle with a letter by the breakwater. The letter is in Swedish, so she walks through town showing it to everyone: the fisherman, the chemist, the postman. Each translates it his own way and every time the letter comes out new. She decides to answer herself, in Russian, and throws the bottle back into the water. The hall is silent, and then it claps.
city.rassvet.hall.1: A request: during the show please do not talk, rustle or crack sunflower seeds. Rustling is an insult to the projectionist and to the people in the film.
city.rassvet.hall.2: Found in the hall: two left gloves, an old programme, a striped scarf. Ask at the cloakroom; name the colour and the character.
city.rassvet.hall.3: At weekends there are ten minutes of newsreel before the evening show, then the film. Latecomers: on tiptoe and no hard feelings.
city.rassvet.hall.4: New Year's week: a tree in the foyer, tangerines at the buffet one to a customer, and before the evening show the whole hall says "Happy New Year" in chorus.
city.rassvet.hall.5: 8 March: ladies get tea at the buffet without queueing. Gentlemen queue as usual, and also get tea.
city.rassvet.hall.6: 1 September: schoolchildren get the front row if they bring a school diary and a smile. The diary need not be opened.
city.rassvet.ladder.1: The club's ladder, in chalk on the board. From the top: Lev Markovich, Zoya, Vadim, Uncle Grisha, Kirill (ten years old). Under him an empty line labelled "a place for the brave".
city.rassvet.ladder.2: Kirill has climbed a rung. Uncle Grisha rubbed out his name and at once wrote it in again, a little lower: just in case.
city.rassvet.ladder.3: Zoya has challenged Lev Markovich. The game is set for Saturday, the stake is tea. Chairs are already set round the board.
city.rassvet.ladder.4: Saturday: Zoya won. Lev Markovich wrote himself onto the second line and left whistling. He likes losing more than winning: there is more to go over afterwards.
city.rassvet.ladder.5: On the bottom, empty line someone's hand has written: "Guest: draw with Vadim." A question mark beside it: everybody is waiting to see if the guest will come again.
city.rassvet.ladder.6: In the cupboard under the board lies a pad of sheets for recording games. The top one is blank, headed: "A start has been made."
city.rassvet.lost.1: A bucket of umbrellas by the hat stand. Tags on the handles: "blue", "black", "somebody's". Above them on the stand hangs a hat from the spring before last, and the cloakroom lady will not touch it: what if they come back.
city.rassvet.lost.2: A note is pinned to the tag on the black umbrella: "I'll call for it as soon as it rains." There is no rain yet, so the owner must be busy.
city.rassvet.lost.3: The cloakroom lady says the thing most often forgotten in the hall is a glove, and always just one. One glove is not a loss, it is a hint.
city.rassvet.menu.1: The menu: tea 15, coffee 30, pie 18, biscuits 20, Buratino 18. At the bottom in chalk: "Ice cream after the show, not during."
city.rassvet.menu.2: On Saturdays there are curd tarts with the tea, two to a customer so there is enough for all. The prices are the same. The buffet lady said the tarts are her way of telling who has come to the cinema for the first time.
city.rassvet.menu.3: The Sunday menu: tea and whatever is left from Saturday. The buffet lady says, "If there's little left, it was good."
city.rassvet.mirror.1: In the mirror: the couples, and the clock on the wall behind me. Half the hall looks at itself, the other half at the clock.
city.rassvet.mirror.2: In the mirror: an empty hall, a piano and me. The piano looks more confident.
city.rassvet.mirror.3: Slips of paper are tucked into the frame: the timetable, the teacher's phone number and somebody's drawing of a dancing dog. The dog keeps better time than many.
city.rassvet.piano.1: By day the pianist sits at the piano learning something without the music. I asked permission, he nodded and moved over. Together it came out twice as bad but twice as loud.
city.rassvet.piano.2: In the evening the piano works for the dance class: all the music is underlined in red. I tried to slip in a tune of my own and the teacher, without turning round, said, "In time."
city.rassvet.piano.3: At night the hall is empty and the piano is under a cloth. I lifted the cloth and pressed one key. The sound went all through the foyer and came back. I covered the piano again.
city.rassvet.piano.4: On the stand: music with no cover, the waltz "The Pier", copied out by hand. I played the first bars and somebody in the foyer said quietly, "That's the one."
city.rassvet.poster.fri: Poster. Today: in the afternoon “The Yard Champion”, in the evening “Waltz on the Pier”. Tomorrow: afternoon “The Case of the Missing Gull”, evening “The Projectionist”. Friday. After the evening show the buffet stays open another half hour.
city.rassvet.poster.mon: Poster. Today: in the afternoon “Holiday at My Own Expense”, in the evening “The Man Who Waited for the Lighthouse”. Tomorrow: afternoon “How Lyudmilovsk Was Built”, evening “The Last Cabin”. On Mondays the box office takes only smiles and thirty roubles.
city.rassvet.poster.sat: Poster. Today: in the afternoon “The Case of the Missing Gull”, in the evening “The Projectionist”. Tomorrow: afternoon “The Hedgehog's Cable-Car Adventures”, evening “The Empty Street”. Saturday: no break between shows; the break is in the buffet.
city.rassvet.poster.sun: Poster. Today: in the afternoon “The Hedgehog's Cable-Car Adventures”, in the evening “The Empty Street”. Tomorrow: afternoon “Holiday at My Own Expense”, evening “The Man Who Waited for the Lighthouse”. Sunday. The front row is for those who came with a hedgehog or without.
city.rassvet.poster.thu: Poster. Today: in the afternoon “Three Friends and a Watermelon”, in the evening “Silence on the Air”. Tomorrow: afternoon “The Yard Champion”, evening “Waltz on the Pier”. Thursday: the radio corner is open; the photo circle meets at six.
city.rassvet.poster.tue: Poster. Today: in the afternoon “How Lyudmilovsk Was Built”, in the evening “The Last Cabin”. Tomorrow: afternoon “The Sun Is Our Home”, evening “A Letter in a Bottle”. Tuesday: dance class in the foyer in the evening; noise is allowed, but in time.
city.rassvet.poster.wed: Poster. Today: in the afternoon “The Sun Is Our Home”, in the evening “A Letter in a Bottle”. Tomorrow: afternoon “Three Friends and a Watermelon”, evening “Silence on the Air”. Wednesday. Please arrive before the bell, not together with it.
city.rassvet.radio_a.1: Radio Lyudmilovsk: morning exercises to a piano. The announcer counts "and one, and two" so briskly that I want to get off my chair, but I stay.
city.rassvet.radio_a.2: A request concert: the fishermen ask for a song about the shore and are given a song about the shore. Requests are always played here, even the unfortunate ones.
city.rassvet.radio_a.3: The evening bulletin: wind from the sea, the cable-car timetable and an announcement about a lost umbrella. The umbrella, they say, has been found, but its owner has not.
city.rassvet.radio_a.4: At night Radio Lyudmilovsk is silent, the set only hisses, and now and then somebody's violin slips through the hiss. Turn the knob: the violin comes closer, then recedes.
city.rassvet.radio_b.1: By day the amateurs chatter on short wave: somebody in Riga asks for the weather again, somebody in Tallinn tells about his cat. The call signs sound like the names of neighbours.
city.rassvet.radio_b.2: Towards evening the distant ones come on. An amateur in Arkhangelsk spells out a QSL card letter by letter, then reads the address: "Lyudmilovsk, House of Culture, radio corner." That's us.
city.rassvet.radio_b.3: At night the air is as wide as the sea. A announcer in a foreign language reads out numbers, someone answers in Morse, and between them something quite different chirps. I wrote down the dots and dashes and understood none of them.
city.rassvet.radio_b.4: Our club's call sign is known in three countries. An amateur in Finland sent greetings to "the circle with the mug"; I did not understand, but passed it on.
city.rassvet.radio_b.5: Towards morning the stations go out one by one. What is left is an even noise, and in it suddenly something short: "...hearing you, Lyudmilovsk." I checked: at this hour there is nobody in the club but me.
city.rassvet.reel.1: The film hisses and the first frames have faded like a postcard. People walk along the pier with buckets and flags, and all of them look into the camera as if they cannot believe they are being filmed. A girl in a big beret climbs the lighthouse and lights the lamp, but the lamp does not burn. The third reel ends, the fourth tears, the fifth is gone: the screen turns white where the morning should have risen. The pianist played the waltz from the poster's sheet, and nobody in the hall moved.
city.rassvet.reel.2: We came again, almost the same people. In the dark somebody said the director's name out loud and several voices answered at once. The white light at the end is now called "the fifth reel", and nobody complains.
city.rassvet.reel.prompt: E — watch from the front row
city.rassvet.stubs.1: Ticket stubs in a tray: red for the afternoon shows, yellow for the evening ones. The clerk counts them every evening and gets a new number every time, but always the same smile.
city.rassvet.stubs.2: At the weekend there are twice as many stubs. The pile is weighed down with a cup so it will not fly about, and the cup is already empty.
city.rassvet.stubs.3: On the top stub in pencil: "Four people asked for Rassvet." The clerk does not know which Rassvet is meant, the house or the film, and writes everything down just in case.
city.rassvet.stubs.4: A stub with a red star: "front row, Rassvet". There are already forty-two of them. The clerk has stopped counting and started smiling.
city.read.art.1: An album by a marine painter. He painted the same pier a hundred times and never got it the same twice.
city.read.art.2: "How to Paint Light." First tip: you can't paint light, you can only leave room for it on the paper.
city.read.art.3: A mosaic exhibition catalogue. In one, a woman holds the sun the way you'd hold a hot frying pan: carefully, a little afraid.
city.read.art.4: A book about this very library: the capsules, it turns out, were meant as "rooms to be alone in without being lonely".
city.read.art.5: Children's drawings published as a book. Under one: "This is my dad at work. Work is where he glows."
city.read.birds.1: "Birds of the Coast: a Field Guide." The laughing gull isn't laughing at you, says a footnote. That's just her voice.
city.read.birds.2: Starlings, the author writes, can imitate a creaking gate, a ringing telephone and a woman calling her cat in.
city.read.birds.3: Chapter: "How to attract a rare bird." A feeder, patience, and not one sudden movement. "Patience" is underlined twice.
city.read.birds.4: On a plate, a jay at life size. The wing feather is so blue I want to touch it to see if it's wet.
city.read.birds.5: The last page: "Birds remember the way to the sun better than we do. If you get lost, watch where they fly in autumn."
city.read.chess.1: A book of studies. White to play and win, if they think of sacrificing the queen. I didn't.
city.read.chess.2: Club championship games, written out by hand. One move is marked "?!" and beside it: "but beautiful".
city.read.chess.3: "Chess for Beginners": the knight moves in an L because, the author explains, it's more fun that way.
city.read.chess.4: An article on the Sicilian defence. I read it twice and understood only that you can defend with gusto too.
city.read.chess.5: A problem on the last page: "Mate in two. Solution in the next issue." The next issue isn't on the shelf.
city.read.cooking.1: A cookbook worn soft with use. On the pie page, a grease stain shaped like Africa.
city.read.cooking.2: A recipe for Lyudmilovsk fish soup: fish, potatoes, onion and "a pinch of fireside talk". Without the last one, it says, it won't work.
city.read.cooking.3: Recipe cards in many handwritings. One says "Granny Zoya's honey cake. Show no one." It's been shown to everyone.
city.read.cooking.4: Japanese cooking for beginners: wash the rice "until the water is as clear as morning". Mornings must be special there.
city.read.cooking.5: A chapter called "Sunshine Jam": apricots, sugar and a south-facing windowsill. Not a word on how to eat it after.
city.read.engineering.1: "Cable Cars: Design and Operation." The tensioning diagram looks like a spider's drawing after a drafting course.
city.read.engineering.2: Plans for a house on stilts. In the margin the architect wrote: "Let the wind walk under the house, and children run there."
city.read.engineering.3: A young engineers' magazine: how to build a radio in a matchbox. I stared at the diagram so long I heard the sea.
city.read.engineering.4: A handbook of lighthouses: a Fresnel lens gathers light the way cupped hands gather water from a stream.
city.read.engineering.5: A textbook on computing machines with a punch card for a bookmark. The holes look like a constellation.
city.read.garden.1: "A Garden in the Sea Wind": what to plant so it won't blow away. The author's answer: "Patience. And sea buckthorn."
city.read.garden.2: A gardener's calendar. For April: "Sow dill, talk to the apple tree." The second is underlined.
city.read.garden.3: A schoolboy's herbarium in a folder. Under a pressed daisy: "Found by the sea. Smelt of sunshine."
city.read.garden.4: How to grow tomatoes on a ninth-floor balcony. The main thing, the author writes, is not to look down and to praise the seedlings often.
city.read.garden.5: A sunflower, the note says, turns its head after the sun only while it's young. Later it faces east and waits.
city.read.kids.1: A pop-up book about a hedgehog who wanted to see the sea. On the last page the sea unfolds right into your hands. I jumped.
city.read.kids.2: "Tales of the Lighthouse." In one the lighthouse falls in love with a star, in another with a steamer. The star never knew.
city.read.kids.3: A picture alphabet: "A for anchor, B for buoy, C for cable car…" Under "Me" there's a boy who looks a lot like me.
city.read.kids.4: A colouring book where someone coloured the sun with felt tip right through the paper: three layers, yellow, orange, yellow again.
city.read.kids.5: A "Why?" encyclopaedia. Why is the sky blue, why is the sea salty, why do we sleep. The last one has no answer, just "sleep".
city.read.local.1: "Lyudmilovsk: a Short Guide." The town, it says, was founded "in time immemorial, roughly on a Thursday".
city.read.local.2: A photo album: the promenade without palms, the square without a fountain, the cable car without cabins. The people in the photos are the ones walking about today.
city.read.local.3: A local history collection: Sun Square once had a great sundial. They say it ran fast whenever the town had a holiday.
city.read.local.4: A list of streets and their old names. One street used to be called "The Street We Walked Home Along". It's written just like that.
city.read.local.5: A pamphlet about the Mires west of town: "Visits are not advised. Reasons are not given, but you will feel them."
city.read.medicine.1: "The Home Doctor." For a cold, tea with raspberry; for melancholy, a walk by the sea. The second has a tick beside it.
city.read.medicine.2: A poster-pamphlet: "The sun is a friend, but even friends have bad days. Wear a sun hat."
city.read.medicine.3: An anatomy atlas. The heart is drawn in such detail it feels rude to look, like peeping.
city.read.medicine.4: A book on sanatorium cures: "Sea air, mineral water and no hurry." The last, it says, is the one least often prescribed.
city.read.medicine.5: A nurse's handbook. In round handwriting in the margin: "The patient in 12 asked again what the sun was like today. I said: good."
city.read.misc.1: I leafed through at random. In the margin someone had neatly underlined one word: "always".
city.read.misc.2: The book fell open by itself at page forty: people must often open it there.
city.read.misc.3: Between the pages: a pressed maple leaf and a tram ticket with no date.
city.read.misc.4: I read half a chapter and realised I'd read it before. I just don't remember where.
city.read.music.1: A teach-yourself guitar book, three chords. On page four someone gave up and drew a cat in the margin.
city.read.music.2: Sheet music for the waltz "Mist Over the Sea". I can't read music, but you can tell by the look of it: slow and a little guilty.
city.read.music.3: A biography of a conductor who once stopped the orchestra so everyone could hear a thrush singing outside.
city.read.music.4: A record catalogue from the Surf label. Next to the song "Sunbeam Bunny" someone has put five exclamation marks.
city.read.music.5: A solfège textbook. "Do" is home, "sol" is the sun, and "ti" is anyone's guess. The author doesn't know either.
city.read.poetry.1: A thin book by a local poet. "The sea writes on the sand / and wipes it all away, / as if it can't quite trust / the draft of its own grey."
city.read.poetry.2: Poems about the cable car: the cabins are "glass nuts on a string". Lovely, though it's unclear who'd crack them.
city.read.poetry.3: An inscription in ink on the flyleaf: "For Lida, so she won't miss the south. Though how much further south can you get." An illegible signature.
city.read.poetry.4: A haiku in translation: "The old pier. / The gull says nothing, / the wave finishes." The translator must have stood on a pier a long time.
city.read.poetry.5: "I saw the sun from within: / it's like a house where someone waits." Then the page is stained with tea, and I never found out who.
city.read.poetry_sale.1: On sale: "Poems of the Sea, Volume Two". There's no volume one. The bookseller swears volume two makes sense without it.
city.read.poetry_sale.2: A slim typewritten collection by a local poet. The dedication: "To the cable car, which never notices me."
city.read.poetry_sale.3: A three-rouble book full of pencil notes. Next to the line "the sun sets into the water and does not go out" someone wrote: "Checked. True."
city.read.poetry_sale.4: Children's verse about a gull who wanted a job at the post office. The last page is torn out, so I never found out if they took her on.
city.read.poetry_sale.5: A sign on the table: "Poetry sold by weight. Sad ones weigh less, happy ones more." Luckily nobody actually weighed them.
city.read.science.1: "Physics for the Curious." If the Earth stopped, the author writes, we'd all fly east. Politely, without panic.
city.read.science.2: A kitchen experiment: a glass of water, a postcard, turn it over. The water stays in. Pencilled beside it: "It doesn't. Tested. Mum."
city.read.science.3: An old science magazine: an article on how machines will learn to think. The last paragraph has been neatly cut out with scissors.
city.read.science.4: A chapter on light: a ray from the Sun takes eight minutes. So I always see the sun as it was eight minutes ago. A bit sad.
city.read.science.5: The periodic table across two pages. Someone pencilled in a hundred-and-nineteenth box and labelled it "lyudmilium".
city.read.sea.1: "Sailing Directions for Lyudmilovsk Bay." Depths in fathoms, shoals marked with crosses, and one with a question mark.
city.read.sea.2: The handbook says the tide here comes not by the timetable but "when it sees fit". Tables attached, just in case.
city.read.sea.3: A book of sea knots. I learnt the figure-eight and tied my shoelace with it at once. Took five minutes to undo.
city.read.sea.4: An old lighthouse keeper's memoir: in forty years he never saw the sea repeat itself. Not one wave the same.
city.read.sea.5: On the current chart the bay looks like a palm and the currents like the lines on it. The long one runs right through the pier.
city.read.sun.1: "The Sun is an ordinary star," the textbook begins. Then it spends twenty pages proving it's nothing of the sort.
city.read.sun.2: A star atlas. A pencil note by the constellation Cygnus: "You can see us from here. Probably."
city.read.sun.3: A pamphlet, "Solar Energy Serving the Town". On the cover, a vast sphere of mirrors round the Sun. Caption: "A project. Someday."
city.read.sun.4: A chapter on sunspots. People have been counting them for centuries, as if someone were counting the sun like loose change.
city.read.sun.5: An old calendar of sunrises and sunsets. Next to the longest day someone drew a little bonfire and wrote: "Don't sleep".
city.read.travel.1: "Shores" magazine: photos of every lighthouse on the coast. Ours is the double spread, and the caption, oddly, says "You are here".
city.read.travel.2: A guide to the north: volcanoes, fumaroles, snowfields and meadows where "the grass is knee-high and the sky lower than usual".
city.read.travel.3: A timetable of ferries that no longer sail. Someone ringed one crossing, "Lyudmilovsk to Far Shore, 06:40", and wrote: "Waiting".
city.read.travel.4: A traveller's diary: "Day three. Went nowhere. Sat on the promenade. Best day of the trip."
city.read.travel.5: An atlas with a sheet glued in: a map of places on no other map. The furthest is labelled simply "later".
city.reg.cog.1: A fresh sheet: "The club chess clock is missing, the one with the crack on the left dial. Whoever borrowed it, please bring it back. No scolding, only joy."
city.reg.cog.2: "Until the clock turns up, games are timed with the hourglass from the first-aid room. The sand is slow. If you're in a hurry, move faster."
city.reg.cog.3: "Thursday's blitz is cancelled: the hourglass was smashed in time trouble. The culprit repents and is sweeping up."
city.reg.cog.4: "To the model-makers: something is ticking under the workbench in the workshop. Please report what of yours is ticking, and why."
city.reg.cog.5: The model-makers' reply, pinned underneath: "It's a ship ticking. It's clockwork. Nothing to do with your clock. But we'll look too."
city.reg.cog.6: "The clock is found! It was on stage among the props for the play Time, Forward! The director swears he thought it was a dummy."
city.reg.cog.7: "Saturday: the Return of the Clock tournament. The left dial is still cracked and still two minutes fast. White plays at its own risk."
city.reg.library.1: A new notice: "Amnesty for overdue borrowers! Books returned free of fines until the end of the month. Even very old ones. Especially very old ones."
city.reg.library.2: "On the night of the 3rd, the book A Guide to Sundials was dropped in the returns box, issued 14 May 1968. Would the reader please call in. Just to talk."
city.reg.library.3: "Found in the Guide: a bookmark, a cable-car ticket to Lighthouse station, and in pencil: 'I read slowly. Forgive me.'"
city.reg.library.4: "The reader has not called in. The book is on display on the 'Returned' shelf by the window. Please don't touch: it's tired."
city.reg.library.5: "Three more books arrived on the 'Returned' shelf this week, all without slips, all about the sun. We now check the returns box twice a day."
city.reg.library.6: "To our unknown reader. If you are reading this: on Tuesdays we put the kettle on for two. There are no fines and there won't be."
city.reg.library.7: Added to the last notice: "We put the kettle on three Tuesdays running. On the third, there was a pressed daisy in the second cup. We consider that he called."
city.reg.market.1: "Jam contest! Jars accepted at the scales until Friday. Judges: the scales attendant, the honey seller and whichever child is around."
city.reg.market.2: "23 jars received. One has no label and tastes like the wind off the sea. Would the owner please come to the scales."
city.reg.market.3: "The judges remind you: pine-cone jam is not cheating, it's courage. But it goes in a separate category."
city.reg.market.4: "Three people have tasted the unlabelled jar. All three are smiling and can't say why. No more tasting, or the whole market will stop."
city.reg.market.5: "Results: 1st, sea buckthorn (Zoya, vegetable row); 2nd, gooseberry and mint; 3rd, pine cones. Audience prize: the unlabelled jar."
city.reg.market.6: "The owner of the unlabelled jar has not come forward. The jar stands by the scales. It's weighed every morning. It doesn't get any lighter."
city.reg.market.7: "Next year there will be a new category: 'Jam Nobody Made'. No entries accepted: such jars turn up on their own."
city.reg.rassvet.1: Notice: behind the radiator in the storeroom the projectionist has found a tin with no label. Film inside. Anyone who knows about film, please come by after the show.
city.reg.rassvet.10: Thank you to everyone who came. The tin is back in the storeroom, but now it has a label on the lid in big letters: "RASSVET. Do not lose." The film is no longer thought a made-up story but ours.
city.reg.rassvet.2: A pencilled note: the lid has one word on it, "Rassvet". Yes, like on our front. The projectionist says the house was named after this film, and everybody took the film for a made-up story.
city.reg.rassvet.3: The box office asks that nobody run the film on our projector: it is brittle, and the machine is meant for new stock. The argument in the buffet is still going.
city.reg.rassvet.4: The radio amateurs propose asking on the air whether anyone knows such a film. The club's call sign is on the card by the radio table, next to the mug.
city.reg.rassvet.5: An answer came at night on short wave from the next port: the film was shot here, on the pier, by the whole town, in 1931. The director left for the north before he could finish it.
city.reg.rassvet.6: The chess players found a poster from those years in the club archive: "Rassvet. Five reels. Live music." Live means the piano in the hall. The waltz from the poster has survived and the sheet is by the piano.
city.reg.rassvet.7: The projectionist rewound the film frame by frame, alone, in white gloves. Three reels of five are whole, the fourth is in shreds, the fifth is missing. He said even that is a lot.
city.reg.rassvet.8: The dance class has decided to learn the waltz from the poster. The teacher says the step is an old one and it needs two more couples. Come, if you can count to three.
city.reg.rassvet.9: It is decided: Rassvet is shown at one screening, from the front row, to anyone who comes and sits down. The ticket is thirty roubles, as always. The piano plays live, if there is somebody to play it.
city.reg.store.1: "At the lost and found: a yellow umbrella with a duck-head handle. Found in the records department. Owner please come to the first floor."
city.reg.store.2: "Yellow duck umbrella returned to its owner. Found again, in the fabrics department. Owner please come to the same place, first floor."
city.reg.store.3: "Dear owner of the yellow umbrella! The lost and found is open until 20:00. You may drop in just like that, without the umbrella."
city.reg.store.4: "Umbrella found in the toy department. The toy seller claims the duck on the handle winked at him. The seller has been given a day off."
city.reg.store.5: "The umbrella's owner has confessed she loses it on purpose: 'It's so nice to hear my name announced over the whole store.'"
city.reg.store.6: "At customers' request, lost-and-found announcements are now read over the radio twice. Slowly. With the name."
city.reg.store.7: "Nothing lost today. The lost and found will announce this over the radio at 12:00, just in case someone was waiting."
city.reg.tarelka.1: Pinned under the menu: "Lost: Kesha the parrot, green. Answers to 'Kesha' and to 'Mind the doors, please'. Finder gets a pastry on the house."
city.reg.tarelka.2: Below, in another hand: "Kesha was seen at Amber Shore station. Announcing the stops. Passengers pleased, the dispatcher less so."
city.reg.tarelka.3: "To cable-car passengers: if the cabin says 'Next stop, Lighthouse' and you're going to Zenith, it isn't the dispatcher. It's Kesha. Stay seated."
city.reg.tarelka.4: "Kesha spotted on the sanatorium roof. Shouting 'Sun! Sun!' The guests applauded; treatments ran half an hour late."
city.reg.tarelka.5: "Please don't try to catch Kesha with nets: he takes offence and stops announcing. Offer him sunflower seeds and say 'Terminus'."
city.reg.tarelka.6: "Kesha came back on his own. He sits on the coffee machine saying 'Terminus. Please vacate the cars.' He ate the pastry himself, too."
city.reg.tarelka.7: The last sheet, quite fresh: "Kesha asks you not to prompt him with station names. He already knows more than he should. Horizon, for example."
