city.story.kiosk1.prices.1: "Evening paper 5 rub. Cosmos and Us 40. Shores 40. Postcard 4. Fresh news after lunch, yesterday's at a discount."
city.story.kiosk1.prices.2: Under the glass, a list headed "Asked for but out of stock": "a magazine about cats", "today's weather for tomorrow", "a letter from my son".
city.story.kiosk1.prices.3: In chalk on the side: "The crossword in Friday's issue is hard. 14 down is 'tide'. Don't mention it."
city.story.kiosk2.freezer.1: The freezer glass has misted up from inside. Someone drew a sun on it with a finger, and it's slowly thawing.
city.story.kiosk2.freezer.2: The cups lie in rows like toy soldiers in a box. Winter breathes out of the chest, though outside it's July.
city.story.kiosk2.freezer.3: At the bottom of the chest, a lonely ice lolly from last summer, furred with frost like a coat. Nobody seems to have the heart to sell it.
city.story.kiosk2.freezer.prompt: E — look into the freezer chest
city.story.kiosk2.prices.1: "Plombir in a cup 28 rub. Buratino, Duchesse 18. Water 20. Ice cream doesn't melt if you eat it fast."
city.story.kiosk2.prices.2: At the bottom of the price list, in a child's hand: "Can I have two scoops?" Underneath, in a grown-up's: "Yes. If it's very hot."
city.story.kiosk2.prices.3: "On sale today: sun, free; shade under the awning, also free. Ice cream, for money."
city.story.kiosk3.prices.1: "Skvorets cigarettes 35 rub. Lighters 10. Seeds 10. Under-sixteens: seeds and good advice only."
city.story.kiosk3.prices.2: On the counter, a shell-shaped ashtray and a sign: "No smoking here. Thinking allowed."
city.story.kiosk3.prices.3: Over the hatch, a faded poster: a smoker whose lungs are two grey clouds. Under it someone has added: "Lovely weather, though."
city.story.kiosk4.buckets.1: Buckets of water, and in them carnations, daisies and one big sprig of dog rose, clearly picked on the way to work.
city.story.kiosk4.buckets.2: It smells of wet stems and a little of the sea. The sunflowers stand apart, facing south, like people at a bus stop.
city.story.kiosk4.buckets.3: In the last bucket, a single daisy with its petals plucked. Someone was asking it. From the look of it, the answer was "loves me".
city.story.kiosk4.prices.1: "Carnation 3 rub., daisies 5 a bunch, sunflower 7, dog rose not for sale, it's mine."
city.story.kiosk4.prices.2: Under the prices: "Bouquets for weddings, graduations and making up. Making up at a discount."
city.story.kiosk4.prices.3: In chalk: "Flowers arrive Thursday. Or Friday. Flowers aren't a bus."
city.story.kiosk4.talk.1: "The tulips are sad today, don't take them. Take the daisies, they're silly and cheerful. Though it's look-only: they haven't sent us anything to sell yet."
city.story.kiosk4.talk.2: The flower seller trims stems and tells me the sunflowers turn to the kiosk window every morning. "They think I'm the sun. I don't argue."
city.story.kiosk4.talk.3: "A bouquet for a girl? For your mum? For yourself? For yourself is the best kind. Come back when they're in and I'll make you one."
city.story.kiosk4.talk.4: A note on the counter: "Anahit! Don't put the buckets out till it's dark: the lilac is afraid of the sun." Signed: "Ales, evening shift."
city.story.kiosk5.prices.1: "Cable-car pin: next door at kiosk No. 1. Information 0 rub. More information, also 0. Advice on where to go: depends on my mood."
city.story.kiosk5.prices.2: Under the glass, a photo: a cabin over the sea at dawn, all pink. Caption: "6:04. Empty. Beautiful, though."
city.story.kiosk5.prices.3: "Children, pensioners and first-timers get a window seat. Everyone else too: it's all windows in there."
city.story.kiosk5.talk.1: "A cable-car ticket? You pay in the cabin; we only give information. Ask away: where, when and why. 'Why' is free."
city.story.kiosk5.talk.2: "Twelve minutes to Zenith if the wind doesn't argue. If it does, the cabin sways, a free ride on top."
city.story.kiosk5.talk.3: The information clerk leafs through a thick exercise book: "Passengers' Questions". The last one: "Why do the cabins never meet in the middle?" No answer.
city.story.kiosk5.talk.4: "The last cabin to the Lighthouse leaves at sunset. Not by the timetable, by the sun. The operator decided, and nobody objected."
city.story.kiosk5.timetable.1: "Cable car. Akademgorodok to Aton. Amber Shore to Zenith. Lighthouse. Interval: as long as the cabin is visible from the window."
city.story.kiosk5.timetable.2: The route map is drawn by hand in coloured pencils. Horizon and Polar Star are dotted in and labelled: "Only in dreams, for now."
city.story.kiosk5.timetable.3: "The cable car does not run in a thunderstorm. In a rainbow it runs, but slower, so everyone has time to look."
city.story.kiosk5.timetable.4: Added in pencil: "Whoever left a knitted mitten in cabin No. 7: it's been riding back and forth since Monday. It likes it."
city.story.kiosk6.prices.1: "Key 6 rub. Zip 10. Heel tips 8. Watches: depending on the watch's state of mind."
city.story.kiosk6.prices.2: "Urgent repairs: tomorrow. Very urgent: the day after; it needs thinking about."
city.story.kiosk6.prices.3: Clocks on the wall, each showing a different time. A sign underneath: "The right one is third from the left. Probably."
city.story.kiosk6.talk.1: The repairman doesn't look up from a watch movement. "Put it on the counter. What's broken? It'll mend itself? Then why are you here?" I've nothing to mend, and he seems pleased about that.
city.story.kiosk6.talk.2: "I cut keys, replace zips, treat watches. A heart? No, hearts go to the clinic. Though people do bring them to me sometimes."
city.story.kiosk6.talk.3: The hatch has a "Lunch" sign. The repairman sits right there eating and looking at me. "'Lunch' doesn't mean I'm not here. It means I'm eating."
city.story.kiosk6.talk.4: "A watch that runs fast is better than one that runs slow," says the repairman. "At least it wants to get somewhere."
city.story.kiosk6.tray.1: A tray of things mended but never collected: an alarm clock, an umbrella, one sandal. Each has a dated tag. The alarm clock has been waiting since spring.
city.story.kiosk6.tray.2: A bunch of keys with no tag. The repairman says they're keys "to everything that came before". He'll give them to whoever remembers what they open.
city.story.kiosk6.tray.3: A pocket watch engraved "To L. from L." It ticks loudly, as if in a hurry to be collected.
city.story.photo_desk.1: The photographer wipes a lens and squints at me. "You've got a face for a portrait. Not for a passport, for a portrait. Sit on the stool."
city.story.photo_desk.2: Envelopes of finished prints on the desk, a surname on each. One just says: "The boy who was looking at the sea." Not mine. Not yet.
city.story.photo_desk.3: "A portrait is sixty, ready on Thursday. Stick it in your diary and it'll show you were here," says the photographer, surprised at how that sounded.
city.story.photo_desk.4: Behind the desk, prints dry on pegs: weddings, school leavers, an old man with a dog. Everyone is squinting, as if he'd shot straight into the sun.
city.story.sanatorium_night.1: The receptionist took the money, handed me a towel with a little sun embroidered on it and made up the couch in the treatment room. "Breakfast at eight; we won't wake you."
city.story.sanatorium_night.2: All night mineral water murmured in the pipes behind the wall like a distant stream. I dreamt I was drinking it and turning transparent.
city.story.sanatorium_night.3: I woke at seven exactly, when the sun reached the pillow. Everyone here seems to wake that way.
city.story.sanatorium_night.4: In the night the duty nurse looked in with a torch, tucked my blanket in and tiptoed away. As if I were here for treatment. Maybe I am.
city.story.sanatorium_night.prompt: E — stay the night at the sanatorium
city.t3.stove.prompt: E — throw water on the stones
city.t3.t3_bars.1: The girls lined up at the wall bars: "legs higher, point your toes." I hung to one side, didn't point my toes, but tried.
city.t3.t3_bars.2: The rungs are warm from somebody's hands. I pulled my legs up to my stomach and held until they shook. The coach calls it an "L-sit," my stomach has another word.
city.t3.t3_bars.3: I hung at the very top and counted the windows. There are so many in the hall that I lost count twice. I liked losing count.
city.t3.t3_bike.1: In the morning the sea outside is a grey blanket. I pedalled and chased it to the very horizon. The horizon didn't give in.
city.t3.t3_bike.2: By day gulls pass the window, and a little ship behind them. The ship and I keep the same pace. I won't overtake it: it seems to be going to Sweden.
city.t3.t3_bike.3: In the evening the lighthouse comes on in the window. Every turn of the pedals, one flash. I counted to forty and lost it.
city.t3.t3_bike.4: At night the window shows only my own outline: a boy on a bicycle that goes nowhere. The boy is very determined.
city.t3.t3_changing.1: Behind the screen it's cramped but cosy: a hook, a mirror with a chipped corner and somebody's socks with kittens. The socks aren't mine, but I like them.
city.t3.t3_changing.2: Changed in three moves and spent three more on the laces. The laces won on a draw.
city.t3.t3_changing.3: The screen is a fabric with a pattern like grandma's sofa. You change and feel like a guest.
city.t3.t3_club_board.1: "Sections: basketball, gymnastics, weights, painting, pottery studio. Sign up with the coach, entry free, socks your own."
city.t3.t3_club_board.2: "Young Marine Painters" circle: Saturday, 11:00. Please bring your own eyes and old shirts: shirts will do for aprons.
city.t3.t3_club_board.3: COURTYARD TOURNAMENT "GOLDEN BALL" on Saturday! The "Surf Juniors" need a fifth player. Skill at shooting is optional.
city.t3.t3_club_board.4: "Surf Juniors" line-up: Lyosha, Taya, Ramil, Vanya and... The fifth line is in pencil: "somebody." "Somebody" is underlined twice.
city.t3.t3_club_board.5: Practice before the tournament: every day at five except Sunday. Late: an extra lap. On time: tea in the buffet (tea is not free).
city.t3.t3_club_board.6: Kit for the "Surf Juniors" is handed out at the till. Jersey No. 5 is free. Size: "still growing."
city.t3.t3_club_board.7: The tournament is on the hall's court, Saturday at 15:00. Fans: seats on the benches. Don't catch the balls. Catch the mood.
city.t3.t3_club_board.8: "SURF JUNIORS: SECOND PLACE!" The team thanks the coach, the buffet lady for the tea, and "number five" for turning up. The certificate is waiting at the till.
city.t3.t3_coach.1: "New here? The hall opens at seven, the sections are on the timetable by the door. Found a free ball? Shoot. Just not at the windows: they cost me more than the balls."
city.t3.t3_coach.10: "Second place is when you're glad and cross at once, and both halves are right. Taya is telling the whole courtyard about your shot. One more time?"
city.t3.t3_coach.2: "You've been around a few days now. I noticed: you come in like it's a job. Good. Sport loves the ones who show up on a boring Tuesday."
city.t3.t3_coach.3: "I hear you were shooting from the far line. Missed, but with a face like you'd scored. In basketball that's half the job. The other half is scoring."
city.t3.t3_coach.4: "Not now, the boys are warming up. Come over when I blow the last whistle."
city.t3.t3_coach.5: "Quiet, the girls are counting their jumps. If anyone loses count they start over, and I'm the one who has to listen."
city.t3.t3_coach.6: "Listen, "Surf Juniors" have a courtyard tournament and there are only four of us. Vova moved away with his parents, his ball stayed behind. Want to be the fifth? Running is optional. Standing there and not getting in the way is a must."
city.t3.t3_coach.7: "Come to practice at five. The hoop on the back wall is for people who mean to play, not pose for photos."
city.t3.t3_coach.8: "Good that you keep coming. The number-five jersey is at the till, locker five is free. Just don't wipe your face on it: there's one jersey and a lot of faces."
city.t3.t3_coach.9: "Game day. Stick close to Taya: she reads the court better than I read the paper. The rest will sort itself out."
city.t3.t3_court.1: The tournament! Lyosha passed me the ball and the hall suddenly went quiet, as if everyone were waiting for me to do something. I did: I shot. The ball knocked twice on the rim and dropped in. Taya shrieked so that the glasses in the buffet shook.
city.t3.t3_court.2: The Seagulls pressed from all sides. Ramil cut right, Taya took the rebound, and I stood under the hoop and waited. And got what I waited for: the ball came into my hands by itself. We lost the final by one point, but they clapped for us too.
city.t3.t3_court.3: The court after the tournament: sweet wrappers, chalk, somebody's hairpin. The fans' ribbon is still hanging on the hoop.
city.t3.t3_court.4: Two on two: me and Taya against Ramil and Lyosha. We lost 6 to 10. Taya said it was a warm-up and I believed her, with relief.
city.t3.t3_court.5: A scrimmage to ten. I scored two, Lyosha scored eight and apologised a lot. All of this is for the tournament.
city.t3.t3_court.6: On Sunday the five don't meet: everyone has families, grannies, lunches. I dribbled alone on the empty court. The ball obeyed well.
city.t3.t3_easel_lighthouse.1: The lighthouse in the morning is pale as a candle in a sunny room. I painted almost without colour, only white, and it began to glow from inside.
city.t3.t3_easel_lighthouse.2: By day the lighthouse is just a red-and-white tower. I painted a tower and got a chimney. I wrote "Lighthouse" under it. The caption helped.
city.t3.t3_easel_lighthouse.3: At sunset the lighthouse turns pink and its shadow lies all the way to the pier. I spent longer on the shadow than on the tower.
city.t3.t3_easel_lighthouse.4: At night the lighthouse is all about the beam. I painted it in yellow on dark, and the canvas seemed to warm up a little.
city.t3.t3_easel_sea.1: The morning sea is grey as pearl: grey, pink and a little green. I painted with a wet brush and the sea came out wet.
city.t3.t3_easel_sea.2: By day the sea is blue and there's never enough blue. I painted until it looked like a postcard and was upset. The studio leader said: "Somebody paints the postcards too."
city.t3.t3_easel_sea.3: In the evening the sea is gold, then copper, then dark. I couldn't mix paints fast enough: the sea changed faster than the brush.
city.t3.t3_easel_sea.4: At night I painted the sea from memory, by lamplight: black, with a moon path. The leader said: "The night sea isn't painted with the eyes." What with, he didn't say.
city.t3.t3_easel_teacher.1: The teacher's easel: a big canvas with a charcoal sketch: a pier, gulls, a boy in a hood. The boy has no face yet.
city.t3.t3_easel_teacher.2: The teacher has put paint on the pier: a peach sky, a steel sea. The boy still has no face but stands more firmly.
city.t3.t3_easel_teacher.3: The boy has got a face. I look at him and try not to think that it's a little familiar.
city.t3.t3_easel_teacher.4: The canvas is signed and stands by the door with a note: "Hang in the foyer." The boy looks at the sea. Now at the sea, not at me.
city.t3.t3_glaze.1: On the bench, jars of glaze: "green," "blue," "do not touch." "Do not touch" is the prettiest. Nothing to touch until Thursday: the bowls haven't been fired yet.
city.t3.t3_glaze.2: I glazed bowl No. 7: green, with a little blue on the bottom. The potter warned me: in the jar the glaze is one colour, out of the kiln it will be another. Like people.
city.t3.t3_glaze.3: The bench is tidied, the jars are shut. On the newspaper, the print of a bowl's foot: someone checked whether it stands level.
city.t3.t3_glaze.4: The bench is empty, only the "do not touch" jar stands at the edge. I didn't touch it. Apparently I'm growing up.
city.t3.t3_hoop_free.1: The west hoop is warmed up by morning: the sun comes through the window right onto the backboard. I aimed at the patch of sunlight. I hit it more often than the hoop.
city.t3.t3_hoop_free.2: It's quiet at the west wall: people come here who aren't ready for spectators yet. I became one of them. Two in a row, and at once I wished someone were watching.
city.t3.t3_hoop_free.3: By evening the floor creaks louder and the ball bounces more cheerfully. I shot until the shadow of the hoop crept to the middle of the hall.
city.t3.t3_hoop_main.1: A practice is under way at the back wall: five boys, three balls, one whistle. They put me on rebounds. I rebounded honestly and even returned a ball to whoever threw it.
city.t3.t3_hoop_main.2: At the back wall the girls practise shots from under the hoop and count aloud. I stood beside them and shot in time: scored on "seventeen."
city.t3.t3_hoop_main.3: In the morning the hoop is mine. The cleaner was wiping the lines, and the ball left dusty marks on them: exactly as many as my misses.
city.t3.t3_hoop_main.4: In the evening the light over the hoop is warm, like in a film about champions. Ten shots, no spectators, I clapped for myself.
city.t3.t3_hoop_main.5: On Saturdays it's courtyard against courtyard here. They took me "for five minutes." It turned out to be twenty.
city.t3.t3_hoop_main.6: On Sunday there's a grandfather and grandson at the hoop. Grandpa teaches shooting "from the chest," the boy says "from the heart." The boy, by the way, scored.
city.t3.t3_kiln.1: The kiln is cold. On the shelf beside it, raw bowls, grey as mice. You can't pick them up: they'd crumble from a glance.
city.t3.t3_kiln.2: The kiln hums and smells evenly of warm brick. Through the peephole, orange light. A note: "Firing. Do not open. Do not knock. Peek no more than three times."
city.t3.t3_kiln.3: The kiln has cooled. The door is ajar, inside white cups with a pink tinge. One has cracked. The potter says: "That's not a flaw, that's character."
city.t3.t3_kiln.4: The second firing, with glaze. A red peephole, a quiet hum. On the kiln, in chalk, a number: 1060.
city.t3.t3_kiln.5: The kiln is open and the finished ware is inside! It shines like wet stones. Bowl No. 7 is green as the sea on a grey day, with two blue specks.
city.t3.t3_kiln.6: The kiln is resting, like everyone. Warm to the touch. On the floor, crumbs of glaze, green and light blue.
city.t3.t3_lockers.1: Lockers by number. On No. 7 someone scratched: "Do not open until victory." The door opens, so there must have been one.
city.t3.t3_lockers.2: On door No. 3 there's a fish sticker and a note: "Slippers live here. Do not feed."
city.t3.t3_lockers.3: A new paper on locker No. 5: "Free. For the fifth." In the coach's handwriting, pressed hard.
city.t3.t3_lockers.4: Locker No. 5 stands open. Inside, a jersey with a five and a note on the hook: "Size: still growing. Don't lose it."
city.t3.t3_lockers.5: On locker No. 5 my name has been added in chalk. Chalk, so it's easy to wipe off. It doesn't come off: I tried with my sleeve.
city.t3.t3_mats.1: On the mats the girls do the "bridge" and the "birch." Mine came out more of a "stump." Lidia Pavlovna said: "A stump is a tree too."
city.t3.t3_mats.2: The mats are warm after the gymnasts. I lay down and looked at the ceiling: a cobweb shaped like a constellation. I named it the Vaulting Horse.
city.t3.t3_pool.1: "POOL (tower, upper bridge, turn left) CLOSED. Tiles being replaced. The tiles have arrived, the tiler has arrived. The glue has not."
city.t3.t3_pool.2: "The glue has arrived. The tiler has gone to fetch tiles of another colour. The pool will be "sea" rather than "white." Thank you for your patience."
city.t3.t3_pool.3: "Tiling in progress. Six 25-metre lanes will be painted on the bottom. Lanes are promised straight, though straightness remains at the tiler's discretion."
city.t3.t3_pool.4: "Filling has begun. The pool fills like a cup in the kefir queue: slowly and with dignity." The lifeguards have hung the ring in its proper place. The ring now looks at the water.
city.t3.t3_pool.5: "The pool opens on Monday. A trial swim for those who bring a doctor's note and a cap." A cap can be found in the "Lost caps" box at the till.
city.t3.t3_reception.1: "The pool needs a doctor's note, the gym a season ticket, table tennis a good mood. Which of those have you got?"
city.t3.t3_reception.2: Cups above the desk, and under them a box marked "Lost swimming caps." There are more caps than cups.
city.t3.t3_reception.3: The cashier hands out a locker key on an elastic band: "Number seven, a lucky one. Don't mix it up with eight, that's the coach's."
city.t3.t3_reception.4: Timetable of sections: gymnastics, swimming, "Health after sixty" and "Health before sixteen." The second one is for me.
city.t3.t3_reception.5: "I'm keeping the number-five jersey, but I hand it only to those who promise not to wipe their face on it. The coach said: "A jersey has a number, not a towel.""
city.t3.t3_reception.6: "The coach has gone to paint the balls yellow. So that from the stands you can tell which is the ball and which is us. We're visible anyway."
city.t3.t3_results.1: Courtyard league table. 1. Seagulls: 12 points. 2. Lighthouse: 10. 3. Surf Juniors: 8. In pencil: "there will be more."
city.t3.t3_results.2: Hall records. Vault: Lyosha, "with room to spare." Pull-ups: Taya, 14, "not counting sighs." Next to it, an empty line: "a record not yet beaten."
city.t3.t3_results.3: Swimming, 25 m record: 19.4 seconds. The plaque is under repair together with the pool. The record-holder is waiting for water.
city.t3.t3_results.4: Courtyard tournament, results. 1. Seagulls: 3 wins. 2. Surf Juniors: 2. 3. Lighthouse. Best newcomer: No. 5 with 4 points, 3 rebounds, 1 ball into his own hoop. The own-hoop ball has been crossed out "for educational reasons."
city.t3.t3_results.5: Under the table, in chalk: "Thanks, number five." In the match record, a name is written against number five. The one I know already.
city.t3.t3_sauna_sit.1: In the morning the sauna is empty and smells of birch. I sat and listened to the stones cooling: tick, tick, tick.
city.t3.t3_sauna_sit.2: After practice the basketball players pile in, red as crayfish. The whole conversation: "Oof." And the answer: "Yep."
city.t3.t3_sauna_sit.3: Saturday steam! On the top bench a man in a felt hat reads a wet newspaper. The news is as fresh as it gets: straight out of the steam.
city.t3.t3_sauna_sit.4: On Sunday there are two people in the sauna, both asleep sitting up. I sat quieter than water so as not to disturb the Sunday.
city.t3.t3_sauna_water.1: I splashed a ladle onto the stones. They hissed and the steam settled on my shoulders like a warm blanket.
city.t3.t3_sauna_water.2: A ladle, a bucket, the stones: very simple. Only the steam doesn't listen and goes where it likes, usually into my face.
city.t3.t3_sauna_water.3: A sign on the stove: "Pour water in moderation." I poured in moderation. Moderation, it turns out, smells of a birch whisk.
city.t3.t3_sections.1: "Timetable. Mon, Wed, Fri: basketball (boys). Tue, Thu: gymnastics (girls). Sat: weights in the morning, games after lunch. Sunday: the hall is yours, there is no coach."
city.t3.t3_sections.2: Today: basketball, "Surf Juniors", 15:00–19:00. Please don't step on the court in street shoes. We ask politely. The coach asks impolitely.
city.t3.t3_sections.3: Today: gymnastics, Lidia Pavlovna's group. The vaulting horse is warming up, the wall bars are taken until six. Spectators: the bench.
city.t3.t3_sections.4: From 7 to 15 the hall is free; at 11:00 there's a PE lesson for class 6B. Please don't mistake the balls for heads.
city.t3.t3_sections.5: Saturday: weights until lunch, games after. Spectators free, players: bring water, leave the nerves.
city.t3.t3_sections.6: Sunday: short day, no coach. The ball is the responsibility of whoever picked it up.
city.t3.t3_sections.7: The hall closes at 21:00. The night watchman asks to be reminded of this very politely and very early.
city.t3.t3_shower.1: The hot water came in fits, like thoughts after practice. Then it steadied, and I stood there until I remembered the queue.
city.t3.t3_shower.2: The soap fell, I went after it, it went away from me. Caught it on the third try. Sport, basically.
city.t3.t3_shower.3: The water washed off the dust, the tiredness and half of my misses. The rest will dry by themselves.
city.t3.t3_shower.4: Steam, the noise of water, an echo. I sing without an ear but loudly. The shower is the one place where I'm surely the champion.
city.t3.t3_tactics.1: A chalk diagram on the board: circles are ours, crosses are not. One arrow leads to the basket. Another leads to the buffet, and it looks thicker.
city.t3.t3_tactics.2: A play called "Five": four circles stand firm, the fifth is empty with a question mark. Underneath: "newcomer: don't get in the way, but do teach."
city.t3.t3_tactics.3: The fifth circle has moved to the left wing and is ringed twice. Beside it: "don't let him fall, pass on time, make noise only when it counts."
city.t3.t3_tactics.4: The plan for Saturday: the Seagulls play rough, so play fast. Over it, big: "Run!" and small: "and think."
city.t3.t3_tactics.5: The board has been wiped clean. In the corner, a circled five and one word: "Thanks."
city.t3.t3_vault.1: Lidia Pavlovna's group: two vaults each over the horse. I got one counted: the second was more of a fall.
city.t3.t3_vault.2: Ran up, pushed off the springboard, cleared it, this time with room to spare. The horse nodded, or I imagined it.
city.t3.t3_ware.1: The shelf is empty apart from somebody's old cups and a bag of plaster.
city.t3.t3_ware.2: On the shelf, raw bowls by number, still grey and damp. No. 7 stands between two others and looks confident.
city.t3.t3_ware.3: The bowls have dried and paled like bread. They stand in line for the kiln. No touching: a finger can leave you in them forever.
city.t3.t3_ware.4: After the first firing the bowls are pink and ring when flicked. No. 7 is whole. Beside it, a cracked No. 3: the potter kept it "for beauty."
city.t3.t3_ware.5: The glazed bowls look wet but matt: the colour will come out in the kiln. Hard to believe, but it will.
city.t3.t3_ware.6: Finished! Green, blue, speckled. Beside them a note: "Take them yourselves. If you can't take them, give them away." No. 7 is mine.
city.t3.t3_ware.7: The shelf is resting. On it, one bowl, somebody's, with a note: "This one's mine. Not for giving." Beside it an empty spot for mine.
city.t3.t3_weights.1: The weightlifting section clatters in the corner: two huge men lift plates and whisper curses at them. I joined the queue for the bar: it moved slowly but respectfully.
city.t3.t3_weights.2: The basketball boys are working their legs. "Squat until you're lower than the hoop," the coach orders. "Then stand up and you'll be taller." I squatted five times. Stood up taller.
city.t3.t3_weights.3: Quiet and iron. I loaded the plates the way the coach taught me: the strength is in the legs, not the face. The face went red anyway.
city.t3.t3_weights.4: Held the bar without lifting. The bar didn't care: it's iron. I did. I think I've made friends with iron.
city.t3.t3_wheel.1: The potter said: "Centre it. Clay is like character: press and it runs away, don't press and it won't stand." On the third try the walls held. Bowl No. 7 came out with one side higher than the other. It was put aside to dry.
city.t3.t3_wheel.2: The wheel is quiet today: the kiln is firing and the potter looks into it every ten minutes, like into an oven with a pie. I just centred clay, for the feel of it.
city.t3.t3_wheel.3: Nobody sits at the wheel today: everyone is waiting. The bowls came out of the kiln after the first firing, No. 7 turned pink and rings like a bell. Next comes glaze, and that's not the wheel, that's the bench.
city.t3.t3_wheel.4: At the weekend the wheel goes to the little ones: they make "wrong" hares. They left me a lump too. I made a hare with one ear. The potter said: "That's not a hare, that's a running hare."
city.take.any.1: Nothing left here. Someone got here first.
city.take.any.2: Empty. Only a dusty rectangle where something used to lie.
city.take.daily_paper.1: I took a paper. On the front page, a fisherman with a flounder the size of a saucepan lid.
city.take.daily_paper.2: Today's issue. Forecast: clear, wind off the sea, music in the park possible in the evening.
city.take.daily_paper.3: The paper's still warm, as if it had just been printed behind the wall.
city.take.postcard.1: I took a postcard of the promenade. The sky on it is bluer than it ever really is.
city.take.postcard.2: A "Greetings from Lyudmilovsk!" card. Nobody to send it to, but I'll keep it.
city.take.postcard.3: On the back someone had pencilled "Dear…" and never finished.
city.talk.butcher.1: The butcher hones his knife and nods to me like an old friend. There's nothing for me to buy from him.
city.talk.butcher.2: "Out of mince, come early tomorrow. Scraps for the cats are free."
city.talk.butcher.3: Above the counter, a chart of beef cuts. The cow on it looks very calm.
city.talk.butcher.4: "What a sun today, eh? Even the meat looks rosier," said the butcher, surprised at himself.
city.talk.caretaker.1: The caretaker is mending a stool and says without looking up: "Stairs were mopped on Wednesday. Shuffle quieter."
city.talk.caretaker.2: Keys hang on nails, each with a tag: "Cellar", "Roof", "Fuse room", "Can't remember". The last one is the shiniest.
city.talk.caretaker.3: "I put a bulb in on the fourth, and it's gone again. Must like the dark," the caretaker sighs.
city.talk.caretaker.4: The radio in the cubbyhole mutters the weather report. The caretaker nods at each figure as if greeting old friends.
city.talk.cashier.1: "First the department, they write you a slip, then me, then back to the department. Clear?" "Clear."
city.talk.cashier.2: The cashier clacks the till so fast she seems to be playing a polka on it.
city.talk.cashier.3: "No small change? What if you look?" I looked. Found a button.
city.talk.cashier.4: By the till there's a saucer for change with one sweet in it. Change too, apparently.
city.talk.cloakroom.1: "Don't lose your token," said the attendant, though I had nothing to hand in.
city.talk.cloakroom.2: The hangers sway and chime softly, like wind chimes.
city.talk.cloakroom.3: "In summer we get only umbrellas, and one hat. The hat's been here since the spring before last."
city.talk.cloakroom.4: The attendant is knitting something long and striped. A scarf, she says. Three years now, she says.
city.talk.closed.1: Nobody. A note on the glass: "Gone to the depot. Back at 15:00." No date.
city.talk.closed.2: The counter's bare: an abacus and a glass of pencils. I tapped on the glass. Silence.
city.talk.closed.3: "Stocktaking." The sign hangs crooked, as if it went up in a hurry long ago.
city.talk.closed.4: Looks like they only sell to the neighbours, and the neighbours are all at home.
city.talk.club_lending.1: "The club's books are for circle members only. Join the chess circle and we'll lend you The Caro-Kann Defence. Gripping."
city.talk.club_lending.2: Names in a column on the record card, each marked "returned". Except one. Next to it, a sad little face.
city.talk.club_lending.3: "Take Radio magazine instead," the attendant suggests. "Lots of diagrams, few words. Rests the eyes."
city.talk.club_lending.4: The "Cog Club Library" stamp goes on everything: books, tickets and once, they say, the cat.
city.talk.concierge.1: The concierge looks up from her knitting. "Who for? Oh, just looking… Well, sit a while, there's a good draught here, off the sea."
city.talk.concierge.2: "The lift's thinking again on the seventh. If you get stuck, sing, I'll hear. Everyone who gets stuck sings. We've got a choir here."
city.talk.concierge.3: On the desk, a book for "Letters and parcels received" and a jar of toffees "for those who say hello politely". I said hello very politely.
city.talk.concierge.4: "Forty-two moved out, forty-three moved in, and the cat from forty-one visits both." The concierge knows the house by heart.
city.talk.counter.1: "Can I help you, young man?" "Just looking." "Look all you like."
city.talk.counter.2: Behind the counter someone is writing in a fat ledger and raises a finger: "One moment."
city.talk.counter.3: "Our break's from one to two, but for you, all right."
city.talk.counter.4: They smiled at me as if I came in every day. Maybe I really do.
city.talk.fishmonger.1: "The flounder's this morning's, the herring's yesterday's, and the gobies — don't ask."
city.talk.fishmonger.2: The fishwife weighs fish in her hand more exactly than the scales. The scales don't argue.
city.talk.fishmonger.3: "Catch something yourself, bring it here, I'll buy it," she said with a wink.
city.talk.fishmonger.4: One fish with a golden flank lies on the ice. "Not for sale," they say. "It's for luck."
city.talk.market_office.1: The market manager checks a weight on the control scales. "A hundred grams must be a hundred grams. Even by the sea."
city.talk.market_office.2: On the door: "Complaints book available on request." The book is brand new. Either there are no complaints or nobody requests it.
city.talk.market_office.3: "Tomorrow's pitches are all taken. Want to sell? Come at five in the morning with a crate and a smile."
city.talk.market_office.4: The little office smells of paper, smoked fish and tangerines. So does the whole market, only here it's official.
city.talk.office.1: "Pass? No pass, no entry. Sit on the sofa and think about it."
city.talk.office.2: The porter doesn't look up from his crossword. "Heavenly body, three letters?" "Sun." "Fits."
city.talk.office.3: "Visitors from nine. And whom are you here to see?" "I… nobody yet."
city.talk.office.4: A bell on the desk and a sign: "Ring once." I rang once. That was enough.
city.talk.reception.1: "Are you a guest? No? Then at least have some water, ours is medicinal."
city.talk.reception.2: A bell on the desk and a booking book for treatments. Next to every name, a little drawn sun.
city.talk.reception.3: "Breakfast from eight, dinner till seven, the sea round the clock," the receptionist rattled off.
city.talk.reception.4: "No rooms. But if you really need one, in 204 only one floorboard creaks."
city.talk.records.1: The record man drops the needle and lifts a finger. "Listen. Here, at two minutes, the singer sighed. That's not in the score."
city.talk.records.2: "No new ones, only good ones." He flicks through the sleeves like cards and pulls one out: "For you, this. You'll thank me later."
city.talk.records.3: On the wall, a record broken in half and glued. "My first waltz," says the man. "I danced on it. Literally."
city.talk.records.4: "Records are tinned time," the man said, and blew on the disc as if it were hot.
city.talk.registry.1: "Surname? Year of birth? I can't find your card. That means you're healthy," the registrar decided.
city.talk.registry.2: The appointment slip comes out of a little wooden box. Number 13. "Don't worry, thirteen's the quickest one here."
city.talk.registry.3: Behind the window, thousands of cards in drawers, alphabetical. The whole town, by its aches. Mine isn't among them.
city.talk.registry.4: "First the scales, then the eye chart, then the doctor. In that order, or the doctor gets offended."
city.talk.rentals.1: "Boats till sunset, deckchairs till six, umbrellas till the first rain."
city.talk.rentals.2: "Deposit's a passport. No passport? Then your word of honour. Got one of those?"
city.talk.rentals.3: Oars stand along the wall, numbered in paint. Number seven is missing: it went to sea last July.
city.talk.rentals.4: "The bikes are being repaired," sighed the man. "All of them. At once. A mystery."
city.talk.repair.1: The repairman doesn't look up from the watch. "Leave it, a week." "I've nothing to leave." "Even better."
city.talk.repair.2: On the shelf an iron, a transistor radio and a toy railway wait for their owners. The tag says "Urgent. 1987".
city.talk.repair.3: "You can fix anything but the weather and a mood," the repairman said, and fixed my shoelace.
city.talk.repair.4: It smells of rosin and machine oil. Somewhere in a corner twenty clocks tick at once, all out of step.
city.talk.salon.1: "Half-box, Canadian, or Like Dad's? No dad here? Then Like the Sea: in waves."
city.talk.salon.2: It smells of Chypre cologne and hot tongs. On the table, magazines of hairstyles that exist only in pictures.
city.talk.salon.3: The barber snips the air like a grasshopper. "Booking for tomorrow. Today I'm only cutting clouds."
city.talk.salon.4: An old lady waits on the sofa with a newspaper. "I'm not here for a haircut," she whispers. "I come for the news. Better than the radio."
city.talk.savings.1: "Got a passbook? No? We'll open one when there's something to put in it," the cashier says, so kindly it hardly stings.
city.talk.savings.2: A poster: "Keep your money in the savings bank." On it a piggy bank smiles as if it has saved up everything already.
city.talk.savings.3: They showed me someone's old passbook as an example: a deposit of 3 roubles 40 kopecks, opened in 1961. "He'll be back," they say.
city.talk.savings.4: The stamp thumped the paper so hard the inkwell jumped. "That's not for you, that's for order," the cashier explained.
city.talk.shoes.1: "What size? Forty-one? We've got forty-three, to grow into. Wool socks and they'll fit like a glove."
city.talk.shoes.2: The saleswoman taps a sole. "Our shoes last for ages. You can't wear them out, only outgrow them."
city.talk.shoes.3: On the shelf, lonely galoshes lined in red. "Nobody buys them," they say, "because everyone's waiting for rain, and it doesn't come."
city.talk.shoes.4: They set out a stool and a shoehorn for me. I didn't buy anything, but I sat there like a real customer.
city.talk.sport_reception.1: "The pool needs a doctor's note, the gym a season ticket, table tennis a good mood. Which of those have you got?"
city.talk.sport_reception.2: Trophies above the desk, and under them a box: "Lost swimming caps". There are more caps than trophies.
city.talk.sport_reception.3: The cashier hands over a locker key on an elastic band. "Number seven, a lucky one. Don't mix it up with eight, that's the coach's."
city.talk.sport_reception.4: The club timetable: gymnastics, swimming, "Health after sixty" and "Health before sixteen". The second one's mine.
city.talk.tickets.1: "Tickets are thirty roubles, pay in the hall. Sit anywhere, it's not busy."
city.talk.tickets.2: "Today it's The Man Who Waited for the Lighthouse. They say everyone cries at the end, even the projectionist."
city.talk.tickets.3: The cashier checks the poster against the wall clock, though the clock has stopped.
city.talk.tickets.4: "Under sixteens aren't allowed at the late show. How old are you? Never mind, don't answer."

city.weather.cloakroom.1: "Wet raincoat on the end hook, over the radiator. It'll be dry by the end of the show."
city.weather.cloakroom.2: "Shake the snow off your collar onto the mat, not onto me. Felt boots can stay under the rack."
city.weather.counter.1: "Put your umbrella in the corner, please, I've got a whole sea on the floor already."
city.xpl.diary.fri: Theme of the day: our town. Find the house you live in on the old map by the book wall. If you cannot, the house is newer than the map. That earns a stamp too.
city.xpl.diary.full: A new slip is pinned to the stand: "Diary completely filled? Then drop in on the librarian. She knows what to do with readers like you."
city.xpl.diary.half: At the bottom of the sheet, in pencil: "Eight stamps already. That is not a grade, it is a route."
city.xpl.diary.mon: Reading diary. Today is Monday and the pages are clean: it is the books' day off. Not laziness, just the order of things.
city.xpl.diary.sat: Theme of the day: anything at all. On Saturdays you may hop from shelf to shelf. At 11 a story is read in the children's corner.
city.xpl.diary.sun: Theme of the day: the sun. At 11 the Sunday story, and tea afterwards. Diaries are accepted for a stamp right up to closing time.
city.xpl.diary.thu: Theme of the day: poems. Reading aloud is allowed in a half-voice. Loud reading earns no stamp, but a good face does.
city.xpl.diary.tue: Theme of the day: the sea. Read a page on the Sea shelf, then get your stamp at the lending desk. On Tuesdays the kettle in the staff room is put on for two.
city.xpl.diary.wed: Theme of the day: birds. Find out from the field guide how a great tit differs from a blue tit, then go outside and check. A stamp for an honest check.
city.xpl.leave.1: I wrote one line on the postcard: "We are waiting here. The kettle is on on Tuesdays." I slipped it between the ticket and the clock without numbers. From the pile by the shelf I took another one to keep: they always leave a few here.
city.xpl.leave.2: I did not sign it: he will know who it is from. I laid the postcard with the other bookmarks and held my palm on it as on a warm mug. From the pile I took a clean one to keep.
city.xpl.leave.prompt: E — slip a postcard into the guide
city.xpl.ledger.1: The 1968 loan ledger, in a blue folder. Entry of 14 May: "Guide to Sundials, lent until 28 May. Reader: G. N." The due date is crossed out and written again, many times, in different inks.
city.xpl.ledger.2: At the bottom of the page, fresh ink: "Returned." Today's date. Below, a second hand: "Received. Do not worry. The kettle is hot."
city.xpl.ledger.3: A second entry in another hand: "Came on Tuesday. Did not come behind the desk, drank his tea standing by the window. Left before I turned round. Left a daisy."
city.xpl.ledger.4: A sheet is pinned to the ledger: "A messenger is needed. Somebody young, whom he will not be afraid of. Let them slip a postcard into the book, the rest is my business."
city.xpl.ledger.5: The ledger is closed, with a fresh line on the cover: "Reader: G. N. Status: comes on Tuesdays." Beside it, on a saucer, an empty cup and a daisy.
city.xpl.notice.1: The reading room is open from 10 to 8, except on Mondays. On Mondays the library rests: shelves need to breathe out now and then.
city.xpl.notice.10: Over the New Year days a tree made of books stands in the reading room. The top ones may be taken down only by two people, and only to be read.
city.xpl.notice.2: Please do not stack more than five books on the tables. A falling tower is not reading, it is gym class.
city.xpl.notice.3: Lost a scarf, a mitten or a thought? Scarves and mittens are in the box at the lending desk. Thoughts are harder, but we try.
city.xpl.notice.4: To the reader from 1968. Your loan card has turned up: no. 3-217, lovely handwriting, the surname blurred by time. The fine for all these years: zero roubles, zero kopecks. We counted twice.
city.xpl.notice.5: A small lamp has appeared by the Returned shelf. We did not put it there. Please leave it on: somebody finds it easier to read that way.
city.xpl.notice.6: A second bookmark was found in the Sundial Guide: a drawn clock without numbers, only a shadow. Signed: "If it is cloudy I will come all the same." A spare lamp for cloudy days has been bought.
city.xpl.notice.7: To our young readers: one quiet story needs a messenger. Postcards are at the lending desk, four roubles. Slip one into the Guide on the shelf by the window. We expect a reply on Tuesdays, at tea time.
city.xpl.notice.8: On Tuesday both cups were empty. That is a good sign: it means they were drunk. The book has been lent to the reader again, due date: "when he has finished". Thank you, all messengers.
city.xpl.notice.9: There is a festival in town today. The lending desk closes at six: the librarian wants to go to the square too, and we are letting him.
city.xpl.piano.1: I lifted the lid two fingers' width and play as if the keys were cotton wool. From the next capsule somebody tapped the wall softly: once, approvingly.
city.xpl.piano.2: I play very softly, a lesson in whispering. The capsule answers with all its concrete and, oddly enough, it sounds beautiful.
city.xpl.piano.3: Evening, few readers. I played everything I remember. From the hall below somebody applauds: pages rustle, one by one, like small palms.
city.xpl.pressA.fri: Friday: the weekend listings. An old film at Rassvet, a chess evening at the Cog club, a story for the smallest at the library. A note below: "Come with your parents, parents listen too."
city.xpl.pressA.mon: The bound run of the Town Herald for last week. There is no fresh issue: on Mondays the print shop rests together with the library.
city.xpl.pressA.sat: Saturday, the thick issue: a half-page crossword. Somebody has pencilled in "lighthouse" where "sea" was wanted, and it turns out both fit.
city.xpl.pressA.sun: The Sunday supplement, readers' letters. One begins: "I should like to find the person who borrowed a library book in May 1968 and took it away for a long while." Signed: "The Library."
city.xpl.pressA.thu: Thursday: an interview with the lighthouse keeper. Asked whether he gets bored, he answered: "I have people to talk to: thirty-three lamps, and all different."
city.xpl.pressA.tue: The Town Herald, Tuesday. On the front page the cable car, which has a new cabin again. Below in small print: the tide table and a yellow umbrella lost near the department store. A reward is promised to the finder.
city.xpl.pressA.wed: Wednesday: a report from the fishermen's pier on how to wean a gull off stealing from the tray. The editors' conclusion: you cannot. The recipe for pasties on page three is given without gulls.
city.xpl.pressB.fs: A chess magazine: a game played by post between two towns over four years. The last move was sent on a postcard. No winner is named: both insist they lost.
city.xpl.pressB.mt: The magazine Sky Above Us: a table of sunrises and sunsets for the week. One sunset is circled, with a note beside it: "The best one is the one you can see from the reading room."
city.xpl.pressB.su: A children's magazine: how to make an hourglass from two glasses and one patient week. Beside it, in somebody's pencil, a clock without numbers, only a shadow.
city.xpl.pressB.wt: Sky Above Us, an article on sundials: the shadow is shortest at noon, then stretches until it becomes night. The author calls it the most honest way to count time.
city.xpl.returned.1: The Returned shelf: books with no loan slips and no readers, but with neat bookmarks. All the spines face the window as if waiting for weather.
city.xpl.returned.2: On top lies the Sundial Guide, lent on 14 May 1968. The cover is worn soft. On the first page in pencil: "I read slowly. Forgive me."
city.xpl.returned.3: Between the pages is a cable-car ticket to the Lighthouse station. The date has rubbed off, but the stamp is the kind only people who treasure tickets have.
city.xpl.returned.4: A new bookmark: a clock without numbers, only the shadow of a gnomon. Signed: "If it is cloudy I will come all the same." I looked out of the window. The sky is just like that.
city.xpl.returned.5: On the shelf a card in the librarian's hand: "If you are reading this and have a postcard, slip it into the Guide. I will pass it on. Do not ask to whom: he will come himself."
city.xpl.returned.6: There are now three bookmarks in the Guide: the ticket, the clock without numbers and a daisy. The daisy is dry but does not crumble: it was carried carefully in a pocket.
city.xpl.returned.prompt: E — look at the Returned shelf
city.xpl.returned.rain: Rain. The lamp by the Returned shelf burns brighter than usual, and I see it is not here by chance: cloudy days are his days.
city.xpl.returns.1: The returns box. Its slot is exactly the thickness of a book: no thinner, no thicker. Inside it is muffled and warm, like a mailbox in winter.
city.xpl.returns.2: A card is stuck on the lid: "Books may be returned at any hour. We will not ask why it took so long."
city.xpl.returns.3: Under the slot there is a faint pencil mark on the metal: somebody checked whether a book would reach the bottom. It did.
city.xpl.returns.4: A corner of an envelope sticks out of the slot. Address: "The library, to the shelf by the window." I did not pull it out: it is not mine. But I can almost see the bookmark inside: a clock without numbers.
city.xpl.returns.5: The box is empty. That is news too: for the first time in many days nothing was returned and nothing was taken. The librarian says that happens when everything is in its place.
city.xpl.returns.prompt: E — look into the returns box
city.xpl.stamp.1: The librarian takes an ink pad from a drawer, breathes on the stamp and presses a round mark into my diary: a lamp with a green shade. "For quiet hours," she says.
city.xpl.stamp.2: At weekends the stamp is different: an open book with wings. "For reading with no use at all," the librarian explains. "The most valuable kind."
city.xpl.stamp.3: Four stamps in the diary. The librarian leafs through it and nods: "You can tell you are not reading for a grade."
city.xpl.stamp.4: Eight stamps, and the diary has swollen. She holds the cover down with a finger: "One day people will read it instead of you. Do not take offence, it is a compliment."
city.xpl.stamp.5: Twelve. The librarian takes out a red pencil and underlines my name on the cover: "This is not a mark, it is a bookmark."
city.xpl.stamp.6: The diary is full: a mark for every shelf, even the Returned. The librarian is silent for a long moment, then presses the last, big stamp: a clock without numbers. "I put that one in one reader's card. Long ago." Now you may come on a Tuesday for tea.
city.xpl.stamp.prompt: E — ask for a diary stamp
city.xpl.story.1: The librarian settles into the armchair by the round rug, and the little ones swoop down on the bean bags like sparrows on crumbs. Today's story is about a Little Lighthouse that was afraid of the dark. Every evening it lit its lamp so the ships would not be frightened, and the ships sailed off without saying thank you. But one day a small boat came back and blinked in reply. Since then the Lighthouse has not been afraid of the dark: it knows someone is sailing toward it in there.
city.xpl.story.2: A story about the Torn Page, which told everyone it came from the most important book. The page was picked up from the floor, smoothed out and held against another book. It fitted as if it belonged. It turns out that the right page sometimes simply gets lost on the way. The little ones argued for a long time about which book it came from. They agreed: a future one.
city.xpl.story.3: Today the story is about a Cat who lived in the reading room and followed those who had dropped a bookmark. He brought the bookmarks back in his teeth, carefully, by the corner. The readers thought that was how things were done. The Cat did not object. The children swore never to lose a bookmark again, just in case, so as not to teach the cat to work.
city.xpl.story.4: A Sunday story about the Kettle that boiled for two on Tuesdays. Once the one it boiled for was half an hour late, and the Kettle kept boiling all that time so the tea would not cool at once. The children listened very quietly. Then they asked whether the latecomer arrived. The librarian smiled: "You will tell me that when you grow up."
city.xpl.story.title: Story hour
city.xpl.tea.1: On Tuesdays the kettle is put on for two. The librarian nods at the second cup: "Have it. If he comes, I will pour again." The tea is strong and smells of thyme.
city.xpl.tea.2: The second cup is already warm: somebody was here before me. The librarian does not raise her head: "He asked me to say he got the postcard. And that our tea is too strong." I drink and stay quiet so as not to scare anyone off.
city.xpl.tea.prompt: E — take a cup of tea

quest.cafe_guest.desc: Leafing through the guest book by the stairs in the Saucer, I realised the pages are running out and my entry is not there.
quest.cafe_guest.done: Done. The barista, passing, glanced over my shoulder and nodded: "Now you're one of ours."
quest.cafe_guest.sign.log: The pen is right there. If I have no thoughts, I can draw a saucer.
quest.cafe_guest.sign.obj: Write an entry in the guest book
quest.cafe_guest.title: A page in the guest book
quest.cafe_kesha.desc: A sheet under the menu says Kesha the parrot has come back on his own. He likes sunflower seeds and the word "Terminus". Worth checking.
quest.cafe_kesha.done: A pastry on the house. Kesha announced the last stop aloud, and then I thought he added "See you soon".
quest.cafe_kesha.feed.log: Kesha is watching me with one eye. The saucer says: first "Terminus", then the seeds.
quest.cafe_kesha.perch.log: Seeds in my pocket. I'll go to the perch at the end of the bar in the Saucer and take a look at Kesha.
quest.cafe_kesha.perch.obj: Talk to Kesha on his perch by the bar
quest.cafe_kesha.seeds.log: I need sunflower seeds. They say you can buy them at the market.
quest.cafe_kesha.title: Terminus
quest.checkup.desc: At the clinic they looked at me as if I'd been due for a check-up for ages. Well, if they've been waiting.
quest.checkup.doctor.log: Only the doctor left. He sees patients on weekdays until five.
quest.checkup.done: "Practically healthy," they wrote on my card. The nurse gave me a boiled sweet as if I were little. I didn't refuse.
quest.checkup.nurse.log: The nurse told me to step on the scales and read the eye chart. Then the doctor.
quest.checkup.title: Practically healthy
quest.chess_ladder.desc: In the club a ladder of names is chalked on a board. The bottom line is empty, and for some reason I feel awkward walking past it.
quest.chess_ladder.done: I wrote my name on the empty line. In chalk, small, so it can be rubbed out. Lev Markovich read it and nodded: that is how everybody starts.
quest.chess_ladder.look.log: I'll look at the ladder: who stands on which rung.
quest.chess_ladder.look.obj: Look at the chess ladder at the Rassvet
quest.chess_ladder.play.log: Now I can sit down at a board. If I lose they will pour me tea; that's the custom here.
quest.chess_ladder.play.obj: Play a game of chess at the Rassvet
quest.chess_ladder.read.log: Before sitting down at a board I'll check the shelf: there should be a book of openings.
quest.chess_ladder.title: A rung of the ladder
quest.cinema_night.desc: They're showing a film at the Rassvet. The poster promises everyone cries at the end, even the projectionist.
quest.cinema_night.done: I came out of the cinema and the light outside had changed. For five minutes the town seemed like the film carrying on.
quest.cinema_night.film.log: A ticket is thirty roubles; the show runs while the projectionist is in, from three till late. I'll sit wherever I like.
quest.cinema_night.title: The evening show
quest.cinema_night.watch.obj: Watch a film at the Rassvet
quest.city_tour.desc: The town is big and I don't know anyone in it. I'll start by just walking through the main doors.
quest.city_tour.done: I've been round the whole centre. Every door greeted me as if I'd been there before.
quest.city_tour.see_cafe.obj: Go up to the Saucer café
quest.city_tour.see_club.obj: Look into the Rassvet culture house
quest.city_tour.title: The town by the sea
quest.city_tour.walk.log: The library, the department store, the market, the Rassvet, the clinic, the Saucer café. If I do something in each one, sit down, leaf through a book, buy something, maybe the town will remember me.
quest.cog_clock.desc: The Cog club's chess clock has gone missing. Everyone seems to know it's gone and nobody knows where.
quest.cog_clock.done: The buffet lady brought tea and a biscuit "for the return". She said the clock came back the most proper way: by itself. I didn't argue.
quest.cog_clock.find.log: Something ticks upstairs. Grasshoppers don't live indoors, but circles do.
quest.cog_clock.look.log: I'll start with the notices: the club's boards usually say more than whoever wrote them meant to.
quest.cog_clock.notices.obj: Read the notices on the club's boards
quest.cog_clock.place.obj: Put the clock back on the chess table
quest.cog_clock.set.log: Seryozha asked me to take the clock back so he wouldn't have to explain. I'll put it in its place and nobody will have to explain anything.
quest.cog_clock.title: The cracked clock
quest.cog_reader.cart.log: Last, a look at the returns trolley: you can see who read what, which is almost like meeting them.
quest.cog_reader.desc: The club library doesn't lend books to just anyone, but the magazines go round freely. I'll start at the shelves.
quest.cog_reader.done: Tamara Ilyinichna stamped "Cog Club. Library" on a postcard and said I was a reader now. The stamp came out crooked, but it's real.
quest.cog_reader.look.obj: See what has been returned to the trolley
quest.cog_reader.read.log: Chess, engineering, the sea. In the margins of every book someone has already argued with the author.
quest.cog_reader.swap.log: By the end wall there is a swap rack: bring one, take one. I have nothing yet, but they let you take a magazine anyway.
quest.cog_reader.take.obj: Take a magazine from the swap rack
quest.cog_reader.title: A reader at the club
quest.first_chess.desc: At the Cog club there are people at the chess tables who never seem to get up.
quest.first_chess.done: After the game the buffet lady brought me tea "for bravery". She said losers always get a glass here.
quest.first_chess.game.log: I'll sit at a free board. Someone is bound to join me; that's the custom here.
quest.first_chess.play.obj: Play a game of chess at the Cog club
quest.first_chess.title: First game
quest.home_aoki.desc: The seamstress Rimma Aoki lives at the top of the second stepped house. The door is open; a clock ticks and fabric rustles in the draught.
quest.home_aoki.done: At the Rassvet the cashier heard me out and wrote in her book: "Sun: will be there." She gave me twenty-five roubles "for the tram". There are no trams in Lyudmilovsk. "Well, for the cable car, then," said the cashier.
quest.home_aoki.dress.log: Something almost finished under the machine's needle. I'll see what.
quest.home_aoki.dress.obj: Look at the sewing under the needle
quest.home_aoki.fitting.log: By her calendar, the costume fitting for the Rassvet is on Thursday, and the Sun for the play isn't ready. I'll look in at the Rassvet and tell them the Sun is being sewn and will be there.
quest.home_aoki.fitting.obj: Tell the cashier at the Rassvet's ticket window
quest.home_aoki.swatches.log: One sun on the hem isn't finished: she couldn't find the right yellow. There are swatches on the wall. Maybe I can find it.
quest.home_aoki.swatches.obj: Pick out a yellow among the swatches on the wall
quest.home_aoki.title: A sun for the hem
quest.home_girma.calendar.log: On Friday Mum comes home. I'll mark it too, just a little, on the family calendar.
quest.home_girma.calendar.obj: Mark Friday on the family calendar
quest.home_girma.charts.log: Daisuke has a whole shelf of star charts. One of them, they say, has the sun drawn on it, at night. I'll find which.
quest.home_girma.charts.obj: Find the star chart with the sun drawn on it
quest.home_girma.desc: The Girmas live at the top of the stepped house: Daisuke, the dad, sells at the market; Nino, the mum, works away; and eight-year-old Tomohiko draws. The terrace door is open.
quest.home_girma.done: On the stairs I met a boy with a satchel. "Did you look with the filter?" "With the filter." "Good, then," said Tomo, and gave me thirty roubles from his money box "for keeping an eye on Papa's telescope". I tried to refuse. "Mama told me to keep watch, and I was at school. So you were working."
quest.home_girma.scope.log: Tomo drew the sun on the night chart. His dad draws the real one every day, through a filter. I'll look through the telescope too. Filter on.
quest.home_girma.scope.obj: Look at the sun through the filtered telescope
quest.home_girma.title: A sun on the night chart
quest.home_holm.desc: The door of a ground-floor flat is wide open. A plate on it: "V. S. Holm, Ocean Navigator." Nobody home, only a clock ticking.
quest.home_holm.done: Without looking up from her knitting, the concierge handed me forty roubles. "Viktor Sergeyevich said: whoever writes the forecast in for him gets ice-cream money. He tells everyone that. You're the first who did."
quest.home_holm.log.obj: Find the watch log on the shelf of pilot books
quest.home_holm.radio.log: His receiver is broken and there's been no forecast in the log for three days. There's a house radio down in the hall. I'll listen for him.
quest.home_holm.radio.obj: Hear the forecast on the radio in the hall
quest.home_holm.read.log: Among his pilot books there's a watch log. Someone else's, of course. I'll just take a look.
quest.home_holm.title: Shore watch
quest.home_holm.write.log: The log lies on the kitchen table, open at today's date. I'll write the forecast in. In my own hand, but neatly.
quest.home_holm.write.obj: Write the forecast in the log in the kitchen
quest.home_kravets.answer.log: Found the time. I'll write it into a corner of the chart on her wall, small, in pencil, so she can rub it out if she wants to solve it herself.
quest.home_kravets.answer.obj: Write the time on the chart on Nora's wall
quest.home_kravets.desc: A student lives by the entrance of the second capsule tower. The door's open, with a note: "Nora Kravets is at the library. Quiet: thinking in progress."
quest.home_kravets.done: Down at the desk there's a box labelled "For whoever helps Nora with physics". The whole building has been dropping coins in since the start of term. They gave me twenty roubles and told me not to tell anyone. I'm not telling. Just writing.
quest.home_kravets.problem.log: Exercise books on the desk. I'll have a look: maybe I'll understand what the thinking's about.
quest.home_kravets.problem.obj: Look at the exercise books on Nora's desk
quest.home_kravets.tides.log: The problem's about tomorrow's high water at the pier. The lighthouse keepers' log is sure to have the tides. I'll go to the lighthouse.
quest.home_kravets.tides.obj: Find the tide table in the lighthouse keepers' log
quest.home_kravets.title: High water
quest.home_okada.canvas.log: I'll see what's on his easel today. Only look.
quest.home_okada.canvas.obj: Look at the canvas on the easel
quest.home_okada.desc: A door on the curved slab's gallery stands ajar; it smells of turpentine. The caretaker downstairs told me: "That's Lev Markovich Okada. He's been painting the same window a thousand times."
quest.home_okada.done: Downstairs, Asanov the caretaker poured me a glass of tea in a holder. "Been up to Markovich's? He asked me: whoever comes and really looks at the paintings, pour them one." I didn't ask how he knew it was really.
quest.home_okada.letter.log: A letter lies on the dining table. You don't read other people's letters. But sitting down next to it is probably allowed.
quest.home_okada.letter.obj: Sit down at the table with the letter
quest.home_okada.title: A thousand and one windows
quest.home_okada.wall.log: Today's canvas was begun and dropped mid-word. Maybe the big picture over the sofa will explain why a thousand identical windows.
quest.home_okada.wall.obj: Study the big picture over the sofa
quest.home_okafor.cafe.log: The tune breaks off at three minutes. Someone has added a fresh note on the reel: the Saucer café, the jukebox, third button. I'll check.
quest.home_okafor.cafe.obj: Play the jukebox at the Saucer café
quest.home_okafor.desc: In the capsule house on the slope, one pair of capsules has been turned into a radio amateur's den. A plate: "Gunnar Okafor. Lyudmilovsk-11." The door's open and something inside is hissing softly.
quest.home_okafor.done: The neighbour from the capsule opposite looked out at the rustling. "You found him that tune? He's been looking for half a year!" And she pressed thirty roubles on me "from the whole building". I didn't cross out "unknown" on the reel: let it be both.
quest.home_okafor.record.log: That's the one, right to the end, no static! Now to find the record on Gunnar's shelf and write the title on the reel.
quest.home_okafor.record.obj: Find the record on the music shelf
quest.home_okafor.tape.log: There's a reel on the tape recorder. I'll switch it on, just to listen.
quest.home_okafor.tape.obj: Listen to the reel on Gunnar's tape recorder
quest.home_okafor.title: The third button
quest.home_okonkwo.barber.log: Emiliano's mum, Yasmin, works as a barber on the promenade, in the barber's nearer the fair square. I'll tell her the whale's in one piece and waiting for Saturday.
quest.home_okonkwo.barber.obj: Sit in the waiting chair at the promenade barber's where Yasmin works
quest.home_okonkwo.desc: In the second house of two drums there's Mads Okonkwo's pottery studio. It smells of wet clay. Nobody inside, only the wheel under a cloth.
quest.home_okonkwo.done: Yasmin laughed without letting go of her scissors. "In one piece? Thank goodness. I water it every morning like a plant." She gave me thirty roubles "for delivering the news" and asked me not to tell Emiliano the whale will have two tails. It's a surprise.
quest.home_okonkwo.drawings.log: The whale is waiting for Papa. The board of drawings should show when he's coming back.
quest.home_okonkwo.drawings.obj: Study the board with the calendar and drawings
quest.home_okonkwo.title: The whale on the wheel
quest.home_okonkwo.wheel.log: Something modelled under the cloth. I'll look without touching anything.
quest.home_okonkwo.wheel.obj: See what's on the potter's wheel
quest.home_santos.board.log: A notice board in the kitchen. Family business, of course, but isn't a board there to be looked at?
quest.home_santos.board.obj: Read the board in the kitchen
quest.home_santos.desc: The blue house in the folded row. The door's open; five pairs of shoes in the hall, from enormous to tiny. Nobody home: all out for a walk, it seems.
quest.home_santos.done: In a little dish on the table: sweets and a slip: "For guests. One each, please." I took one. Let the dishes go to whoever never found Venus. Which is probably Dad.
quest.home_santos.note.log: Found her! I'll leave a hint in Lina's exercise book on the children's desk. I won't be doing their dishes anyway, and it'll help her.
quest.home_santos.note.obj: Leave a hint in the exercise book on the children's desk
quest.home_santos.title: Queen of the evening
quest.home_santos.venus.log: A contest: first to see Venus gets a week off the dishes. The telescope is in the loft. Venus is the evening star: look west after sunset.
quest.home_santos.venus.obj: Find Venus with the telescope in the loft
quest.home_singh.answer.log: Gunnar lives a kilometre away, in the capsule house on the slope, and they've never met. If his door's open too, I'll answer from his own set.
quest.home_singh.answer.obj: Go on air from Gunnar's set in the capsule house
quest.home_singh.desc: The caretaker's den in the capsule tower is open, and inside the valves of a radio set are glowing. On the door: "Ilmar Singh, caretaker. On my rounds."
quest.home_singh.done: Ilmar answered himself: back from his rounds. When he heard I was sitting at Gunnar's, he was quiet for a long time, then said: "Tell him, if you see him: Saturday, the Saucer. No static." There was a stack of QSL cards under the transmitter. I took one to remember it by.
quest.home_singh.listen.log: A note on the desk: if he's on his rounds, listen on the air for him. That seems to mean me too.
quest.home_singh.listen.obj: Listen to the air on Ilmar's set
quest.home_singh.map.log: Someone called Gunnar is calling him, call sign Lyudmilovsk-11. There seems to be more about him on the wall over the desk.
quest.home_singh.map.obj: Study the map and the cards on the wall
quest.home_singh.title: A kilometre of air
quest.home_tadesse.desc: In the house of two joined drums there's a studio behind the partition. On the door: "V. Tadesse. No need to ring, come in. Don't feed the fish."
quest.home_tadesse.done: A grey-haired man came down from upstairs: the man in the portrait, half a century on. "Hamish," he said. "Here for Valya? She's on the promenade, painting water." He gave me a postcard with one of her fish. "She paints fish by the hundred. But not the sun. Not yet."
quest.home_tadesse.fish.log: Fifty-four names on the aquarium glass. I'll count how many fish there really are.
quest.home_tadesse.fish.obj: Look at the fish in the aquarium
quest.home_tadesse.paintings.log: Fish on the walls, pines, and a young man with a fishing rod. I'll look at three of the paintings in turn.
quest.home_tadesse.pines.obj: Look at the pines on the cliff
quest.home_tadesse.portrait.obj: Look at the portrait with the fishing rod
quest.home_tadesse.title: Fish and the sun
quest.library_1968.cup.obj: Have tea with the librarian on a Tuesday
quest.library_1968.desc: On the shelf by the east window lies a book that came back after more than half a century. The librarian says the reader will return if nobody gets in his way. Or if someone helps him a little.
quest.library_1968.done: On Tuesday the second cup was empty before I finished mine. A daisy lay on the saucer, and in the Guide my postcard stood with its writing up: "Thank you. I will come."
quest.library_1968.find.log: I'll look at the Returned shelf by the east window and at the ledger in the staff room. The door has no lock, but the Staff sign asks for quiet.
quest.library_1968.leave.log: I need a postcard: they cost four roubles at the lending desk and turn up elsewhere in town. I'll slip it into the Guide, and he will do the rest.
quest.library_1968.leave.obj: Slip the postcard into the Guide
quest.library_1968.ledger.obj: Read the ledger in the librarian's room
quest.library_1968.tea.log: The librarian said the reply will come on Tuesday, at tea time. So I wait for Tuesday.
quest.library_1968.title: The reader from 1968
quest.library_day.desc: The capsule library is quiet and smells of paper. You can sit there till closing and nobody will chase you out.
quest.library_day.done: My head is full of other people's pages. On my way out the librarian gave me a postcard: "So you have somewhere to write a thought down."
quest.library_day.read.log: I'll browse three shelves: birds, our town and the sun. There seem to be more books here about the sun than anything.
quest.library_day.title: A day at the library
quest.library_diary.ask.obj: Get a stamp from the librarian
quest.library_diary.desc: By the library door hangs a stand: every shelf has its own stamp, and the stamps are gathered in a diary. The librarian gives them to those who read for no grade.
quest.library_diary.done: There are four new stamps in the diary and a fifth, invisible one: the kind you get for a story when you are no longer five.
quest.library_diary.hour.obj: Listen to the story in the children's corner
quest.library_diary.shelves.log: To begin with, three shelves: poems, the sea and art. Leafing through is enough, the stamps go on by themselves.
quest.library_diary.stamp.log: Now to the lending desk: let the librarian look at the diary and put in her own stamp.
quest.library_diary.story.log: On weekends at 11 a story is read in the children's corner. I'll sit on a bean bag and listen; nobody will say I'm too big.
quest.library_diary.title: The reading diary
quest.mineral_water.desc: The Druzhba sanatorium has a pump room. The guests go there on schedule, like going on a date.
quest.mineral_water.done: A taste of iron and of something warm. I drank it, and for a minute the sun seemed to shine from inside rather than out.
quest.mineral_water.drink.log: Now to drink it. Slowly, thinking of good things, as the sign says.
quest.mineral_water.fill.log: I'll fill a bottle at the tap by the entrance. They say the water comes out warm by itself, no heating at all.
quest.mineral_water.pump.obj: Fill a bottle of mineral water at the sanatorium
quest.mineral_water.title: Healing water
quest.photo_strip.booth.obj: Have my photo taken at the promenade studio
quest.photo_strip.desc: There isn't a single photo in my diary. Not even of me.
quest.photo_strip.done: I put the prints in my diary. The boy in them looks at me closely, as if he wants to ask something.
quest.photo_strip.photo.log: There's a photo studio on the promenade. Twenty roubles and I'll have proof I was here.
quest.photo_strip.title: A photo to remember
quest.rassvet_reel.board.log: A sheet about the find is pinned to the foyer board. I'll read what it says.
quest.rassvet_reel.board.obj: Read the notice on the foyer board
quest.rassvet_reel.desc: At the Rassvet they have found a tin of film. The lid has the same word as the front of the building. The whole house is wondering what is on it.
quest.rassvet_reel.done: Nobody took the white light at the end for the end. We went out in silence, and the clerk slipped me a postcard: "In memory of what was never finished."
quest.rassvet_reel.piano.log: The sheet of the waltz from the old poster lies by the piano. I'll play at least a few bars.
quest.rassvet_reel.piano.obj: Play the piano in the foyer
quest.rassvet_reel.radio.log: The radio amateurs asked about this film on the air. I'll listen and see whether anyone has answered.
quest.rassvet_reel.screening.log: The screening is in the front row, one show only. A ticket is thirty roubles; the projectionist is in from three o'clock.
quest.rassvet_reel.screening.obj: Watch Rassvet from the front row
quest.rassvet_reel.title: The tin from the storeroom
quest.school_lesson.board.log: The teacher said: "New boy, to the board!" Well then. To the board.
quest.school_lesson.desc: You can hear School No. 1's bell from the street. I wonder if anyone would notice if I quietly sat at the back.
quest.school_lesson.desk.obj: Sit through a lesson at the school
quest.school_lesson.done: Got a B for an answer I don't remember giving. The teacher said: "Come again, there'll always be a place for you here."
quest.school_lesson.lesson.log: Lessons run on weekdays from eight till three. I'll find a classroom and a free desk.
quest.school_lesson.title: The lesson
quest.store_errand.buy.log: The grocery counter on the ground floor has kefir and bread. I'll buy them while I'm here.
quest.store_errand.deliver.log: Now to the Stepped House, flat 4. I'll leave the bag at the door and sit on the bench outside for a bit, in case she looks out.
quest.store_errand.desc: A note on the department store door: "Anyone going to the Stepped House: please bring kefir and a loaf to flat 4. Money under the mat. Thank you!"
quest.store_errand.done: While I sat on the bench the bag by the door vanished. Under the mat: the money and a note: "You're a good person. Come round for tea." No signature.
quest.store_errand.stepped_house.obj: Take the shopping to the Stepped House and sit outside
quest.store_errand.title: A note on the door
quest.store_fitting.booth.obj: Listen to a record in the booth
quest.store_fitting.cubicle.obj: Try something on in the fitting room
quest.store_fitting.desc: In the department store you don't have to buy anything, but you can't help noticing it. A window, a fitting room, records: I'll try to be a proper customer and spend nothing.
quest.store_fitting.done: I left the store with empty hands and a full head: a waltz in one ear, and a "well, how is it?" from behind a curtain in the other. The assistants seem to have smiled after me.
quest.store_fitting.fit.log: Upstairs in the clothes department there's a fitting room with a curtain. I'll try something on, anything.
quest.store_fitting.listen.log: In the records department there's a listening booth. I can't buy a record, but nobody forbids listening.
quest.store_fitting.title: Being a Customer
quest.store_fitting.window.log: I'll start with the window: in the morning someone usually works there, and by day it's simply pretty.
quest.store_umbrella.announce.obj: Announce over the loudspeaker that the umbrella has been found
quest.store_umbrella.cloak.log: First I'll look into the stand by the cloakroom: umbrellas like to turn up there on their own.
quest.store_umbrella.desc: The lost and found has announced the yellow umbrella again; this time it was found in the toy department. The umbrella seems to wander the store by itself. I should find out where it is today and tell its owner.
quest.store_umbrella.done: For a second everybody in the hall froze, then somebody clapped. A minute later a woman in a checked scarf came to the bureau, took the umbrella and said "thank you" in a voice she'd clearly rehearsed a hundred times. The duck on the handle winked at me. Or I imagined it.
quest.store_umbrella.lost.log: It isn't here, or isn't any more. I'll ask at the lost and found: they have their own stand and their own tag.
quest.store_umbrella.mic.log: The owner, they say, loves to hear her name over the radio. The bureau has allowed me to tell her myself, through the microphone, that the umbrella has been found.
quest.store_umbrella.shelf.obj: Look at the umbrellas at the lost and found
quest.store_umbrella.stand.obj: Look into the umbrella stand by the cloakroom
quest.store_umbrella.title: The Yellow Umbrella with the Duck
quest.t3_bowl.desc: There's a pottery studio in the brick hall. The potter promised: in a week a lump of clay becomes a bowl. A week is a lot, but I'm in no hurry.
quest.t3_bowl.done: Green as the sea on a grey day, with two blue specks and one side a little higher than the other. The potter said: "It's alive." I'll pour tea into it.
quest.t3_bowl.fire.log: The bowl went off to dry, then into the kiln. I'll look in at the kiln and see how it's getting on.
quest.t3_bowl.glaze.log: After the first firing the bowl is pink as a piglet. Time to colour it: green, blue, and the "do not touch" one stays untouched.
quest.t3_bowl.glaze.obj: Glaze the bowl at the bench
quest.t3_bowl.take.log: The second firing is done. All that's left is to find my bowl on the shelf among the others.
quest.t3_bowl.take.obj: Look over the shelf of finished ware
quest.t3_bowl.throw.log: I'll start at the wheel: centre, pull up the walls, not press but persuade.
quest.t3_bowl.title: Bowl No. 7
quest.t3_fifth.ask.log: To start with I'll just go up to the coach. Just talk, promise nothing.
quest.t3_fifth.desc: At the sports centre the "Surf Juniors" are one player short for the courtyard tournament. The coach is looking at me as if I'd do. That's dangerous.
quest.t3_fifth.done: We took second place. Locker No. 5 now has my name and a certificate is waiting for me at the till. The coach said: "One more time?" I think I said yes.
quest.t3_fifth.play.log: Taya said I shoot "almost scarily." All that's left is to step on the court and play for real.
quest.t3_fifth.title: Number five
quest.t3_fifth.train.log: The coach said: "Come at five." To warm up I'll shoot at the back-wall hoop while nobody's watching.
